# 1. About this manual {#ch-00-introduction}

## 1.1 What PTXprint is {#00-introduction--what-ptxprint-is}

PTXprint makes print-ready PDF files of Scripture. It takes the text from a Paratext project and
lays it out on pages: with columns, headings, chapter and verse numbers, footnotes,
cross-references, pictures, headers and footers. You can use the PDF for checking and
proofreading, or send it to a printer to make a book.

PTXprint uses a typesetting program called **XeTeX** to place every letter and line on the page.
You never need to use XeTeX yourself. You make all your choices in the PTXprint window, and
PTXprint tells XeTeX what to do.

PTXprint never changes your Paratext text. It reads the text, makes a temporary copy, and
typesets that copy. To correct the words of the text, use Paratext.

## 1.2 Who this manual is for {#00-introduction--who-this-manual-is-for}

This manual is for everyone who uses the PTXprint window: translators, typesetters, project
leaders and support staff. You do not need to know about typesetting or computers.

* Every instruction can be done in the PTXprint window. You never need to edit files by hand or
  type commands.
* Sections marked **advanced** explain how to type special codes in the few places where
  PTXprint gives you a text box for them (for example the front matter). You can skip them until
  you need them.
* Technical words are explained the first time they appear in a chapter, and listed in the
  [**Glossary of terms**](#ch-32-glossary) at the end.

## 1.3 How this manual is organised {#00-introduction--how-this-manual-is-organised}

The manual has four parts.

**Part 1: Start here**

* [**About this manual**](#ch-00-introduction) – this chapter.
* [**Getting started with PTXprint**](#ch-01-getting-started) – a first walk-through: from opening PTXprint to your first PDF.
* [**The main window, menu and view levels**](#ch-02-main-window) – the parts of the window, configurations, view
  levels, and how PTXprint saves your settings.

**Part 2: Find an answer**

* [**How do I...? (step-by-step tasks)**](#ch-30-howto) – short instructions for common jobs.
* [**Problems and solutions**](#ch-31-troubleshooting) – what to do when something goes wrong.

**Part 3: Reference, tab by tab**

One chapter for each tab of the PTXprint window, in the same order as the tabs. Then come chapters
about the PDF Preview window, importing settings and getting help.

* [**Basic tab**](#ch-03-basic) – choose the project, the configuration and the books to print.
* [**Layout tab**](#ch-04-layout) – page size, margins, columns, font size and line spacing.
* [**Fonts+Script tab**](#ch-05-fonts) – fonts, writing system, hyphenation and spacing.
* [**Body tab**](#ch-06-body) – what is printed from each book (introductions, headings, verse numbers…).
* [**Notes+Refs tab**](#ch-07-notes) – footnotes, cross-references and study notes.
* [**Header+Footer tab**](#ch-08-headfoot) – the running header and footer, and page numbers.
* [**Pictures tab**](#ch-09-pictures) – illustrations and maps.
* [**Diglot tab (two or more languages)**](#ch-10-diglot) – two or more texts side by side.
* [**Tabs+Borders tab**](#ch-11-tabsborders) – thumb tabs and decorative borders.
* [**Styles tab**](#ch-12-styles) – the look of each kind of text (each USFM marker).
* [**Advanced tab**](#ch-13-advanced) – settings for experienced users.
* [**View+Edit tab**](#ch-14-viewedit) – front matter, the adjustment list, and the files PTXprint makes.
* [**Peripherals tab (front and back matter)**](#ch-15-peripherals) – front matter, table of contents, colophon, maps and covers.
* [**Publications tab**](#ch-16-publications) – a list of publications that you can print together.
* [**Finishing tab**](#ch-17-finishing) – PDF type for the printer, crop marks, booklets and comparing PDFs.
* [**Printers tab**](#ch-18-printers) – price estimates and orders from print companies.
* [**PDF Preview window, layout analysis and page filling**](#ch-19-preview) – look at the PDF and fix the layout of pages.
* [**Importing settings**](#ch-20-import) – copy settings from a PDF, an archive or another configuration.
* [**Help tab and getting support**](#ch-21-help) – find your files, and ask for help.

**Part 4: Glossary**

* [**Glossary of terms**](#ch-32-glossary) – the meaning of the words used in this manual.

Most tab chapters have the same parts:

* **What this tab is for** – when you would use the tab.
* One section for each area of the tab, using the names you see on the screen.
* **Common tasks** – numbered steps for the things people do most often.
* **Common problems** – what you see, why it happens, and what to change.
* **Settings reference** – every setting on the tab (see below).

You don't have to look things up yourself: in PTXprint, press **F1** with the mouse over any setting
to open this manual at its entry, or **Ctrl+click** the name of a tab to open it at the chapter about
that tab.

## 1.4 How to read a settings-reference entry {#00-introduction--how-to-read-a-settings-reference-entry}

At the end of each tab chapter, the **Settings reference** lists every setting (check box, list,
number box, button and so on) in that part of PTXprint. The settings are grouped by tab or dialog,
then by area, for example *Layout › Page Setup*. Each heading is the setting's name on the
screen. If it has no name, the heading is the label beside it, or a short description.

Each entry has these parts:

* **First line** – the kind of control (for example Checkbox, Radio, Number, Drop-down, Button,
  Text box, Colour or Link). For a check box, **on** means it is ticked by default and **off**
  means it is not. Then the lowest view level that shows the setting: **Mini+** (all views),
  **Basic+**, **Regular+**, or **Full** (only the Full view).
* **Second line** (only when needed) – more facts, separated by dots:
  * **Values** – for a number: the lowest and highest number, and the default.
  * **Choices** – the items in a list.
  * **Also** – a longer, descriptive name for the setting.
  * **Beside** – the label next to the control on the screen.
  * **Needs** – the setting can only be used when that other setting is turned on.
  * **Greyed out by** – the setting cannot be used while that other setting is ticked.
  * **Hidden until** – the setting is not shown until that check box is ticked.
  * **Shown when** – the tab or area only appears when that check box is ticked.
* **Tooltip** – the help text PTXprint shows when you hold the mouse over the setting, shown as a
  quotation.
* **Explanation** – in plain words: what the setting does, when to use it, a sensible value, and
  what to watch out for.

If you cannot find a setting in the window, check its view level, then **Needs**,
**Hidden until** and **Shown when**.

## 1.5 A short note about view levels {#00-introduction--a-short-note-about-view-levels}

PTXprint has hundreds of settings, but most people need only a few. So PTXprint can hide the
settings you do not need. This is the [**view level**](#s-btn-menu-level). There are four: **Mini** (fewest settings),
**Basic**, **Regular** and **Full** (every setting).

To change the view level, click the **≡** button at the top-left of the window, point to
**View Level**, and choose a level.

A hidden setting still works. It keeps its value and still changes the PDF. So if the PDF does
not look as you expect, change to the **Full** view and check the settings again.

A note such as "(Regular and Full views)" tells you which view levels show a setting. For more,
see the chapter [**The main window, menu and view levels**](#ch-02-main-window).

# 2. Getting started with PTXprint {#ch-01-getting-started}

## 2.1 About this chapter {#01-getting-started--about-this-chapter}

This chapter is for people who use PTXprint for the first time. It takes you step by step from
opening PTXprint to your first PDF. Then it shows how to change a few common things, and how to
keep different sets of settings for different kinds of output.

You do not need to read the rest of the manual first. Each step tells you which chapter to read
for more.

In this chapter, "pt" means point. One point is about 0.35 mm. Font sizes and line spacing are
given in points.

## 2.2 Before you start {#01-getting-started--before-you-start}

Check these things before you open PTXprint:

1. **You have a Paratext project** on this computer. PTXprint prints its text. If you use
   Send/Receive in Paratext, do a Send/Receive first, so that you have the latest text.
2. **The text has no serious marker errors.** PTXprint uses the USFM markers in the text (for
   example `\p` for a paragraph or `\v` for a verse). Run the Basic Checks in Paratext. Marker
   errors can stop PTXprint or give strange results.
3. **The fonts are installed** on this computer **for all users**. If a font is installed only
   for one user, PTXprint may not find it.
4. **No project, but you want to practise?** PTXprint can install a sample English Bible (the
   Berean Standard Bible) for you. See ["Get a text to practise with"](#03-basic--get-a-text-to-practise-with) in the [**Basic tab**](#ch-03-basic) chapter.

## 2.3 Open PTXprint {#01-getting-started--open-ptxprint}

1. Start PTXprint like other programs on your computer, for example from the Windows Start menu.
2. The main PTXprint window opens. It has:
   * **tabs** across the top (**Basic**, **Layout**, **Fonts+Script** and others). Each tab holds
     one group of settings;
   * the **≡** button at the top-left, for the main menu;
   * a **bar at the bottom** with the **Save**, **Print (Make PDF)** and **Quit** buttons.

The first time PTXprint starts, it uses the **Regular** view level, which shows most tabs and
settings. If the window looks too full, click **≡**, point to [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level), and click
**Basic View** or **Mini View**. Hidden settings still work. See the chapter **The main window,
menu and view levels**.

If your projects are not in the **Project** list, PTXprint may be looking in the wrong folder. See
["Use projects from another Paratext folder"](#21-help--use-projects-from-another-paratext-folder) in the chapter [**Help tab and getting support**](#ch-21-help).

## 2.4 Choose the project and the configuration {#01-getting-started--choose-the-project-and-the-configuration}

Everything starts on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.

1. Click the **Basic** tab.
2. In the **Project** list, choose your Paratext project. PTXprint shows the full name of the
   project next to the list.
3. In the **Layout Configuration** area, look at the **Name** list. The first time, it shows
   **Default**.

A **configuration** is a named set of PTXprint settings for one project: page size, fonts,
pictures and so on. Every project has a configuration called **Default**. You can make more later
(see ["Keep different settings for different outputs"](#01-getting-started--keep-different-settings-for-different-outputs) below). For now, use **Default**.

## 2.5 Choose the books {#01-getting-started--choose-the-books}

On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, in the **What to Print** area:

1. Click [**Single Book**](#s-r-book-single).
2. Choose a book from the list. For your first PDF, choose a short book (for example Ruth, Jonah,
   Philippians or Jude), because it prints quickly.
3. To print only some chapters, type the first chapter in [**From Chapter**](#s-t-chapfrom) and the last chapter in
   **To**.

To print several books, click [**Select Multiple Books...**](#s-btn-chooseBooks), click the books you want, and click
**OK**. See the **Basic tab** chapter for more ways to choose books and passages.

## 2.6 Make your first PDF {#01-getting-started--make-your-first-pdf}

1. Click **Print (Make PDF)** at the bottom right of the window (or press **Ctrl+P**).
2. PTXprint saves your settings, then makes the PDF. A progress bar shows that it is working. This
   takes from a few seconds to a few minutes, depending on the number of books and pictures.
3. When PTXprint has finished, the **PDF Preview** window opens and shows the PDF.

If a message appears instead of the PDF, read it carefully. Two common messages at the start are:

* **"No books to print"** – no book is selected. Choose a book on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.
* **"One or more fonts have not been set yet"** – on the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, choose a font for
  the main text (see ["Change the main font"](#01-getting-started--change-the-main-font) below).

## 2.7 Look at the PDF in the preview {#01-getting-started--look-at-the-pdf-in-the-preview}

The **PDF Preview** window shows the pages of your PDF.

* To move from page to page, use the arrow buttons at the top, the **Left/Right arrow** keys, or
  the mouse wheel.
* To make the page bigger or smaller, use the [**Zoom**](#s-s-pdfZoomLevel) box, or hold **Ctrl** and turn the mouse
  wheel.
* Tick [**Book View**](#s-c-bkView) (or press **Ctrl+B**) to see two facing pages side by side, as in a printed
  book.
* The title bar shows the name of the PDF file and the time it was made. Check it, so you know
  you are looking at the newest PDF.
* Click **Show main PTXprint settings** (or press **Alt+S**) to go back to the main window.

Closing the Preview window only hides it. It comes back the next time you print. The Preview
window can also find layout problems and fix them. See the chapter **PDF Preview window, layout
analysis and page filling**.

## 2.8 Change a few common things {#01-getting-started--change-a-few-common-things}

After each change, click **Print (Make PDF)** again to see the result.

### Change the page size {#01-getting-started--change-the-page-size}

1. Click the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.
2. In the **Page Setup** area, open the [**Page Size**](#s-ecb-pagesize) list.
3. Choose a size, for example **148mm, 210mm (A5)**. Or type your own size: the width, a comma,
   then the height, for example `140mm, 216mm`.

Ask your printer for the exact page size (the ["trim size"](#18-printers--trim-size)) before you do a lot of work. If you
change the page size later, every line of the book moves.

### Change the main font {#01-getting-started--change-the-main-font}

1. Click the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab.
2. In the **Font Configuration** area, click the **Select Font...** button next to **Regular**.
3. The **Pick a Font (and Typeface)** dialog opens. Type part of the font name in the search box,
   then click the font in the list.
4. Click **OK**.

PTXprint then fills in the [**Bold**](#s-c-styFaceBold), [**Italic**](#s-c-styFaceItalic) and **Bold Italic** fonts from the same font
family. If some characters print as empty boxes, the font does not have those characters. See the
**Fonts+Script tab** chapter.

### Change the font size {#01-getting-started--change-the-font-size}

1. Click the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.
2. In the **Page Setup** area, change [**Base Font Size (pt)**](#s-s-fontsize). For example, 11 pt is a common size
   for the main text.

When [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) is ticked (the normal setting), PTXprint changes the [**Base Line Spacing (pt)**](#s-s-linespacing)
with the font size, so the page keeps the same look. Headings, footnotes and verse numbers also
grow or shrink with the main text. See the **Layout tab** chapter.

### Change between one and two columns {#01-getting-started--change-between-one-and-two-columns}

1. Click the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.
2. Tick **Two Column Layout** for two columns, or untick it for one column.

PTXprint changes the [**Base Indent**](#s-s-indentUnit) for you when you change the number of columns.

### Turn pictures on or off {#01-getting-started--turn-pictures-on-or-off}

The [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab is not shown in the **Mini** view. If you cannot see it, click **≡** ›
[**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) › **Basic View** (or higher).

1. Click the **Pictures** tab.
2. On the [**Global Options**](#s-lb-settings) sub-tab, tick [**Include Pictures (illustrations)**](#s-c-includeillustrations) to print the
   pictures, or untick it to leave them out.

The first time you turn pictures on, PTXprint needs a list of the pictures (the PicList). It makes
this list from the `\fig` entries in your Paratext text. See "Show the pictures that are in the
Paratext text" in the **Pictures tab** chapter. For a draft, choose **Low Resolution (Smaller
File)** on the same sub-tab, so that the PDF stays small.

## 2.9 Keep different settings for different outputs {#01-getting-started--keep-different-settings-for-different-outputs}

You often need more than one kind of PDF from the same project. For example:

* a **draft** for checking, with wide spacing, "DRAFT" on each page and small pictures;
* a **final** PDF for the printer, with high-quality pictures and the PDF type that the printer
  asks for.

Do not change one configuration back and forth. Make a separate configuration for each kind of
output. Each configuration remembers its own settings.

### Make a new configuration {#01-getting-started--make-a-new-configuration}

1. Click **Save** at the bottom of the window, so that your latest changes are kept.
2. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, in the **Layout Configuration** area, click the **Save As** button (the
   icon next to the **Name** list).
3. The [**Save Current Configuration As...**](#03-basic--save-current-configuration-as) dialog opens. Type a name, for example `Draft` or
   `Final_A5`. Use only letters, numbers, brackets `( )`, underscores `_` and hyphens `-`. No
   spaces.
4. Click **OK**. PTXprint makes the new configuration as a copy of the current settings, and
   changes to it.
5. Now change the settings for this kind of output. The other configuration stays as it was.

### Change to another configuration {#01-getting-started--change-to-another-configuration}

1. Click **Save** first. PTXprint does **not** save the current configuration when you choose
   another one.
2. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, choose the configuration in the **Name** list.

You can lock a finished configuration with a password, so that nobody changes it by mistake. See
["Protect a finished configuration"](#03-basic--protect-a-finished-configuration) in the **Basic tab** chapter.

## 2.10 How PTXprint saves your settings {#01-getting-started--how-ptxprint-saves-your-settings}

* **Save** (or **Ctrl+S**) saves the settings of the current configuration.
* **Print (Make PDF)** always saves the settings first, then makes the PDF.
* When you choose a different **project**, PTXprint saves the current configuration first.
* When you choose a different **configuration**, PTXprint does **not** save first.
* **Quit** closes PTXprint **without saving**. Click **Save** before you click **Quit**.

PTXprint keeps the configurations inside the Paratext project. So when you use Send/Receive in
Paratext, the other people on your team get the same configurations.

## 2.11 Where the PDF is saved {#01-getting-started--where-the-pdf-is-saved}

PTXprint saves the PDF inside the Paratext project, in a folder called `local\ptxprint`. This
folder is not shared by Send/Receive. The file name is made from the project code, the
configuration name and the books, for example `ABC_Default_JHN_ptxp.pdf`.

To open the folder, do one of these:

* Click the **Open folder containing the PDF** button in the bar at the bottom of the main window
  (**Regular** and **Full** views).
* On the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab, click the blue link next to [**Output PDF Location**](#s-l-working-dir).
* In the PDF Preview window, click **Open folder containing the PDF**.

PTXprint makes the PDF again each time you print, with the same name. To keep a PDF (for example
the one you sent to a consultant), copy it to another folder, or click **Save the PDF with a
different name** in the PDF Preview window.

## 2.12 When something goes wrong {#01-getting-started--when-something-goes-wrong}

* **Read the message.** PTXprint shows a message in a window, or in the status line above the
  bottom bar. It often tells you what to change.
* **Check the view level.** If a tab or setting has disappeared, the view level may be too low.
  Click **≡** › [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) › **Full View**. Or type the name of the setting in the
  **Search for settings** box at the bottom-left of the window.
* **Check the "Common problems" section** of the chapter about the tab you were using.
* **Look in the chapter "Problems and solutions"** for problems that are not about one tab.
* **Ask for help.** The chapter [**Help tab and getting support**](#ch-21-help) explains how to ask the Support
  Agent, the PTXprint User Community, or the support team, and how to make an archive file that
  the support team can use to see your problem.

## 2.13 What to read next {#01-getting-started--what-to-read-next}

* [**The main window, menu and view levels**](#ch-02-main-window) – more about configurations, view levels and saving.
* [**Basic tab**](#ch-03-basic) and [**Layout tab**](#ch-04-layout) – the most important settings for every publication.
* [**How do I...? (step-by-step tasks)**](#ch-30-howto) – short instructions for many common jobs.

# 3. The main window, menu and view levels {#ch-02-main-window}

## 3.1 What this part of PTXprint is for {#02-main-window--what-this-part-of-ptxprint-is-for}

The main window is where you do all your work in PTXprint. It has three parts:

* **The tabs** across the top (**Basic**, **Layout**, **Fonts+Script**, [**Body**](#s-lb-Body) and so on). Each tab holds one group of settings.
* [**The ≡ main menu**](#02-main-window--the-main-menu) button at the top-left corner, before the first tab. It holds settings about PTXprint itself, not about your book: how to show the PDF, the [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level), the interface **Language**, and links to [**Donate**](#s-btn-menu-donate) and [**Give Feedback**](#s-btn-menu-feedback).
* **The bar at the bottom of the window**, with the **Search for settings** box, the button to open the output folder, the [**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun) and [**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate) check boxes, and the **Save**, **Print (Make PDF)** and **Quit** buttons.

This chapter also explains three ideas that you need everywhere in PTXprint: **configurations**, [**view levels**](#02-main-window--view-levels), and how PTXprint **saves** your settings.

## 3.2 Projects and configurations {#02-main-window--projects-and-configurations}

A **project** is a Paratext project – the Scripture text that you want to print. You choose it on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, in the **Project** list.

A **configuration** (also called a "layout" or "config") is a named set of PTXprint settings for one project. One project can have many configurations, for example `Default` for a draft, `NT_A5` for a small New Testament, and `Large_Print`. Each configuration remembers its own page size, fonts, pictures, styles, front matter and so on.

* Every project has a configuration called **Default**. You cannot delete it, lock it or copy it to other projects, but you can reset it.
* You choose, create, lock, copy and delete configurations on the **Basic** tab, in the **Layout Configuration** area. See the chapter about the Basic tab.
* PTXprint keeps the configurations inside the Paratext project folder. So when you use **Send/Receive** in Paratext, other people on the team get the same configurations.

## 3.3 How PTXprint saves your settings {#02-main-window--how-ptxprint-saves-your-settings}

* **Save** (or **Ctrl+S**) saves the settings of the current configuration.
* **Print (Make PDF)** (or **Ctrl+P**) **always saves** the settings first, then makes the PDF.
* When you choose a **different project** in the **Project** list, PTXprint saves the current configuration first.
* When you choose a **different configuration** in the **Layout Configuration** list, PTXprint does **not** save the current one first. Click **Save** before you change, or your recent changes are lost.
* **Quit** closes PTXprint **without saving**. Click **Save** or **Print (Make PDF)** before **Quit** to keep your changes.
* If a configuration is **locked** with a password, PTXprint does not save changes to it. You can still change settings on the screen and make a PDF, but the changes are not kept.

Some things are remembered for you (the user), not for the configuration: the view level, the interface language, the [**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF) choice and the [**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun) setting. These stay the same for all projects and configurations.

## 3.4 View levels {#02-main-window--view-levels}

PTXprint has hundreds of settings. Most people need only a few. So PTXprint can hide the settings that you do not need. This is the [**view level**](#s-btn-menu-level). There are four view levels:

| View level | What you see | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Mini** | Only the **Basic**, **Layout**, **Fonts+Script** and **Help** tabs, and only the most important settings on them: project, books, configuration name, page size, font size, two columns, the main font. | A first look at PTXprint, or a quick draft. |
| **Basic** | Adds the [**Body**](#s-lb-Body), [**Notes+Refs**](#s-lb-NotesRefs), [**Header+Footer**](#s-lb-HeadFoot), **Pictures**, [**Peripherals**](#s-lb-Peripherals) and [**Finishing**](#s-lb-Finishing) tabs, and more settings on each tab (margins, line spacing, bold and italic fonts, the **Import Settings** button…). On **Peripherals** and **Finishing** it shows only the main settings (table of contents and front matter; pages per sheet and comparing PDFs). | Most simple publications. |
| **Regular** | Adds the [**Diglot**](#s-lb-Diglot), [**Tabs+Borders**](#s-lb-TabsBorders), **Styles**, **Advanced** and [**View+Edit**](#s-lb-Viewer) tabs, and many more settings on all tabs. | Most typesetters. PTXprint uses this level the first time it starts. |
| **Full** | Shows every setting, including the [**Publications**](#s-lb-Publications) and [**Printers**](#s-lb-Printers) tabs. | Experienced users who need special settings. |

**How to change the view level:** click the **≡** button (top-left), point to **View Level**, and click **Mini View**, **Basic View**, **Regular View** or **Full View**. The current level is shown in blue and bold in that list. The change happens at once, without a restart.

**Hidden settings still work.** A lower view level only *hides* settings. A hidden setting keeps its value, is still saved with the configuration, and still changes the PDF. For example, if you turned on pictures or a diglot in the **Regular** view and then change to the **Mini** view, the pictures or the diglot are still in the PDF, though you cannot see the tab. If the PDF looks different from what you expect, change to the **Full** view and check the settings again.

**Search finds hidden settings.** If you choose a setting in **Search for settings** that is hidden at your view level, PTXprint changes to a higher view level to show it.

## 3.5 Tab labels and highlighted settings {#02-main-window--tab-labels-and-highlighted-settings}

PTXprint uses colour and bold text to show what is turned on or changed:

* The open tab has a light blue background and a bold label.
* Some tab labels turn **blue** when their main feature is turned on:
  * **Pictures** – pictures are included.
  * [**Diglot**](#s-lb-Diglot) – the diglot is turned on.
  * [**Peripherals**](#s-lb-Peripherals) – front matter, back matter PDFs or a table of contents is turned on.
  * [**Finishing**](#s-lb-Finishing) – more than one page per sheet.
  * **Advanced** – one of its special files or options (custom script, changes file, extra TeX or style files, interlinear) is turned on.
  * **Fonts+Script** – the word "Fonts" is blue when coloured text is enabled.
  * [**Notes+Refs**](#s-lb-NotesRefs) – "Refs" is blue when an extended cross-reference list is used.
  * [**Tabs+Borders**](#s-lb-TabsBorders) – "Tabs" or ["Borders"](#s-btn-sbBorders) is blue when thumb tabs or decorative borders are turned on.
* Some number settings (mostly on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab: font size, line spacing, margins, column gutter, header and footer positions and similar) have a label that becomes [**bold**](#s-c-styFaceBold) when the value is different from the PTXprint default. So you can see quickly which values you have changed.

## 3.6 Help on any setting: F1 and Ctrl+click {#02-main-window--help-on-any-setting-f1-and-ctrl-click}

This manual is always at hand while you work:

* Press **F1** with the mouse over a setting to open the manual at that setting's entry. If the setting
  has no entry of its own, the manual opens at the part about the group of settings, dialog or tab it
  is in. This works in dialogs too.
* **Ctrl+click** the name of a tab (also the smaller tabs inside some tabs, such as **Footnotes**) to open
  the manual at the part about that tab. The tab's tooltip reminds you of this.

The manual opens in the **Manual** tab of the PDF Preview window, fitted to the window. Use **Alt+Left**
(or the **◀** button under the contents) to go back to where you were reading before.

## 3.7 The bottom bar {#02-main-window--the-bottom-bar}

From left to right, the bar at the bottom of the window has:

* **Search for settings** – type a word to find a setting.
* **Open folder containing the PDF** – opens the output folder. (Regular and Full views.)
* [**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun) and [**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate) – two check boxes that make printing faster.
* **Print** – only appears when you are looking at the secondary text of a diglot.
* **Save**, **Print (Make PDF)** and **Quit**.

Above the bar, a **status line** sometimes shows a message from PTXprint (for example "No books to print"). Click **Dismiss** to hide it.

When a newer version of PTXprint is available, a **Check for updates...** button can appear at the top-left, just to the right of the ≡ button. (PTXprint checks at most once a day, only on Windows, and only if Internet use is allowed on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab.)

## 3.8 The ≡ main menu {#02-main-window--the-main-menu}

* [**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF) – what happens with the PDF after printing:
  * **Preview Pane** – PTXprint shows the PDF in its own preview window. This is the usual choice. PTXprint can also use the preview for some editing tools.
  * **System Viewer** – the PDF opens in the PDF program on your computer.
  * **Output Folder** – PTXprint opens the folder that holds the PDF.
* [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) – see ["View levels"](#02-main-window--view-levels) above.
* **Language** – the language of the PTXprint menus and labels.
* [**Donate**](#s-btn-menu-donate) and [**Give Feedback**](#s-btn-menu-feedback) – open a web page.

## 3.9 Common tasks {#02-main-window--common-tasks}

### See more (or fewer) settings {#02-main-window--see-more-or-fewer-settings}

Click **≡** › [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) › **Full View** to see every setting, or **Mini View** to see only the most important ones.

### Find a setting when you do not know which tab it is on {#02-main-window--find-a-setting-when-you-do-not-know-which-tab-it-is-on}

1. Click in the **Search for settings** box at the bottom-left (or press **Ctrl+F**).
2. Type a word, for example `margin` or `footnote`, and press **Enter**.
3. A short list of settings appears above the box. Click the one you want.
4. PTXprint opens the right tab and highlights the setting. If the setting was hidden, PTXprint changes the view level so you can see it.
5. To clear the search, click the small clear icon at the right end of the box.

### Make a PDF {#02-main-window--make-a-pdf}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, choose the project, the configuration and the books.
2. Click **Print (Make PDF)** (or press **Ctrl+P**).
3. Wait. A progress bar shows that PTXprint is working. Then the PDF appears (in the preview pane, the system viewer or the output folder, depending on [**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF)).

### Make the PDF faster while you work on the layout {#02-main-window--make-the-pdf-faster-while-you-work-on-the-layout}

1. Tick [**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun) (or press **Ctrl+Q**).
2. If you only change layout settings (spacing, margins, styles), you can also tick [**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate) (Regular and Full views).
3. When the layout is ready, untick **Quick Run** and click **Print (Make PDF)** one more time, so that the table of contents, page references and other details are correct.

### Show the PDF in another program {#02-main-window--show-the-pdf-in-another-program}

Click **≡** › [**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF) › **System Viewer**.

### Find the PDF file on your computer {#02-main-window--find-the-pdf-file-on-your-computer}

Click the **Open folder containing the PDF** button at the bottom of the window (Regular and Full views), or choose **≡** › [**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF) › **Output Folder**. The folder with the PDF files for this project opens.

### Change the language of PTXprint {#02-main-window--change-the-language-of-ptxprint}

1. Click **Save** first, so you do not lose changes.
2. Click **≡** › **Language** and click a language.
3. PTXprint closes its window and opens it again in the new language, with the same project and configuration.

## 3.10 Common problems {#02-main-window--common-problems}

### A tab or setting that I used before has disappeared {#02-main-window--a-tab-or-setting-that-i-used-before-has-disappeared}

**Likely cause:** The view level is lower than before. **What to do:** Click **≡** › [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) › **Regular View** or **Full View**. Or type the name of the setting in **Search for settings**.

### The PDF has pictures (or a diglot, borders, thumb tabs…) but I cannot find the setting {#02-main-window--the-pdf-has-pictures-or-a-diglot-borders-thumb-tabs-but-i-cannot-find-the-setting}

**Likely cause:** The setting was turned on in a higher view level, and now that tab is hidden. Hidden settings still work. **What to do:** Change to **Full View** and turn the feature off on its tab.

### I lost my changes after I chose another configuration {#02-main-window--i-lost-my-changes-after-i-chose-another-configuration}

**Likely cause:** PTXprint does not save the current configuration when you choose another one in the **Layout Configuration** list. **What to do:** Always click **Save** (or **Print (Make PDF)**) before you change to another configuration.

### I lost my changes after I clicked Quit {#02-main-window--i-lost-my-changes-after-i-clicked-quit}

**Likely cause:** **Quit** does not save. **What to do:** Click **Save** before **Quit**.

### The Print (Make PDF) and Save buttons are greyed out {#02-main-window--the-print-make-pdf-and-save-buttons-are-greyed-out}

**Likely cause:** PTXprint cannot print yet. For example, no project is selected, or another problem is shown in the status line. **What to do:** Read the message in the status line above the bottom bar. Choose a project on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab and fix the problem that is described.

### PTXprint says "Cannot update PDF file while it is locked!" {#02-main-window--ptxprint-says-cannot-update-pdf-file-while-it-is-locked}

**Likely cause:** The old PDF is still open in another PDF program, so PTXprint cannot replace it. **What to do:** Close the PDF in the other program and click to try again. To avoid this, use **≡** › [**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF) › **Preview Pane**.

### PTXprint says "No books to print" {#02-main-window--ptxprint-says-no-books-to-print}

**Likely cause:** No book is selected, or the book list is empty. **What to do:** On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, in **What to Print**, choose a book or click [**Select Multiple Books...**](#s-btn-chooseBooks).

### PTXprint says "One or more fonts have not been set yet" {#02-main-window--ptxprint-says-one-or-more-fonts-have-not-been-set-yet}

**What to do:** On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, choose a font for the main text.

### The table of contents or page numbers in the PDF are wrong {#02-main-window--the-table-of-contents-or-page-numbers-in-the-pdf-are-wrong}

**Likely cause:** [**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun) is ticked, so PTXprint ran the typesetting only once. **What to do:** Untick **Quick Run** and print again.

### My change to the text in Paratext does not appear in the PDF {#02-main-window--my-change-to-the-text-in-paratext-does-not-appear-in-the-pdf}

**Likely cause:** PTXprint usually notices that the text changed and processes it again, even when [**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate) is ticked. If it does not, **Layout Only** may be stopping it. **What to do:** Untick **Layout Only** and print again.

### The changes I make are not kept {#02-main-window--the-changes-i-make-are-not-kept}

**Likely cause:** The configuration is locked with a password, so it is not saved. **What to do:** On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click the lock button and enter the password to unlock it. Or use **Save As** to make a new configuration.

## 3.11 Settings reference {#02-main-window--settings-reference}

### Main menu (top-left ≡ button) {#02-main-window--main-menu-top-left-button}

#### Show PDF {#s-btn-menu-showPDF}

Menu button · shown in: all views

> Choose how the PDF is shown after printing: in the preview pane, in your system's PDF viewer, or by opening the output folder.

The current choice is shown in blue. When you click a choice, PTXprint uses it at once to show the last PDF, and remembers it for all projects. **Preview Pane** is best for most people: PTXprint can then update the preview itself, and no other program keeps the PDF file open.

#### View Level {#s-btn-menu-level}

Menu button · shown in: all views

> Choose how many settings PTXprint shows. Hidden settings keep their values and still take effect.

The current level is shown in blue. PTXprint remembers the view level for you, not for each configuration. The first time PTXprint starts, it uses the **Regular View**.

#### Language {#s-btn-menu-lang}

Menu button · shown in: all views

> Change the language of the PTXprint user interface.

The current language is shown in blue. When you choose another language, PTXprint closes and opens its window again in that language, with the same project and configuration. PTXprint saves your settings first (a locked configuration is not saved). This changes only the PTXprint menus and labels, not the language of your book.

#### Donate {#s-btn-menu-donate}

Button · shown in: all views\
Also: Donate toward PTXprint Development

> PTXprint is a tool that is freely available to all without any restrictions. Our aim is to help people get the Scriptures out to people in formats that work best for their local context.
>
> Click to contribute toward the ongoing development and maintenance of tools by SIL Global's Language Technology Developers so that others can also benefit.
>
> https://give.sil.org/campaign/725128/donate

Opens the SIL donation web page in your web browser. If [**Disable ALL Internet Use**](#s-c-noInternet) is ticked on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, PTXprint shows a message instead.

#### Give Feedback {#s-btn-menu-feedback}

Button · shown in: all views\
Also: Link to PTXprint Feedback Form (Google Form)

> Psst! Can we have 5 minutes of your time? You could help us make PTXprint better!
>
> The developers of PTXprint would love to know how this tool is being used. What is your favorite feature? Are there any annoyances? Tell us what you like, or don't like. Tell us what you dream for in the future.
>
> Click this button to fill in the Google form or type this in a browser: https://tiny.cc/ptxprintfeedback

Opens the feedback form in your web browser. It needs Internet access (see [**Disable ALL Internet Use**](#s-c-noInternet) on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab).

### Main window {#02-main-window--main-window}

#### Basic {#s-lb-Basic}

Label · shown in: all views

> Select the Project and Book(s), to be used to create the PDF file.
>
> You can also Save/Share Configuration settings.

Choose the project, the configuration and the books here. Always visible.

#### Layout {#s-lb-Layout}

Label · shown in: all views

> Page Setup, Font Size and Line Spacing. Margins, Columns and Rules (lines).

Some number labels on this tab become bold when you change the value from the default.

#### Fonts+Script {#s-lb-Font}

Label · shown in: all views

> Basic Fonts and Advanced Font options. Also a range of Advanced typography settings to support any Writing System. Advanced Spacing Settings. Fallback fonts for characters missing in primary font.

The word "Fonts" in the tab label turns blue when coloured text is enabled.

#### Body {#s-lb-Body}

Label · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> Main settings to control the beginning and ending of books, and options for what should be included in the Main Body of text. Also settings for special books.

What goes into the main text, and how books and chapters start.

#### Notes+Refs {#s-lb-NotesRefs}

Label · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> Control how Footnotes, Cross-references, Study Notes and Questions should appear.

The word "Refs" in the label turns blue when an extended cross-reference list is used.

#### Header+Footer {#s-lb-HeadFoot}

Label · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> Adjust the content of headers and footers.

What appears at the top and bottom of each page.

#### Pictures {#s-lb-Pictures}

Label · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> Manipulate the pictures to be used in the publication. Control everything from quality to position, from captions to copyrights.

The label turns blue when pictures are included in the PDF. In the **Mini** view the tab is hidden, but pictures that are turned on are still printed.

#### Diglot {#s-lb-Diglot}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Create a diglot publication by selecting a secondary project and configuration.

For printing two (or more) texts side by side. The label turns blue when the diglot is turned on.

#### Tabs+Borders {#s-lb-TabsBorders}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Settings for thumb-tabs and options to add decorative borders or embellishments to the text.

"Tabs" or ["Borders"](#s-btn-sbBorders) in the label turns blue when that feature is turned on.

#### Styles {#s-lb-StyleEditor}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Edit style information of markers without having to edit the USFM stylesheet files.

Change how each USFM marker looks (font, size, spacing, colour…).

#### Advanced {#s-lb-Advanced}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Define stylesheets, tex macros, front and back matter PDFs, watermarks and various other advanced settings including interlinear (& ruby text) output.

Also holds the [**Disable ALL Internet Use**](#s-c-noInternet) option. The label turns blue when one of its special options is turned on (for example a custom script, a changes file, extra TeX or style files, or interlinear output).

#### View+Edit {#s-lb-Viewer}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> View and edit various control and log files. Examine final SFM output and tweak adjust lists.

Look at and edit the front matter, adjust lists, log files and the processed text.

#### Peripherals {#s-lb-Peripherals}

Label · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> Define what material should be placed before and/or after the main scripture pages.

Front matter, table of contents, back matter and variables. The label turns blue when front matter, front or back PDFs, or an automatic table of contents is turned on. In the **Basic** view it shows only the table of contents and front matter settings.

#### Publications {#s-lb-Publications}

Label · shown in: Full view only

> Define several publications (each with its own books, titles and other variables) from this one configuration, and print them all in one go.

Define several publications from one configuration and print them together.

#### Finishing {#s-lb-Finishing}

Label · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> Options to control pagination, PDF output format and compare output with a previous PDF.

The label turns blue when more than one page per sheet is chosen. In the **Basic** view it shows only the pages-per-sheet and compare-PDF settings.

#### Printers {#s-lb-Printers}

Label · shown in: Full view only

> Estimate printing costs, compare printers and check the book thickness. Some printers also give live quotations and take orders.

The [**Printers**](#ch-18-printers) tab.

#### Help {#s-lb-Help}

Label · shown in: all views

> Links to useful folders and online resources. Where to obtain help from others.

Links to folders and to online help. Always visible.

#### btn_menu {#s-btn-menu}

Menu button · shown in: all views

The **≡** button at the top-left of the window. It opens the main menu ([**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF), [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level), **Language**, [**Donate**](#s-btn-menu-donate), [**Give Feedback**](#s-btn-menu-feedback)). Always visible.

#### Find help {#s-t-find}

Text box · shown in: all views

> Type in a word to search for a setting that you can't locate. A short list of relevant topics will appear above. Select a topic to jump to the appropriate setting which will be highlighted.
>
> Shortcut: Ctrl-F

Press **Enter** (or click the magnifying-glass icon) to search. Click a result: PTXprint opens the right tab, highlights the setting and, if needed, raises the view level so you can see it. Click the clear icon at the right end of the box to remove the highlight. Short, simple words (for example `margin`, `caption`, `verse`) work best. While PTXprint is printing, this box shows "Processing...".

#### Open folder containing the PDF {#s-btn-openFolder}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Open the folder which contains the PDF file(s) created for this project.

Opens the folder in your file manager. In views where this button is hidden, use **≡** › [**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF) › **Output Folder**.

#### Quick Run {#s-c-quickRun}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: all views\
Also: Quick run (to speed up process)

> Enabling this option will give quicker output, but it may be less refined.
>
> PTXprint needs to rerun the typesetting process in order to ensure the Table of Contents & other dynamically updated details are accurate.
>
> Shortcut: Ctrl-Q

Without it, PTXprint runs the typesetting several times (up to 5) so that the table of contents, cross-page details and page layout are correct. With it, it runs only once. Tick it while you try out settings. Untick it for the final PDF. PTXprint remembers this setting for you, not for the configuration.

#### Layout Only {#s-c-noupdate}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Layout Only (skip USFM processing)

> Re-runs page layout without regenerating or processing USFM scripture content.
>
> Useful for quick layout tweaks (+1 / −1 spacing or style changes).
>
> PTXprint still re-processes the USFM when the text has changed in Paratext, or when you change a setting that affects the text (the box then shows a dash until the next successful print).
>
> This setting is not saved with the configuration.

Faster when you only change layout, spacing or style settings. Settings that change the text include which books, footnotes, or verse numbers to include. If you tick it while the colophon is turned on, PTXprint turns the colophon off.

#### Print {#s-b-print2ndDiglotText}

Button · shown in: all views

> The configuration displayed now is for the secondary project of the Diglot. You can use this button to create a PDF with just the secondary text to check the settings specified.
>
> Use the larger 'Return to Primary' button to get back to the primary project in order to print a diglot with both texts.

Only appears when the main window shows the secondary project of a diglot (after you switch to it on the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab).

#### Save {#s-btn-saveConfig}

Button · shown in: all views\
Also: Save configuration

> Save current settings in named Configuration (set on the [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic)).
>
> Shortcut: Ctrl-S

Saves all settings of the current configuration, including hidden ones. You do not need it before **Print (Make PDF)**, because printing saves too. Greyed out when PTXprint cannot print (for example when no project is selected) and when the configuration is locked. If you typed a new name in the configuration name box on the **Basic** tab, **Save** creates a new configuration with that name.

#### Print (Make PDF) {#s-b-print}

Button · shown in: all views

> Create the PDF as specified (automatically saves settings).
>
> Shortcut: Ctrl-P

First checks that there are books to print and that the main font is set. If an old PDF with the same name is open in another program, PTXprint asks you to close it. While PTXprint is printing, you cannot start another print. When you are looking at the secondary text of a diglot, this button is called **Return to Primary**.

#### Quit {#s-b-close}

Button · shown in: all views

> Close PTXprint without saving.
>
> Shortcut: Ctrl-W

Click **Save** first if you want to keep your changes.

# 4. How do I...? (step-by-step tasks) {#ch-30-howto}

## 4.1 How to use this chapter {#30-howto--how-to-use-this-chapter}

This chapter gives short, step-by-step answers to the questions people ask most often. A task often uses more than one tab. **See also** names the chapter with more detail.

For every task:

* Most changes appear in the PDF only after you click **Print (Make PDF)** again.
* Lower [**view levels**](#02-main-window--view-levels) hide many settings. If you cannot see a tab or setting, click **≡** (top-left) › [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) › **Full View**, or type its name in the **Search for settings** box (bottom-left).
* Click **Save** before you change to another configuration. PTXprint does not save the current configuration when you choose another one.
* "pt" means point. 1 pt is about 0.35 mm.

## 4.2 Printing: what goes into the PDF {#30-howto--printing-what-goes-into-the-pdf}

### How do I make a PDF? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-a-pdf}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, choose the **Project**, the configuration (**Name**) and the books.
2. Click **Print (Make PDF)** at the bottom of the window (or press **Ctrl+P**).
3. Wait for the progress bar to finish. The PDF opens in the **PDF Preview** window.

See also: [Main window](#ch-02-main-window); [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I print one book? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-one-book}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, in **What to Print**, click [**Single Book**](#s-r-book-single).
2. Choose the book, then click **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I print only some chapters of a book? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-only-some-chapters-of-a-book}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click [**Single Book**](#s-r-book-single) and choose the book.
2. Type the first chapter in [**From Chapter**](#s-t-chapfrom) and the last in **To**.
3. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

When you choose another book, PTXprint sets the chapters back to the whole book.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I print several books? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-several-books}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click [**Select Multiple Books...**](#s-btn-chooseBooks).
2. Click each book, or a group button: [**All Books**](#s-b-mbsAll), [**Old Testament**](#s-b-mbsOT), [**New Testament**](#s-b-mbsNT), [**Deuterocanon**](#s-b-mbsDC) or [**Extra Material**](#s-b-mbsXtra). Click a group button again to unselect that group. [**Toggle Books**](#s-b-mbsToggle) reverses the selection and [**Reset All**](#s-b-mbsNone) unselects all. Hold **Shift** and click to select all books between two books.
3. Click **OK**, then **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I print only some passages (for example Psalm 23 and Luke 15)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-only-some-passages-for-example-psalm-23-and-luke-15}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click in the box beside [**Portions or Multiple Books**](#s-r-book-multiple) (or press **Ctrl+B**).
2. Type references with 3-letter book codes, for example `PSA 23; 100 LUK 15:11-32`. Ranges such as `MAT-ACT` or `GEN 1:1-2:3` also work.
3. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

Use book codes such as `JHN`, not names such as `John`.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I make the PDF faster while I am still working on the layout? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-the-pdf-faster-while-i-am-still-working-on-the-layout}

1. At the bottom of the window, tick [**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun) (or press **Ctrl+Q**).
2. If you only change layout settings (spacing, margins, styles), also tick [**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate) (Regular and Full views).
3. For the final PDF, untick both and print again, so the table of contents and page references are correct.

See also: [Main window](#ch-02-main-window).

### How do I find the PDF file on my computer? {#30-howto--how-do-i-find-the-pdf-file-on-my-computer}

Click **Open folder containing the PDF** at the bottom of the window (Regular and Full views), or **≡** › [**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF) › **Output Folder**. Or click the blue link next to [**Output PDF Location**](#s-l-working-dir) on the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab.

The PDF name starts with the project name, then the configuration name and the books, for example `ABC_NT_A5_MAT-REV_ptxp.pdf`.

See also: [Main window](#ch-02-main-window); [Help tab](#ch-21-help).

### How do I open the PDF in my normal PDF program instead of the preview? {#30-howto--how-do-i-open-the-pdf-in-my-normal-pdf-program-instead-of-the-preview}

Click **≡** › [**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF) › **System Viewer**. Or, in the **PDF Preview** window, click **Open the PDF in Default PDF Viewer**.

Close the PDF in the other program before you print again. Otherwise PTXprint cannot replace the file.

See also: [Main window](#ch-02-main-window); [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview).

### How do I get a Bible text to practise with? {#30-howto--how-do-i-get-a-bible-text-to-practise-with}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, open the **Project** list and choose **Import...** (the last item).
2. Click [**Install BSB**](#s-b-installBSB). PTXprint installs the Berean Standard Bible and opens it.

In the same dialog you can also install a Scripture text bundle (.zip) from the Digital Bible Library or Open.Bible.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I learn PTXprint with a tutorial? {#30-howto--how-do-i-learn-ptxprint-with-a-tutorial}

1. Choose a practice project and configuration (make one with **Save As**). The tutorial changes its settings.
2. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click [**Run Tutorial...**](#s-btn-runTutorial) (Basic, Regular and Full views) and choose the tutorial file (.json, or a recorded test in a .zip). You may get one from a trainer.
3. A small tutorial window shows the next step, and PTXprint highlights the control it uses.
4. Click **Step** (or press **Space**) for the next step, **Skip** ([**S**](#32-glossary--s)) to leave it out, **Play** ([**P**](#32-glossary--p)) to run the steps one after another, or **Run to end**.
5. Close the tutorial window to stop. If PTXprint raised the view level for the tutorial, it changes it back.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

## 4.3 Page size, margins and columns {#30-howto--page-size-margins-and-columns}

### How do I change the page size (for example to A5)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-the-page-size-for-example-to-a5}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, in **Page Setup**, choose a [**Page Size**](#s-ecb-pagesize), for example **148mm, 210mm (A5)**.
2. If [**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) is red, click one fine-tune button (see ["How do I stop wasting space at the bottom of every page?"](#30-howto--how-do-i-stop-wasting-space-at-the-bottom-of-every-page)).
3. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

Ask your printer for the exact trim size before you start. A change of page size moves every line in the book.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout).

### How do I use a page size that is not in the list? {#30-howto--how-do-i-use-a-page-size-that-is-not-in-the-list}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, click in the [**Page Size**](#s-ecb-pagesize) box.
2. Type the width, a comma, and the height, for example `140mm, 216mm`. You can use `mm`, `cm` or `in`.
3. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

The size is saved when you save or print. After that it is in the **Page Size** list for all your projects. To remove a saved size, select it, right-click in the box and choose **Remove**.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout).

### How do I make the margins smaller? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-the-margins-smaller}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, in **Margins**, make [**Side Margin Width (mm)**](#s-s-margins) smaller for the left and right margins.
2. Make [**Start of Page to Top of Text (mm)**](#s-s-topmargin) and [**Bottom of Text to End of Page (mm)**](#s-s-bottommargin) smaller for the top and bottom.
3. Check the blue numbers in the margin picture. A very small one means the header or footer is too close to the paper edge.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

Many printers cannot print closer than about 10 mm to the edge. Ask your printer.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout).

### How do I change from two columns to one column (or back)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-from-two-columns-to-one-column-or-back}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, tick or untick **Two Column Layout**.
2. For two columns, set **Gutter Width (mm)** (the space between the columns) and choose whether you want a **Vertical Rule in Gutter**.
3. Check [**Base Indent**](#s-s-indentUnit). PTXprint halves or doubles it for you.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

If **Two Column Layout** is greyed out, a diglot is on. A diglot always uses columns.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout).

### How do I print some books in one column and the rest in two columns? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-some-books-in-one-column-and-the-rest-in-two-columns}

1. Change to the **Full** view.
2. On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, in **Other Features**, tick **Use One Column Layout for These Books** (it says **Use Two Column Layout** if the publication is one column).
3. Type the book codes in the box beside it, for example `GLO PSA`, and print.

See also: [Body tab](#ch-06-body).

### How do I add extra space at the spine for binding? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-extra-space-at-the-spine-for-binding}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, in **Page Setup**, tick [**Binding Gutter (mm)**](#s-c-pagegutter).
2. Type the extra space, for example 5 mm. Thicker books need more. Ask your printer.
3. Leave [**Outer Gutter**](#s-c-outerGutter) unticked, and print.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout).

### How do I stop wasting space at the bottom of every page? {#30-howto--how-do-i-stop-wasting-space-at-the-bottom-of-every-page}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, look at [**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) (Regular and Full views). If it is red, part of a line is empty at the bottom of each page.
2. Click **one** fine-tune button: next to [**Base Line Spacing (pt)**](#s-s-linespacing), or next to the top or bottom margin in **Margins**.
3. The number turns blue. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

If [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) is ticked, the line-spacing button also changes the font size a little. Use a margin button to keep the font size.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout).

### How do I make a journaling Bible with a wide margin for notes? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-a-journaling-bible-with-a-wide-margin-for-notes}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, tick [**Notelines**](#s-c-noteLines) (Regular and Full views).
2. PTXprint ticks **Binding Gutter** and [**Outer Gutter**](#s-c-outerGutter) and sets a wide gutter (at least 40 mm).
3. Change the gutter width if needed, choose the line colour with the colour button, and print.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout); [Advanced tab](#ch-13-advanced).

## 4.4 Fonts and text size {#30-howto--fonts-and-text-size}

### How do I change the font? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-the-font}

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, click **Select Font...** next to **Regular**.
2. Type part of the font name in the search box, and click the font.
3. Click **OK**. PTXprint fills in [**Bold**](#s-c-styFaceBold), [**Italic**](#s-c-styFaceItalic) and **Bold Italic** from the same family.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

Choose a different bold or italic font **after** the Regular font. Choosing the Regular font again replaces the other three.

See also: [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts).

### How do I make the text bigger or smaller? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-the-text-bigger-or-smaller}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, in **Page Setup**, make sure [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) is ticked.
2. Change [**Base Font Size (pt)**](#s-s-fontsize). The line spacing changes with it.
3. If [**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) turns red, click one fine-tune button, then print.

All other text (headings, footnotes, verse numbers) changes by the same proportion.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout).

### How do I put more space between the lines but keep the same letter size? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-more-space-between-the-lines-but-keep-the-same-letter-size}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, untick [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline).
2. Make [**Base Line Spacing (pt)**](#s-s-linespacing) larger, for example from 14 to 15.
3. Tick **Lock Ratio** again if you want to keep the new ratio, and print.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout).

### How do I change the size or font of one kind of text (for example section headings or footnotes)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-the-size-or-font-of-one-kind-of-text-for-example-section-headings-or-footnotes}

1. Open the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab (Regular and Full views).
2. Type the marker in [**Find**](#s-t-styleSearch), for example `s1` for section headings, `f` for footnotes or `v` for verse numbers.
3. In **Character Settings**, change [**Font Size Factor**](#s-s-styFontSize) (1.0 = normal, 1.2 = 20% bigger). Tick [**Bold**](#s-c-styFaceBold) or [**Italic**](#s-c-styFaceItalic) if you want.
4. For a different font for this marker only, click **Select Font...**.
5. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

Each level has its own style: a change to `s1` does not change `s2`. To undo all your changes to a style, click its Reset (circular-arrows) button.

See also: [Styles tab](#ch-12-styles).

### How do I fix empty boxes (missing characters) in the PDF? {#30-howto--how-do-i-fix-empty-boxes-missing-characters-in-the-pdf}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, select as many books as possible.
2. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, tick [**Use Fallback Font**](#s-c-useFallbackFont) (Regular and Full views).
3. Click [**Find Missing Characters**](#s-btn-findMissingChars). PTXprint lists the characters that the Regular font does not have.
4. Click **Select Font...** next to the list and choose a font that has them. If the label turns red, that font lacks some of them too.
5. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

A Regular font that has your whole alphabet is often the better solution.

See also: [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts); [Problems and solutions](#ch-31-troubleshooting).

### How do I get real bold and italic instead of fake ones? {#30-howto--how-do-i-get-real-bold-and-italic-instead-of-fake-ones}

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, look at the [**Bold**](#s-c-styFaceBold), [**Italic**](#s-c-styFaceItalic) and **Bold Italic** buttons. A style in brackets, for example *(bold)*, is faked.
2. Click **Select Font...** for **Regular** and choose a family that has all four typefaces. **Pick a Font** shows these families in **bold**.
3. Or click **Select Font...** for **Bold** (or **Italic**) and choose a real bold (or italic) typeface from another family.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts).

### How do I print numbers in my own script's digits? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-numbers-in-my-own-script-s-digits}

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, click the [**Script for Numbers**](#s-lb-NumberScript) link.
2. In **Pick a Font**, choose your script in [**Digit mapping**](#s-fcb-fontdigits). Click **OK**, then print.
3. Check that the font has those digits. If not, you will see empty boxes.

See also: [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts).

### How do I print some text in colour (for example red verse numbers)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-some-text-in-colour-for-example-red-verse-numbers}

1. On the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab, find the marker, for example `v` (verse numbers) or `wj` (words of Jesus).
2. Click the button next to **Color** and choose a colour.
3. PTXprint ticks [**Enable Colored Text (as Specified in Stylesheet)**](#s-c-colorfonts) on the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab. Keep it ticked.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [Styles tab](#ch-12-styles); [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts).

## 4.5 Scripts, languages and hyphenation {#30-howto--scripts-languages-and-hyphenation}

### How do I set up a right-to-left script (for example Arabic or Hebrew)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-set-up-a-right-to-left-script-for-example-arabic-or-hebrew}

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, choose a font made for your script.
2. In **Writing System**, set [**Text Flow Direction**](#s-fcb-textDirection) to **Right-to-Left**. PTXprint ticks [**RTL Book Binding**](#s-c-RTLbookBinding).
3. Set [**Text Script**](#s-fcb-script), for example **Arabic** or **Hebrew**.
4. If the font needs Graphite, click **Select Font...** for **Regular**, tick [**Graphite Rendering**](#s-c-fontGraphite), and click **OK**.
5. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts).

### How do I set up a script that has no spaces between words (for example Thai or Khmer)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-set-up-a-script-that-has-no-spaces-between-words-for-example-thai-or-khmer}

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, set [**Text Script**](#s-fcb-script) to your script.
2. If your text marks word breaks with `/` (Thai, Lao, Myanmar, Tai Tham, New Tai Lue), nothing more is needed. The `/` marks become invisible break points.
3. Otherwise, tick [**Specify Line Break Locale**](#s-c-linebreakon) (Regular and Full views) and type the code, for example `th`, `km`, `my`, `zh`, `ja` or `ko`.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts).

### How do I turn on hyphenation? {#30-howto--how-do-i-turn-on-hyphenation}

1. In Paratext, approve the hyphenation points in the Wordlist tool.
2. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, in **Hyphenation**, click [**Create List...**](#s-btn-generateHyphenationList).
3. Click **OK** in the **Create List** dialog. The message says how many words were used.
4. Tick [**Hyphenate**](#s-c-hyphenate), and print.

If the list is empty, untick [**Only Use Approved Hyphenation Words**](#s-c-hyphenApprovedWords) in the dialog and try again.

See also: [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts).

### How do I choose a different form of a letter that my font offers? {#30-howto--how-do-i-choose-a-different-form-of-a-letter-that-my-font-offers}

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, click **Select Font...** for **Regular**, then [**Select Features...**](#s-btn-fontFeatures).
2. Choose your language in **Language** (if listed). Then tick or choose the feature.
3. Click **OK** in both dialogs, then print.

See also: [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts).

### How do I print an interlinear text (glosses under each word)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-an-interlinear-text-glosses-under-each-word}

1. In Paratext, approve the interlinear glosses.
2. Change to the **Full** view.
3. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Main** sub-tab, **General** area, tick **Interlinear** and type the language code of the glosses beside it, for example `en`.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [Advanced tab](#ch-13-advanced).

## 4.6 Making the text fit {#30-howto--making-the-text-fit}

### How do I make the book fit on fewer pages? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-the-book-fit-on-fewer-pages}

Try these one at a time. Print after each change and compare the page count.

1. [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab: make [**Base Font Size (pt)**](#s-s-fontsize) a little smaller (with [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) ticked).
2. **Layout** tab: make the margins a little smaller, or tick **Two Column Layout**.
3. [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, **Spacing Adjustments**: make [**Min/Shrink**](#s-s-minSpace) (Between Words) a little smaller.
4. [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab: untick [**Start Each Footnote on a New Line**](#s-c-fneachnewline). On the **Cross-References** sub-tab, choose [**Blend with Footnotes**](#s-r-xrpos-blend).
5. [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab: make large pictures smaller with **Scale**, or use **Column Width** instead of **Span Width**.
6. [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** sub-tab, **Page Layout and Spacing**: set [**Where to start a new book**](#s-fcb-bookstartpage) to **Same page**.
7. **PDF Preview** window: shrink paragraphs on short last pages (see "How do I fix a page that is not full?").

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout); [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts); [Notes+Refs tab](#ch-07-notes).

### How do I fit more text on each line? {#30-howto--how-do-i-fit-more-text-on-each-line}

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, in **Spacing Adjustments**, make [**Min/Shrink**](#s-s-minSpace) (Between Words) a little smaller.
2. Or click **Select Font...** for **Regular** and set [**Stretch**](#s-s-fontExtend) a little below 1.00, for example 0.97.
3. Print and check that the text is still easy to read.

See also: [Fonts+Script tab](#ch-05-fonts).

### How do I start each book on a right-hand page? {#30-howto--how-do-i-start-each-book-on-a-right-hand-page}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** sub-tab, open **Page Layout and Spacing**.
3. Set [**Where to start a new book**](#s-fcb-bookstartpage) to **Odd page**, and print. PTXprint adds blank pages where needed.

See also: [Advanced tab](#ch-13-advanced).

### How do I let a new book start on the same page as the end of the previous book? {#30-howto--how-do-i-let-a-new-book-start-on-the-same-page-as-the-end-of-the-previous-book}

1. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** sub-tab, open **Page Layout and Spacing**.
2. Set [**Where to start a new book**](#s-fcb-bookstartpage) to **Same page**.
3. If a book still starts on a new page, increase [**Page full factor**](#s-s-pagefullfactor) a little (for example from 0.65 to 0.75), and print.

See also: [Advanced tab](#ch-13-advanced).

## 4.7 Scripture text: headings, numbers and other content {#30-howto--scripture-text-headings-numbers-and-other-content}

### How do I remove (or add back) the section headings? {#30-howto--how-do-i-remove-or-add-back-the-section-headings}

On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, in [**Include Scripture Text**](#s-c-mainBodyText), untick (or tick) [**Headings**](#s-c-sectionHeads), and print. Unticking **Headings** also removes the parallel passage references.

See also: [Body tab](#ch-06-body).

### How do I hide the verse numbers or the chapter numbers? {#30-howto--how-do-i-hide-the-verse-numbers-or-the-chapter-numbers}

On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, untick [**Verse Numbers**](#s-c-verseNumbers) or [**Chapter numbers**](#s-c-chapterNumber), and print. The header references still work.

See also: [Body tab](#ch-06-body).

### How do I show verse number 1 at the start of each chapter? {#30-howto--how-do-i-show-verse-number-1-at-the-start-of-each-chapter}

On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, untick [**Hide First Verse Number**](#s-c-omitverseone) (Regular and Full views), and print.

See also: [Body tab](#ch-06-body).

### How do I leave out the book introductions? {#30-howto--how-do-i-leave-out-the-book-introductions}

1. On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, in **Beginning and Ending Material**, untick [**Book Introductions**](#s-c-bookIntro).
2. Also untick [**Introductory Outlines**](#s-c-introOutline) to remove the outline. Then print.

To print **only** the introductions, untick [**Include Scripture Text**](#s-c-mainBodyText) instead. Remember to tick it again later.

See also: [Body tab](#ch-06-body).

### How do I print a draft that has many untranslated verses? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-a-draft-that-has-many-untranslated-verses}

1. On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, in [**Include Scripture Text**](#s-c-mainBodyText), tick [**Hide Empty Verses**](#s-c-hideEmptyVerses).
2. Tick [**Show '...'**](#s-c-elipsizeMissingVerses) if readers should see where text is missing. Then print.

See also: [Body tab](#ch-06-body).

### How do I print "Psalm 1", "Psalm 2" … instead of big chapter numbers? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-psalm-1-psalm-2-instead-of-big-chapter-numbers}

1. Change to the **Full** view.
2. On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, in **Other Features**, tick [**Use Special Features for These Books**](#s-c-useChapterLabel).
3. Type `PSA` in the box beside it. (An empty box means **all** books.)
4. In [**Chapter Label**](#s-t-clHeading), type the word for "Psalm" in your language, and print.

For the books in this list you can also tick [**Optimize Layout for Poetry Books**](#s-c-optimizePoetryLayout). It lets the columns end at different heights, which often removes large white gaps in Psalms.

See also: [Body tab](#ch-06-body).

### How do I put the verse numbers in the margin? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-the-verse-numbers-in-the-margin}

1. On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, tick [**Marginal Verses**](#s-c-marginalverses).
2. In [**Position on Page**](#s-fcb-marginVrsPosn), choose **Left**, **Right**, **Inner** or **Outer**.
3. In [**Col Width (pts)**](#s-s-columnShift), type a width that fits the longest verse number, for example 12–16. Then print.

See also: [Body tab](#ch-06-body).

### How do I change how glossary words are marked in the text? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-how-glossary-words-are-marked-in-the-text}

1. On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, in **Other Features**, open [**Glossary Word Appearance**](#s-fcb-glossaryMarkupStyle).
2. Choose a style, for example **format as bold**, **star \*before word**, or **star \*before and after\*** for a star on both sides.
3. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [Body tab](#ch-06-body).

### How do I leave out one kind of text (for example remarks or a special marker)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-leave-out-one-kind-of-text-for-example-remarks-or-a-special-marker}

1. On the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab, find the marker in [**Find**](#s-t-styleSearch).
2. Untick [**Include Contents of Marker**](#s-c-styTextProperties). The marker is now shown with a line through it. Then print.

The text stays in Paratext. Only the PDF changes.

See also: [Styles tab](#ch-12-styles).

## 4.8 Footnotes and cross-references {#30-howto--footnotes-and-cross-references}

### How do I hide all footnotes? {#30-howto--how-do-i-hide-all-footnotes}

On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, **Footnotes** sub-tab, untick [**Include Footnotes**](#s-c-includeFootnotes), and print.

See also: [Notes+Refs tab](#ch-07-notes).

### How do I remove (or add back) the cross-references? {#30-howto--how-do-i-remove-or-add-back-the-cross-references}

1. On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, **Cross-References** sub-tab, untick (or tick) [**Include Cross-References (From Project Text)**](#s-c-includeXrefs).
2. To remove all cross-references, also untick [**Use External List of Cross-References**](#s-c-useXrefList) if it is ticked. Then print.

See also: [Notes+Refs tab](#ch-07-notes).

### How do I put the footnotes at the end of each book? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-the-footnotes-at-the-end-of-each-book}

On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, **Footnotes** sub-tab, under **Placement of Footnotes**, choose **End of Book**, and print. The notes appear after the last chapter of each book.

See also: [Notes+Refs tab](#ch-07-notes).

### How do I start each footnote on a new line? {#30-howto--how-do-i-start-each-footnote-on-a-new-line}

1. On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, **Footnotes** sub-tab, tick [**Start Each Footnote on a New Line**](#s-c-fneachnewline).
2. For cross-references, tick [**Start Each Cross-Reference on a New Line**](#s-c-xreachnewline) on the **Cross-References** sub-tab. Then print.

Notes on new lines use more space.

See also: [Notes+Refs tab](#ch-07-notes).

### How do I change the footnote callers (the small letters or symbols)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-the-footnote-callers-the-small-letters-or-symbols}

1. On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, **Footnotes** sub-tab, make sure **Show Callers** is ticked.
2. In the box beside it, type the marks separated by commas, with no spaces, for example `*,†,‡,§`.
3. If some notes still show other marks, tick [**Override hidden/automatic Footnote caller settings**](#s-c-fnOverride).
4. Tick **Reset Callers on Page** if the sequence should start again on each page.
5. Print. If the reset does not look right, print a second time.

See also: [Notes+Refs tab](#ch-07-notes).

### How do I save space by mixing cross-references with the footnotes? {#30-howto--how-do-i-save-space-by-mixing-cross-references-with-the-footnotes}

1. On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, **Cross-References** sub-tab, under [**Placement of Cross-References**](#07-notes--placement-of-cross-references), choose [**Blend with Footnotes**](#s-r-xrpos-blend).
2. Make sure [**Include Footnotes**](#s-c-includeFootnotes) is ticked on the **Footnotes** sub-tab, and print.

See also: [Notes+Refs tab](#ch-07-notes).

### How do I add a column of cross-references from a ready-made list? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-a-column-of-cross-references-from-a-ready-made-list}

1. Change to the **Full** view.
2. On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, **Cross-References** sub-tab, tick [**Use External List of Cross-References**](#s-c-useXrefList).
3. Under [**Placement of Cross-References**](#07-notes--placement-of-cross-references), choose [**Column Cross-References**](#s-r-xrpos-centre).
4. In **Source for References**, choose a list in [**External Refs**](#s-fcb-xRefExtListSource), for example **Standard list**.
5. In [**Include Refs for Books in**](#s-fcb-filterXrefs), choose which books the references may point to, for example [**New Testament**](#s-b-mbsNT). Then print.

See also: [Notes+Refs tab](#ch-07-notes).

### How do I put footnotes in the side margin, next to their verse? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-footnotes-in-the-side-margin-next-to-their-verse}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, tick [**Margin Notes Col Width (mm)**](#s-c-useMarginNotes) (Regular and Full views) and type the width of the margin column.
2. On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, set **Placement of Footnotes** (and/or [**Placement of Cross-References**](#07-notes--placement-of-cross-references)) to **Side Margin**. Then print.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout); [Notes+Refs tab](#ch-07-notes).

## 4.9 Pictures and maps {#30-howto--pictures-and-maps}

### How do I print the pictures that are in my Paratext text? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-the-pictures-that-are-in-my-paratext-text}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
