2. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, [**Global Options**](#s-lb-settings) sub-tab, tick [**Include Pictures (illustrations)**](#s-c-includeillustrations).
3. Click **Generate...**. If a dialog opens, choose [**Append Pictures to PicList From These Books**](#s-r-generate-selected), keep [**Protect existing PicList settings**](#s-c-protectPicList) ticked, and click **OK**.
4. Look for grey rows in the picture table. A grey row means PTXprint cannot find that picture file.
5. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures).

### How do I add a new picture from the illustration catalogue? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-a-new-picture-from-the-illustration-catalogue}

1. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, click [**Show Catalogue...**](#s-btn-getPictures). If you have no image set yet, download one first.
2. Choose the [**Image Set**](#s-ecb-artPictureSet). Type a word in [**Search**](#s-t-artSearch), or check [**Limit to Range of References**](#s-t-artRefRange), then click [**Search + Update Images**](#s-btn-imgRefresh).
3. Click the pictures you want, then [**Add Images to PicList**](#s-btn-imagePicker-ok).
4. On the **Details** sub-tab, type a **Caption** for each new picture and check its **Anchor Ref**. Then print.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures).

### How do I make a picture bigger or smaller? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-a-picture-bigger-or-smaller}

1. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, click the picture's row, then open the **Details** sub-tab.
2. Change **Frame Size** (**Column Width**, **Span Width**, **Page (in Margins)** or **Page (to Edge)**).
3. Change **Scale**. 100% is the full width of the frame. Then print.

Or, in the **PDF Preview** window, right-click the picture and choose **Shrink by 1 line** or **Grow by 1 line**. A red row in the table means the picture is too tall for the page: make **Scale** smaller.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures); [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview).

### How do I change where a picture sits on the page? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-where-a-picture-sits-on-the-page}

1. Select the picture in the table and open the **Details** sub-tab.
2. Set **Frame Size** first, then **Vertical Position** (for example **Top** or **Bottom**), then **Horizontal Position** (for example **Left**, **Right**, **Inner** or **Outer**). Then print.

Or, in the **PDF Preview** window, right-click the picture and choose **Vertical Position** or **Horizontal Position**.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures); [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview).

### How do I move a picture to an earlier or later page? {#30-howto--how-do-i-move-a-picture-to-an-earlier-or-later-page}

1. Select the picture and open the **Details** sub-tab.
2. Change **Anchor Ref** to a verse a few verses earlier (to move it back) or later (to move it forward). Keep the dot: `LUK 2.7`. Then print.

Or right-click the picture in the **PDF Preview** window and choose **Change Anchor Ref**.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures); [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview).

### How do I make the text flow around a small picture? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-the-text-flow-around-a-small-picture}

1. Select the picture. On the **Details** sub-tab, set **Frame Size** to **Column Width**.
2. Set **Vertical Position** to **Cutout** and **Horizontal Position** to **Left** or **Right** (or **Inner**/**Outer**).
3. Set **Scale** to about 40%.
4. Set **Number of Lines** to the line where the picture should start (0 = first line of the paragraph). Then print.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures).

### How do I use high-quality pictures for the final PDF? {#30-howto--how-do-i-use-high-quality-pictures-for-the-final-pdf}

1. Put the high-resolution files in the project's `local\figures` folder, or tick [**Use Other Location**](#s-c-useCustomFolder) and click [**Picture Folder...**](#s-btn-selectFigureFolder) to choose their folder.
2. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, [**Global Options**](#s-lb-settings), choose [**High Resolution (Larger File)**](#s-r-pictureRes-High).
3. Print and check that the missing-pictures count is 0.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures).

### How do I make a small PDF to send by email? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-a-small-pdf-to-send-by-email}

1. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, [**Global Options**](#s-lb-settings), choose [**Low Resolution (Smaller File)**](#s-r-pictureRes-Low). For an even smaller file, choose [**Use Place-holders (Smallest PDF File)**](#s-c-figplaceholders): each picture becomes an empty box.
2. On the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab, make sure [**PDF Output Format**](#s-fcb-outputFormat) is **Screen (Quickest)**. Then print.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures); [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

### How do I add maps? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-maps}

1. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, click **Add Maps...** (or on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick [**Include Maps**](#s-c-inclMaps) and click **Add Maps...**).
2. Check [**Book Code for Maps**](#s-fcb-ptxMapBook) (usually **XXM**).
3. Click [**Select Map...**](#s-btn-selectMap) and choose the map file. Type a **Caption** if you want one.
4. Click **Size and Position...** to choose the frame size and position.
5. Click [**Add Another Map**](#s-btn-mapAddAnother) for the next map, or [**OK - Done!**](#s-btn-addMap) to finish. Then print.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures); [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals).

### How do I print the copyright credits for the pictures? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-the-copyright-credits-for-the-pictures}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick [**Colophon at End of Publication**](#s-c-colophon). Its text normally contains `\zimagecopyrights`. If not, add the line `\pc \zimagecopyrights` (or put it on the copyright page of the front matter).
3. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, **Details** sub-tab, check each picture. Known illustration series show **Automatic**. For other pictures, type the credit in [**Copyright Attribution**](#s-t-plCopyright).
4. Print twice. The first run finds the page of each picture.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures); [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals); [View+Edit tab](#ch-14-viewedit).

### How do I print a small credit line on top of a picture? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-a-small-credit-line-on-top-of-a-picture}

1. Select the picture on the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab and open the **Details** sub-tab.
2. Click **© ...**. The **Illustration Credit Overlay** dialog opens.
3. Type the [**Image Credit Text**](#s-t-plCreditText), choose the position, click **OK**, and print.

See also: [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures).

## 4.10 Diglot (two texts side by side) {#30-howto--diglot-two-texts-side-by-side}

### How do I make a diglot (two languages side by side)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-a-diglot-two-languages-side-by-side}

1. Make sure both projects print well on their own.
2. Open the primary project. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click **Save As** and give the diglot its own configuration name, for example `Diglot`.
3. On the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab (Regular and Full views), tick [**Diglot (or Polyglot)**](#s-c-diglot). Click **Yes** in the message.
4. In the [**R**](#32-glossary--r) row of the table, choose the second **Project**, then its **Configuration**.
5. Check that the **% Width** values add up to 100 (for example 50 and 50).
6. Choose one short book that is in both projects, and print.

See also: [Diglot tab](#ch-10-diglot).

### How do I change the column widths in a diglot? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-the-column-widths-in-a-diglot}

1. On the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab, click the **% Width** cell of each text and type a new value, for example 55 and 45. The numbers must add up to 100.
2. Print and compare the number of pages. Give more width to the text that needs more space.
3. Or select one short book and click **Auto-calculate optimum widths of diglot columns** (diglots with exactly two texts). It prints many times, so it takes a while.

See also: [Diglot tab](#ch-10-diglot).

### How do I change the font of the second text in a diglot? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-the-font-of-the-second-text-in-a-diglot}

1. On the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab, right-click the [**R**](#32-glossary--r) row and choose **Edit Settings…**.
2. The window now shows the second text's configuration. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, change the font.
3. Click **Return to Primary** (the big button at the bottom), then print.

To change only the font size or line spacing, type it in the **Font Size** or **Spacing** cell of that row on the **Diglot** tab.

See also: [Diglot tab](#ch-10-diglot).

### How do I print the captions of both texts under a shared picture? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-the-captions-of-both-texts-under-a-shared-picture}

1. On the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab, tick [**Captions**](#s-c-pic-Captions) in the row of the secondary text. (The [**L**](#32-glossary--l) text always shows its captions.)
2. Make sure both texts use the same picture file at the same verse. Only then is the picture shared.
3. Print.

Pictures are not shared in the books listed in [**Use Serial Layout for These Books**](#s-t-diglotSerialBooks).

See also: [Diglot tab](#ch-10-diglot).

### How do I put the two texts on facing pages? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-the-two-texts-on-facing-pages}

1. On the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab, in the [**R**](#32-glossary--r) row, change **1|2** to **2**.
2. Check that the **Layout** box shows **L,R**.
3. Set **% Width** to 100 for each text, and print.

See also: [Diglot tab](#ch-10-diglot).

### How do I add a third text (polyglot)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-a-third-text-polyglot}

1. On the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab, right-click in the table and choose **Add a row/text**.
2. Choose the **Project** and **Configuration** for the new row.
3. Right-click a row and choose **Distribute Widths**, then print.

See also: [Diglot tab](#ch-10-diglot).

### How do I turn a diglot back into a normal (one text) configuration? {#30-howto--how-do-i-turn-a-diglot-back-into-a-normal-one-text-configuration}

1. On the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab, untick [**Diglot (or Polyglot)**](#s-c-diglot). The [**Save As Monoglot**](#10-diglot--save-as-monoglot) dialog opens.
2. Type a new configuration name (no spaces) and click **OK**.
3. PTXprint opens the new one-text configuration. The diglot configuration is still there.

See also: [Diglot tab](#ch-10-diglot).

## 4.11 Thumb tabs, borders and decorations {#30-howto--thumb-tabs-borders-and-decorations}

### How do I add thumb tabs? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-thumb-tabs}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, select all the books of the publication.
2. On the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab (Regular and Full views), tick [**Thumb Tabs**](#s-c-thumbtabs).
3. Set [**Height**](#s-s-thumbheight) and **Length** (for example 8 mm and 15 mm), and choose a dark [**Tab Color**](#s-col-thumbback).
4. Click [**Edit Style**](#s-lb-style-toc3) and set a light text colour, for example white. Then print.

See also: [Tabs+Borders tab](#ch-11-tabsborders).

### How do I put a decorative border around the text? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-a-decorative-border-around-the-text}

1. On the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab, tick [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments), then **Border**.
2. Choose **Dynamic Border**.
3. Click the [**\textborder**](#s-lb-style-textborder) link. The [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab opens with the `textborder` style.
4. In **Sidebar Settings**, click [**Borders...**](#s-btn-sbBorders). Choose the [**Type of Border**](#s-fcb-sbBorderStyle), the colours and the **Border Width** (at least 10 pt for ornaments). Click **OK**.
5. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, make the margins larger if the border is too close to the text or the paper edge. Then print.

For a ready-made frame, choose **PDF border (Legacy)** in step 2 and click **Select...** to choose the PDF.

See also: [Tabs+Borders tab](#ch-11-tabsborders); [Styles tab](#ch-12-styles).

### How do I add a decoration at the end of each book? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-a-decoration-at-the-end-of-each-book}

On the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab, tick [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments), then [**End of Book Decoration**](#s-c-inclEndOfBook). Click **Select...**, choose a PDF graphic, and print.

See also: [Tabs+Borders tab](#ch-11-tabsborders).

### How do I put a border around book titles or section headings? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-a-border-around-book-titles-or-section-headings}

1. On the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab, tick [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments).
2. Tick [**Book Title Borders**](#s-c-inclTitleBorders), or tick [**Section Headings**](#s-c-inclSectionHeader) and choose **Dynamic Border**.
3. Click the style link next to it. The [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab opens.
4. Choose a background colour, and click [**Borders...**](#s-btn-sbBorders) in **Sidebar Settings** for the border. Then print.

With **PDF border (Legacy)** for section headings, **Shift** moves the graphic: a positive number moves it up.

See also: [Tabs+Borders tab](#ch-11-tabsborders).

### How do I decorate the verse numbers? {#30-howto--how-do-i-decorate-the-verse-numbers}

1. On the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab, tick [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments), then [**Verse Number Decorator**](#s-c-inclVerseDecorator).
2. Choose [**Verse Border Graphic**](#s-r-decorator-file) and click **Select...** to choose a small PDF graphic. (For Arabic script you can choose [**End of Ayah**](#s-r-decorator-ayah).)
3. Print. Change **Scale** and **Shift** if the number does not fit.

See also: [Tabs+Borders tab](#ch-11-tabsborders).

## 4.12 Front matter, back matter and covers {#30-howto--front-matter-back-matter-and-covers}

### How do I add a title page, copyright page and table of contents? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-a-title-page-copyright-page-and-table-of-contents}

1. On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick [**Local Front Matter**](#s-c-frontmatter). If there is no front matter yet, PTXprint makes a **BASIC** one: a title page, a copyright and licence page, and a table of contents.
2. In the **Variables and Values** table, type the values, for example **maintitle** and **subtitle**.
3. Print twice. The table of contents needs two runs.

See also: [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals); [View+Edit tab](#ch-14-viewedit).

### How do I start the front matter from a different template? {#30-howto--how-do-i-start-the-front-matter-from-a-different-template}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab, click the **Front Matter** sub-tab.
3. Click **Generate**. Choose **BASIC**, **ADVANCED**, [**DIGLOT**](#s-lb-Diglot) or **PARATEXT** (a copy of the FRT book in Paratext), and click **OK**.
4. Click [**Edit Variables...**](#s-btn-editZvars), fill in the values, and print.

**Warning:** **Generate** replaces all of the current front matter. If you have already changed it, click **Cancel**.

See also: [View+Edit tab](#ch-14-viewedit).

### How do I change the text of the title page? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-the-text-of-the-title-page}

1. On the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab, click the **Front Matter** sub-tab.
2. If the line says `\mt1 \zvar|maintitle\*`, the title comes from a variable. Click [**Edit Variables...**](#s-btn-editZvars) and change **maintitle**.
3. If the line has normal text, change it in the editor.
4. Click outside the text area to save, then print.

See also: [View+Edit tab](#ch-14-viewedit); [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals).

### How do I set the copyright and licence text? {#30-howto--how-do-i-set-the-copyright-and-licence-text}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click **Copyright & Licensing** to open it.
3. Type the copyright text (type `(c)` for ©), or click **Reload copyright from Paratext project**.
4. Choose or type the [**License**](#s-ecb-licenseText).
5. Make sure the front matter or the colophon contains `\zcopyright` and `\zlicense` (the BASIC template has them). Then print.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic); [View+Edit tab](#ch-14-viewedit).

### How do I turn on the table of contents? {#30-howto--how-do-i-turn-on-the-table-of-contents}

1. On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick **Table of Contents** and type the heading in the **Title** box beside it.
2. Choose which book names to show (`\toc1`, `\toc2`, `\toc3`) and the [**Leaders**](#s-fcb-leaderStyle) (the dots between the name and the page number) (Regular and Full views).
3. Make sure the front matter contains `\ztoc|main\*` (the BASIC template has it).
4. Print twice.

See also: [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals); [View+Edit tab](#ch-14-viewedit).

### How do I add a colophon at the end of the book? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-a-colophon-at-the-end-of-the-book}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick [**Colophon at End of Publication**](#s-c-colophon).
3. Change the text in the colophon box if needed. The button beside it reloads the default text.
4. Tick [**Force Page Break Before Colophon**](#s-c-standAloneColophon) if it must start on a new page. Then print.

When you tick [**Local Front Matter**](#s-c-frontmatter) or [**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate), PTXprint unticks the colophon. Check it again afterwards.

See also: [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals).

### How do I add an existing PDF at the front or the back of the book? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-an-existing-pdf-at-the-front-or-the-back-of-the-book}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick [**Front Matter PDF(s)**](#s-c-inclFrontMatter) (or [**Back Matter PDF(s)**](#s-c-inclBackMatter)).
3. Click **Select...** beside it and choose one or more PDF files. Then print.

Several files are added in alphabetical order of their file names. Name them `01-title.pdf`, `02-preface.pdf` and so on to control the order. Make the PDF pages the same size as your book pages.

See also: [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals).

### How do I make a cover? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-a-cover}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick [**Local Front Matter**](#s-c-frontmatter) (a cover needs it), then tick [**Create Cover Page**](#s-c-makeCoverPage).
3. Click [**Cover Wizard...**](#s-btn-coverGenerate). If the message **Existing cover settings found** appears, click **Delete and Continue** to start a new cover, or **Cancel (keep my settings)** to keep the old cover (the wizard then does not open).
4. Go through the steps: book and spine, picture, background, front cover text, spine text, back cover. Click **Finish** on the **Review** step.
5. Print. The cover is a separate PDF whose name ends with **\_cover**. It is shown on the [**Cover**](#15-peripherals--cover) tab of the **PDF Preview** window.

**Finish** replaces the cover sections of the front matter, and puts the title, subtitle, language name and ISBN into the variables table. PTXprint keeps your wizard answers, so you can open the wizard again later to change the cover. To fine-tune colours, borders or pictures, click [**Front Cover**](#s-lb-style-cat-coverfront-esb), [**Spine**](#s-lb-style-cat-coverspine-esb), [**Back Cover**](#s-lb-style-cat-coverback-esb) or [**Cover Spread**](#s-lb-style-cat-coverwhole-esb) on the **Peripherals** tab.

The spine must be as wide as the book is thick. The wizard can work it out from the page count and paper, and the [**Printers**](#ch-18-printers) tab (Full view) gives an estimate. Ask your printer for the exact spine width.

See also: [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals); [Printers tab](#ch-18-printers).

## 4.13 Headers, footers and page numbers {#30-howto--headers-footers-and-page-numbers}

### How do I put the page number in the outer corner and the references in the centre? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-the-page-number-in-the-outer-corner-and-the-references-in-the-centre}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, in **Page Setup**, tick [**Mirror Pages**](#s-c-mirrorpages).
2. On the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab, set [**Outer (Right)**](#s-ecb-hdrright) to **Page Number**, **Center** to **Reference Range**, and [**Inner (Left)**](#s-ecb-hdrleft) to **-empty-**.
3. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [Header+Footer tab](#ch-08-headfoot).

### How do I mirror the headers for double-sided printing? {#30-howto--how-do-i-mirror-the-headers-for-double-sided-printing}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, in **Page Setup**, tick [**Mirror Pages**](#s-c-mirrorpages).
2. On the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab, use [**Inner (Left)**](#s-ecb-hdrleft) for the spine side and [**Outer (Right)**](#s-ecb-hdrright) for the page-edge side. Then print.

With **Mirror Pages** ticked, the inner and outer items change sides on left-hand pages, and **First Reference** and **Last Reference** are swapped there.

See also: [Header+Footer tab](#ch-08-headfoot); [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout).

### How do I show verse numbers in the header references? {#30-howto--how-do-i-show-verse-numbers-in-the-header-references}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab, under **Include in References**, make sure [**Chapter**](#s-c-rangeShowChapter) is ticked.
3. Tick [**Verse**](#s-c-rangeShowVerse), choose [**Colon (ch:vs)**](#s-r-CVsep-colon) or [**Period (ch.vs)**](#s-r-CVsep-period), and print.

See also: [Header+Footer tab](#ch-08-headfoot).

### How do I put the page number at the bottom of the page? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-the-page-number-at-the-bottom-of-the-page}

1. On the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab, set **Center Footer** to **Page Number**.
2. Set the header place that had **Page Number** to **-empty-**, and print.

See also: [Header+Footer tab](#ch-08-headfoot).

### How do I add "DRAFT" and the date (or time) to every page? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-draft-and-the-date-or-time-to-every-page}

1. On the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab, open **Center Footer** (or a header place).
2. Choose **Printed on YYYY-MM-DD**, **Date (YYYY-MM-DD)**, **Time (HH:MM)**, or **Date and Time** (useful when you print several drafts on one day).
3. Or type your own text, for example `DRAFT\ \isodate`. Type `\ ` (a backslash and a space) for each space.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**. The date and time are those of printing.

For a large "DRAFT" across each page, use a watermark (see "How do I put DRAFT across every page?").

See also: [Header+Footer tab](#ch-08-headfoot).

### How do I start the page numbers at a given number? {#30-howto--how-do-i-start-the-page-numbers-at-a-given-number}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab, in **Other**, set [**Starting Page Number (for Scripture Books)**](#s-s-startPageNum), for example to 101, and print.

In the front matter you can also use `\resetpagenums` (advanced; see the View+Edit chapter).

See also: [Header+Footer tab](#ch-08-headfoot); [View+Edit tab](#ch-14-viewedit).

### How do I print a page number on the first page of each book? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-a-page-number-on-the-first-page-of-each-book}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab, in **Other**, tick [**Print Page Number at Bottom of Intro Page(s)**](#s-c-pageNumTitlePage), and print.

PTXprint never prints a header on the first page of a book. This setting puts the page number in its footer.

See also: [Header+Footer tab](#ch-08-headfoot).

### How do I put a line under the header? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-a-line-under-the-header}

On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, in **Margins**, tick [**Horizontal Rule**](#s-c-rhrule), set [**Space between Rule and Top of Text (pt)**](#s-s-rhruleposition), and print.

See also: [Layout tab](#ch-04-layout).

## 4.14 Fixing the page layout {#30-howto--fixing-the-page-layout}

### How do I fix a page that is not full (too much white space at the bottom)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-fix-a-page-that-is-not-full-too-much-white-space-at-the-bottom}

1. Print. The **PDF Preview** window opens.
2. Go to the page. Or tick [**Layout Analysis**](#s-c-layoutAnalysis) on the **Content** tab, click **Locate...**, tick [**Underfilled Pages**](#s-c-findUnbalanced), and click **Locate the next issue**.
3. Find a paragraph on this page or the page before whose last line is very short.
4. Right-click it and choose **Try Shrink -1 line** (or **Shift + left-click** it). This pulls text up from the next page.
5. Wait a few seconds for the update (if [**Auto-update**](#s-c-updatePDF) is ticked), or click **Print (Update PDF)**.
6. If nothing changed, try **Shrink Both**, or another paragraph.

Do this last, when all other layout settings are final. Work from the front of the book to the back.

See also: [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview).

### How do I fix a page that is too full (make text go to the next page)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-fix-a-page-that-is-too-full-make-text-go-to-the-next-page}

1. In the **PDF Preview** window, find a paragraph on that page whose last line is nearly full.
2. Right-click it and choose **Expand +1 line** (or **Shift + right-click** it).
3. Wait for the update, then check this page and the following pages.

See also: [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview).

### How do I fill all pages automatically? {#30-howto--how-do-i-fill-all-pages-automatically}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, choose the books to fill, and print once.
2. In the **PDF Preview** window, click the lightning icon (**Show/hide Page Fill tool with progress monitor**) (Regular and Full views).
3. Click **Start Fill** for a fresh start, or **Resume Fill** to keep the existing adjustments. **Start Fill** removes your earlier adjustments for these books.
4. Wait. This can take from minutes to hours.
5. When it has finished, use **Locate the next issue** to find pages that could not be filled, and fix them by hand.

The tool also works for a diglot or polyglot (experimental). It then also tries to keep the columns at the same height. [**The cost of imbalance in a polyglot slice**](#s-s-pbpolyimbalance) ([**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab › **Other** › **Automatic Page Filler**) sets how important that is. Check the result carefully.

See also: [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview); [Diglot tab](#ch-10-diglot).

### How do I undo paragraph adjustments? {#30-howto--how-do-i-undo-paragraph-adjustments}

1. In the **PDF Preview** window, right-click the paragraph.
2. Choose **Reset Adjustments**, then **Paragraph**, **Column**, **Page**, [**Spread**](#s-c-mapSpread) or **End of Book**.
3. Or, on the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab, [**Adj List**](#s-l-AdjList) sub-tab, choose the book, select the rows and press **Delete**.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

See also: [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview); [View+Edit tab](#ch-14-viewedit).

### How do I work quickly on pages in the middle of a long book? {#30-howto--how-do-i-work-quickly-on-pages-in-the-middle-of-a-long-book}

1. In the **PDF Preview** window, go to the page.
2. Right-click a `\p` or `\m` paragraph at the top of the page and choose **SpeedSlice** (not available for diglots).
3. Type the first word on the page in [**First Word on This Page**](#s-t-sliceWord), and set **Length of Slice** (for example 3 chapters).
4. Click [**Enable**](#s-btn-slice-ok). Now each print makes only this part of the book.
5. When you have finished, open **SpeedSlice** again and click [**Disable**](#s-btn-slice-cancel). Then print the whole book.

Always disable SpeedSlice before you make the final PDF.

See also: [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview).

### How do I find spacing problems, letters that touch, or missing characters? {#30-howto--how-do-i-find-spacing-problems-letters-that-touch-or-missing-characters}

1. In the **PDF Preview** window, on the **Content** tab, tick [**Layout Analysis**](#s-c-layoutAnalysis).
2. Look at the coloured marks: red = letters that touch, purple = missing characters, yellow = rivers of white space, light blue-green = wide spaces.
3. Click **Locate...** and tick the kinds of issue you want. Use the arrow buttons to go from page to page.

See also: [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview).

### How do I see two facing pages together? {#30-howto--how-do-i-see-two-facing-pages-together}

In the **PDF Preview** window, tick [**Book View**](#s-c-bkView) (or press **Ctrl+B**).

See also: [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview).

## 4.15 Preparing the PDF for a printer {#30-howto--preparing-the-pdf-for-a-printer}

### How do I make a print-ready PDF for a commercial printer (PDF/X, CMYK)? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-a-print-ready-pdf-for-a-commercial-printer-pdf-x-cmyk}

1. Ask the printer for their requirements: trim size, colour (CMYK, grey or RGB), PDF type (PDF/X-1a or PDF/X-4), crop marks and bleed.
2. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, check that [**Page Size**](#s-ecb-pagesize) is the trim size.
3. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, choose [**High Resolution (Larger File)**](#s-r-pictureRes-High).
4. On the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab, in **PDF Details**, set [**PDF Output Format**](#s-fcb-outputFormat). For PDF/X-1a in CMYK, choose **Print-CMYK**. For PDF/X-4, choose **Digital-CMYK (Transparency)** or **Digital-RGB**.
5. Tick [**Crop Marks**](#s-c-cropmarks) only if the printer asks for them.
6. Make sure [**Pages Per Spread**](#s-fcb-pagesPerSpread) is **1-up (No booklet)**.
7. Print. The PDF name ends with the format, for example **\_CMYK**.

See also: [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

### How do I make a black-and-white PDF for printing? {#30-howto--how-do-i-make-a-black-and-white-pdf-for-printing}

On the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab, set [**PDF Output Format**](#s-fcb-outputFormat) to **Print-Gray (B/W)**, and print. The file name ends with **\_BW**.

See also: [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

### How do I add crop marks? {#30-howto--how-do-i-add-crop-marks}

On the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab, in **PDF Details**, tick [**Crop Marks**](#s-c-cropmarks), and print.

Each PDF page becomes 0.5 inch (about 12.7 mm) larger on every side, to make room for the marks. Many print-on-demand printers do not want crop marks.

See also: [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

### How do I set the bleed for the cover? {#30-howto--how-do-i-set-the-bleed-for-the-cover}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view.
2. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** sub-tab, open **PDF Options, Covers, Show/Hide**.
3. Set [**Cover Bleed (mm)**](#s-s-bleed) to the value your printer asks for (often 3–5 mm), and print.

See also: [Advanced tab](#ch-13-advanced); [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

### How do I print an A5 booklet on A4 paper? {#30-howto--how-do-i-print-an-a5-booklet-on-a4-paper}

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, set [**Page Size**](#s-ecb-pagesize) to A5.
2. On the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab, in **Booklet Pagination**, set [**Pages Per Spread**](#s-fcb-pagesPerSpread) to **2-up**.
3. Set [**Physical Paper Size**](#s-ecb-sheetSize) to **210mm, 297mm (A4)**.
4. Print. The new PDF ends with **\_2up**.
5. Print it double-sided ("flip on short edge"). Fold the sheets in the middle and staple.

Commercial printers want single pages (**1-up**), not a booklet.

See also: [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

### How do I put "DRAFT" across every page? {#30-howto--how-do-i-put-draft-across-every-page}

1. On the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab, in **PDF Details**, tick [**Apply Watermark PDF**](#s-c-applyWatermark).
2. Click **Select...** and choose a watermark that matches your page size, for example **A5-Draft.pdf**. Then print.

See also: [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

### How do I see what changed since the last PDF? {#30-howto--how-do-i-see-what-changed-since-the-last-pdf}

1. On the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab, tick [**Compare PDFs**](#s-c-createDiff) (or press **Ctrl+R**). PTXprint now always keeps the previous PDF (**\_1.pdf**), even if [**Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept**](#s-s-keepVersions) is 0.
2. Make your corrections, then print.
3. If there are differences, the **Diff** tab of the **PDF Preview** window shows them in colour: added text in the [**New Text**](#s-l-ndiffNew) colour (blue at first), removed text in the [**Old Text**](#s-l-ndiffOld) colour (red at first). Otherwise the status line says why, for example **No differences found**.
4. Untick **Compare PDFs** when you have finished. It makes printing slower.

See also: [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

### How do I compare with an older proof, or ignore changes in the margins or headers? {#30-howto--how-do-i-compare-with-an-older-proof-or-ignore-changes-in-the-margins-or-headers}

1. To compare with an older PDF (not the last run), click **Select...** in the [**Compare PDFs**](#s-c-createDiff) area and choose it. To go back to the last run, click **Select...** and then **Cancel**.
2. Change to the **Full** view for these options:
   * [**Start Page Offset**](#s-s-diffOffset) – when one PDF has extra pages at the start (for example a cover). A positive number skips pages of the **old** PDF, a negative number skips pages of the **new** PDF.
   * **Ignore When Comparing: Headers + Footers** or [**Side Margins**](#s-c-diffIgnoreSides) – those areas are not compared (shaded grey in the diff PDF). Not used with booklets (more than 1-up) or [**Scale to fit**](#s-c-scaleToFit).
   * [**Smart Check**](#s-c-diffSmart) – after you changed only the margins or gutter, it lines up each old page with the new one and shows only real changes (words, line breaks).
3. Tick **Compare PDFs** and print.

Both PDFs must have the same page size.

See also: [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

### How do I get a price estimate for printing? {#30-howto--how-do-i-get-a-price-estimate-for-printing}

1. Make the PDF of the whole book first, so that the page count is right.
2. Change to the **Full** view and open the [**Printers**](#ch-18-printers) tab.
3. Check **Pages** and [**Trim size**](#18-printers--trim-size). Type the number of [**Copies**](#s-s-prn-copies), and choose [**Interior**](#s-fcb-prn-interior), [**Binding**](#s-fcb-prn-binding) and [**Currency**](#s-fcb-prn-currency).
4. Read the **Est. per copy** column. These are estimates only. Always ask the printer for a real quotation.

See also: [Printers tab](#ch-18-printers).

## 4.16 Configurations and settings {#30-howto--configurations-and-settings}

### How do I save my settings as a new configuration? {#30-howto--how-do-i-save-my-settings-as-a-new-configuration}

1. Click **Save** first, so the new configuration starts from your latest settings.
2. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, in **Layout Configuration**, click the **Save As** button (the icon next to **Name**).
3. Type a name, for example `NT_A5`. Use only letters, numbers, `(`, `)`, `_` and `-`. No spaces.
4. Click **OK**. PTXprint changes to the new configuration. The old one stays as it was.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I replace an existing configuration with my current settings? {#30-howto--how-do-i-replace-an-existing-configuration-with-my-current-settings}

1. Click **Save**, then click the **Save As** button on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.
2. Type the name of the configuration to replace, and tick [**Replace it if it already exists**](#s-c-overwriteConfig).
3. Click **OK**. PTXprint deletes the old configuration and saves the current settings in its place. This cannot be undone.

The **Default** configuration can never be replaced. The box is unticked each time the dialog opens.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I change to another configuration without losing my changes? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-to-another-configuration-without-losing-my-changes}

1. Click **Save** (or **Print (Make PDF)**, which also saves).
2. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, choose the other configuration in **Name**.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic); [Main window](#ch-02-main-window).

### How do I copy a configuration to other projects? {#30-howto--how-do-i-copy-a-configuration-to-other-projects}

1. Choose the configuration (not **Default** – it is never copied) and click **Save**.
2. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click **Copy configuration to other projects** (Regular and Full views).
3. Click the target project(s).
4. Choose [**Do NOT Replace Existing Config**](#s-r-copyConfig-noReplace) (the safe choice the first time).
5. Leave [**Keep each project's own language-specific variables**](#s-c-copyConfig-skipVars) ticked, so each project keeps its own titles and language name. Click **OK**.
6. Choose the target project in **Project** and check the copied configuration.

Adjust lists (paragraph adjustments) are not copied.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I get back the settings that were used to make a PDF? {#30-howto--how-do-i-get-back-the-settings-that-were-used-to-make-a-pdf}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click **Import Settings...**.
2. Click [**PDF file (with embedded settings) or ZIP archive file**](#s-r-impSource-pdf), then **Select...**, and choose the PDF.
3. Under **Target**, choose [**A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration**](#s-r-impTarget-prjcfg) and type a new configuration name, for example `FromPDF`. PTXprint ticks [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything) for a new name.
4. Click **OK**.

This only works if the PDF was made with [**Include Config Settings Within PDF**](#s-c-inclSettingsInPDF) ticked on the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab.

See also: [Importing settings](#ch-20-import); [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

### How do I import settings from a ZIP archive? {#30-howto--how-do-i-import-settings-from-a-zip-archive}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click **Import Settings...**.
2. Click [**PDF file (with embedded settings) or ZIP archive file**](#s-r-impSource-pdf), then **Select...**, and choose the ZIP file.
3. Choose the **Target** configuration. A new name is safest.
4. Tick [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything), or only the groups you want (into an existing configuration). Click **OK**.

See also: [Importing settings](#ch-20-import).

### How do I copy only some settings (for example only the pictures or the headers) from another configuration? {#30-howto--how-do-i-copy-only-some-settings-for-example-only-the-pictures-or-the-headers-from-another-configuration}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click **Import Settings...**.
2. Click [**A Previously Saved Configuration**](#s-r-impSource-config) and choose the source **Project** and **Configuration**.
3. Choose an **existing** target configuration. (For a new name PTXprint always imports everything.)
4. Change to the **Regular** view if needed, and untick [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything).
5. Tick only the group you want, for example **Pictures**, or **Other** and then [**Header+Footer settings**](#s-c-oth-HeaderFooter) on the **Other** tab. Click **OK**.

There is no Undo. If you are not sure, first try it on a copy made with **Save As**.

See also: [Importing settings](#ch-20-import).

### How do I lock a configuration so nobody changes it? {#30-howto--how-do-i-lock-a-configuration-so-nobody-changes-it}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, choose the configuration in **Name** (not **Default** – it cannot be locked).
2. Click the **lock** button, type a password (it cannot be empty), and click **OK**. Remember the password.

To unlock, click the lock button again and type the same password. **Cancel** never locks or unlocks.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I protect a finished layout from accidental changes? {#30-howto--how-do-i-protect-a-finished-layout-from-accidental-changes}

1. Change to the **Full** view.
2. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Main** sub-tab, **General** area, tick [**Lock UI Layout Settings**](#s-c-lockUI4Layout). Most **Layout**, **Fonts+Script** and **Styles** settings are now greyed out.
3. Also tick [**Lock XeTeX Layout Level**](#s-c-lockXeTeXLayout) if future PTXprint versions must give exactly the same layout.
4. Untick these boxes when you need to change the layout again.

See also: [Advanced tab](#ch-13-advanced).

### How do I delete a configuration I do not need? {#30-howto--how-do-i-delete-a-configuration-i-do-not-need}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, choose the configuration in **Name**.
2. Click **Delete**. Check that the message names the right configuration, then click **Yes**.
3. PTXprint changes to **Default** and deletes the settings and working files of the old configuration. This cannot be undone.

The PDFs you made from it stay in the output folder. Other configurations are not touched.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic).

### How do I go back to the PTXprint default settings? {#30-howto--how-do-i-go-back-to-the-ptxprint-default-settings}

* **Default** configuration: choose **Default** in **Name** and click [**Reset**](#20-import--reset) (Regular and Full views; it replaces **Delete**). PTXprint does not ask first. It also removes the files of **Default**, such as its styles and picture list.
* Another configuration: click **Import Settings...** and then **RESET**. Style settings are not reset. Click **Save** if you want to keep the result.

See also: [Basic tab](#ch-03-basic); [Importing settings](#ch-20-import).

## 4.17 Finding settings and getting help {#30-howto--finding-settings-and-getting-help}

### How do I find a setting that I cannot see? {#30-howto--how-do-i-find-a-setting-that-i-cannot-see}

1. Click in the **Search for settings** box at the bottom-left (or press **Ctrl+F**).
2. Type a word, for example `margin` or `footnote`, and press **Enter**.
3. Click the setting in the list. PTXprint opens the right tab, highlights the setting, and raises the view level if needed.

See also: [Main window](#ch-02-main-window).

### How do I see more (or fewer) settings? {#30-howto--how-do-i-see-more-or-fewer-settings}

Click **≡** (top-left) › [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) › **Mini View**, **Basic View**, **Regular View** or **Full View**.

Hidden settings still work and still change the PDF.

See also: [Main window](#ch-02-main-window).

### How do I send my project to the support team? {#30-howto--how-do-i-send-my-project-to-the-support-team}

1. Choose the project, configuration and only the book(s) that show the problem.
2. If the problem is not about pictures, untick [**Include Pictures (illustrations)**](#s-c-includeillustrations) on the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab to make the file smaller.
3. On the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab, click [**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra).
4. Choose where to save the ZIP file and click **Save**. PTXprint prints again and then makes the ZIP file.
5. Email it to **ptxprint_support@sil.org** with a description of the problem, your PTXprint version (from **About**) and screenshots.

The archive contains the text of your project. If the text is sensitive, ask your project leader first.

See also: [Help tab](#ch-21-help).

### How do I check the last PDF for warnings and errors? {#30-howto--how-do-i-check-the-last-pdf-for-warnings-and-errors}

1. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.
2. On the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab, click [**Create Report...**](#s-btn-generateReport) (or **Show Report Information** in the **PDF Preview** window).
3. The report opens in your web browser. Read the warnings and errors.

See also: [Help tab](#ch-21-help); [PDF Preview window](#ch-19-preview).

### How do I change the language of PTXprint's menus? {#30-howto--how-do-i-change-the-language-of-ptxprint-s-menus}

Click **≡** › **Language** and choose a language. PTXprint saves the configuration and opens again in the new language, with the same project and configuration.

See also: [Main window](#ch-02-main-window).

### How do I use projects from another Paratext folder? {#30-howto--how-do-i-use-projects-from-another-paratext-folder}

1. On the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab, click [**Change...**](#s-btn-changeProjectsDir) next to [**Base Projects Directory**](#s-l-projects-dir).
2. Choose a folder that PTXprint found, or click **Browse for a different folder…**. Choose the folder that *contains* the project folders.
3. Click **Use Selected**, then choose a project on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.

See also: [Help tab](#ch-21-help).

### How do I free up disk space? {#30-howto--how-do-i-free-up-disk-space}

On the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab, click [**Tidy Up**](#s-btn-deleteTempFiles). PTXprint deletes temporary working folders. Your settings and PDF files are kept.

See also: [Help tab](#ch-21-help).

# 5. Problems and solutions {#ch-31-troubleshooting}

## 5.1 How to use this chapter {#31-troubleshooting--how-to-use-this-chapter}

This chapter lists common problems, grouped by kind, in the words users often use. Each has **Why this happens** and **What to do**.

First try these three quick checks. They solve many problems:

1. **Print again.** Most changes appear in the PDF only after you click **Print (Make PDF)**.
2. **Check the view level.** A setting can be hidden but still turned on. Click **≡** › [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) › **Full View** to see every setting.
3. **Check the configuration name.** Look at **Name** on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab. Is it the configuration you think it is?

"pt" means point. 1 pt is about 0.35 mm.

## 5.2 Printing fails or no PDF appears {#31-troubleshooting--printing-fails-or-no-pdf-appears}

### Nothing happens when I click Print, or the status line says "No books to print" {#31-troubleshooting--nothing-happens-when-i-click-print-or-the-status-line-says-no-books-to-print}

**Why this happens:** No book is selected, or the book list is empty.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, in **What to Print**, click [**Single Book**](#s-r-book-single) and choose a book. Or click [**Select Multiple Books...**](#s-btn-chooseBooks), choose books and click **OK**.
2. Print again.

### The status line says "One or more fonts have not been set yet" {#31-troubleshooting--the-status-line-says-one-or-more-fonts-have-not-been-set-yet}

**Why this happens:** No font has been chosen for the main text.

**What to do:** On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, click **Select Font...** next to **Regular**, choose a font, and print.

### The status line says "Printing busy" {#31-troubleshooting--the-status-line-says-printing-busy}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint is still making a PDF.

**What to do:** Wait until the progress bar has finished, then print again.

### PTXprint says "Cannot update PDF file while it is locked!" {#31-troubleshooting--ptxprint-says-cannot-update-pdf-file-while-it-is-locked}

**Why this happens:** The old PDF is open in another program (for example Adobe Reader), so PTXprint cannot replace it.

**What to do:**

1. Close the PDF in the other program and click **Yes** to try again.
2. To avoid this, click **≡** › [**Show PDF**](#s-btn-menu-showPDF) › **Preview Pane**. The preview does not lock the file.

### The Print (Make PDF) and Save buttons are greyed out {#31-troubleshooting--the-print-make-pdf-and-save-buttons-are-greyed-out}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint cannot print yet. For example, no project is selected, or a diglot row has no project or configuration.

**What to do:**

1. Read the message in the status line above the bottom bar.
2. Choose a project on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.
3. For a diglot, check that every row on the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab has a **Project** and a **Configuration**.

### An error window says "Failed to create: … .pdf" {#31-troubleshooting--an-error-window-says-failed-to-create-pdf}

**Why this happens:** The typesetting program stopped because of an error. The window shows the last lines of the log and often a hint. The hint is the most useful part (see the table below).

**What to do:**

1. Find the hint in the table below and follow the advice.
2. Note any "References to check" or "File(s) to check" at the end of the message. They tell you where to look.
3. If you changed a setting just before the error, change it back and print again.
4. For more detail, open the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab, **XeTeX Log** sub-tab, and scroll to the end. Error lines start with `!`.
5. If you still cannot fix it, click [**Tidy Up**](#s-btn-deleteTempFiles) on the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab and print again. If that does not help, send an archive ([**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra) on the **Help** tab) to support.

| Hint in the error window | What it usually means | What to do in PTXprint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Cannot find the Font specified. Install it, restart PTXprint and try again" | A font in the configuration (on **Fonts+Script**, or in a style) is not installed. The message may name the marker that uses it. | Install the font for all users and restart PTXprint. Or choose an installed font on **Fonts+Script**, or in the named style on the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab. |
| "Fallback Font issue - set a font on the Fonts+Scripts tab" | [**Use Fallback Font**](#s-c-useFallbackFont) is ticked, but no valid fallback font is chosen. | On **Fonts+Script**, choose a fallback font, or untick **Use Fallback Font**. |
| "Fallback font probably being applied to text in a footnote (not permitted!)" | A character that needs the fallback font is in a footnote. | Choose a Regular font that has the character, or remove it from the fallback character list. |
| "Check if picture file is located in 'Figures', 'local\figures' or a specified folder" | A picture file cannot be found or loaded. | On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, look for grey rows and fix the file name or folder. Or tick [**Omit Missing Pictures**](#s-c-skipmissingimages). |
| "Check if image/PDF file is available on the system" | A front or back matter PDF, a watermark PDF or a picture is missing. | Check [**Front Matter PDF(s)**](#s-c-inclFrontMatter) and [**Back Matter PDF(s)**](#s-c-inclBackMatter) ([**Peripherals**](#s-lb-Peripherals)) and [**Apply Watermark PDF**](#s-c-applyWatermark) ([**Finishing**](#s-lb-Finishing)). Choose the file again with **Select...**, or untick the option. |
| "This might be related to a USFM marker error (using an unsupported marker)" | A marker in the text is wrong or unknown, or a line in a mods file is wrong. | Run **Basic Checks** in Paratext. If you edited `ptxprint-mods.tex` ([**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab), untick [**Apply Customized Settings (ptxprint-mods.tex)**](#s-c-useModsTex) and print again. |
| "Failed due to an error in the generated USFM file. Run the Basic Checks in Paratext" | The text has a marker error that PTXprint cannot process. | Run **Basic Checks** in Paratext and fix the errors. If you use a changes file (**Advanced** tab), check the last rule you added. |
| "Uh oh! You've pushed TeX too far! Try turning Hyphenation off" | The job is too big, often because of a very long hyphenation list. | On **Fonts+Script**, untick [**Hyphenate**](#s-c-hyphenate), or make a shorter list with [**Limit Hyphenation List to Words Found in**](#s-c-hyphenLimitBooks). Print fewer books at once. |
| "Possible fault in the hyphenation file" | The hyphenation list has a bad entry. | Untick **Hyphenate** on **Fonts+Script**. Click [**Create List...**](#s-btn-generateHyphenationList) to make the list again. |
| "You may have too many paragraphed footnotes on the page" | Too many run-on footnotes on one page. | On [**Notes+Refs**](#s-lb-NotesRefs), tick [**Start Each Footnote on a New Line**](#s-c-fneachnewline). |
| "Possibly a missing +/- value in the Adjust List" or "Check for errors in the Adjust List" | A row in the paragraph adjustment list has a wrong value. | On [**View+Edit**](#s-lb-Viewer), [**Adj List**](#s-l-AdjList) sub-tab, check the [**Stretch**](#s-s-fontExtend) column. Each value must start with `+` or `-`. Delete the bad row if you are not sure. |
| "One of the settings in the Stylesheet may be missing the units" | A value in a style or an extra stylesheet is not valid. | Undo your last change on the **Styles** tab. On the **Advanced** tab, untick extra stylesheets (**custom.sty**, **ptxprint-mods.sty**) one at a time to find the problem. |
| "Font size setting issue. Check to see if the font size in a style … is incorrect (maybe it is set to 0.00)" | A style near the reference in the message has font size 0. | On the **Styles** tab, set that style's [**Font Size Factor**](#s-s-styFontSize) to a normal value, or click its Reset button. |
| "Expecting a number for \Color definition, not a color name" | A colour in a style was written as a word. | On the **Styles** tab, choose the colour again with the **Color** button. |
| "Problem with Formatting Intro Outline" | The right-aligned outline references cause a problem. | On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, untick [**Right-align \ior With Tabbed Leaders**](#s-c-prettyIntroOutline). |
| "Sorry! XeTeX was unable to complete the typesetting" | The typesetter could not place the text on a page. Common in diglots, or when a forgotten feature is on. | For a diglot, first print each text on its own. Check tabs with blue names (for example [**Pictures**](#31-troubleshooting--pictures), [**Diglot**](#31-troubleshooting--diglot), [**Tabs+Borders**](#s-lb-TabsBorders)) and turn off features you do not need. Look for very large pictures. |
| "To fix this error: Use a different font which is not a Variable Font" | The font is a "variable font", which PTXprint cannot use. | Choose a normal font on **Fonts+Script**. |
| "Bad xdvi file, probably failed to load a picture or font" | A picture or font could not be loaded when the PDF was written. | Check missing pictures on **Pictures** and the fonts on **Fonts+Script**. |
| "Possibly a faulty installation" | Files that come with PTXprint are missing. | Install PTXprint again. |
| "Oops! Something unexpected happened…" or "Probably a TeX macro problem" | PTXprint does not recognise the error. | Click **Tidy Up** (**Help** tab) and print again. If it still fails, send an archive to support and say which setting you changed last. |

### The status line says "Rerun to fix: …" {#31-troubleshooting--the-status-line-says-rerun-to-fix}

**Why this happens:** Some things depend on page numbers (the table of contents, picture credits, margin notes), and PTXprint learned new page numbers during this run. Most common with [**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun) ticked.

**What to do:** Untick **Quick Run** at the bottom of the window, and print again.

### PTXprint says "Unknown book code" {#31-troubleshooting--ptxprint-says-unknown-book-code}

**Why this happens:** The book list has a word that is not a 3-letter USFM book code, for example `John` instead of `JHN`.

**What to do:** On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, correct [**Portions or Multiple Books**](#s-r-book-multiple) with codes such as `MAT`, `JHN`, `1CO`. Or click [**Select Multiple Books...**](#s-btn-chooseBooks) and click the books.

### Printing takes a very long time {#31-troubleshooting--printing-takes-a-very-long-time}

**Why this happens:** Some settings need much extra work: a [**PDF Output Format**](#s-fcb-outputFormat) other than **Screen**, [**Compare PDFs**](#s-c-createDiff), Strong's numbers in the text, very large cross-reference lists, many high-resolution pictures, or a whole Bible.

**What to do:**

1. While you work, tick [**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun) at the bottom of the window.
2. On the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab, use **Screen (Quickest)** until the final PDF. Untick **Compare PDFs** when you do not need it.
3. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, choose [**Low Resolution (Smaller File)**](#s-r-pictureRes-Low) or **Use Place-holders** while you work.
4. Print one book at a time, or use **SpeedSlice** in the **PDF Preview** window for long books.

## 5.3 The PDF does not change {#31-troubleshooting--the-pdf-does-not-change}

### I changed a setting, but the PDF looks the same {#31-troubleshooting--i-changed-a-setting-but-the-pdf-looks-the-same}

**Why this happens:**

* You did not print again, or the last print failed. The preview still shows the old PDF.
* The PDF is shown in another program that has not reloaded it.
* Another setting overrides yours (for example a style, or an extra stylesheet).
* You changed a different configuration, or the secondary text of a diglot.
* [**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate) is ticked, so PTXprint did not process the text again.

**What to do:**

1. Print and wait for it to finish. The date and time in the title bar of the **PDF Preview** window must be the time of your last print.
2. If an error message appeared, fix that first. The old PDF stays on the screen when printing fails.
3. Check **Name** on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.
4. For a diglot, see ["My change has no effect in a diglot"](#31-troubleshooting--my-change-has-no-effect-in-a-diglot) below.
5. Untick **Layout Only** and [**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun), and print again.
6. For style and font changes, see ["My change on the Styles tab has no effect"](#31-troubleshooting--my-change-on-the-styles-tab-has-no-effect) below.

### My text changes in Paratext do not appear in the PDF {#31-troubleshooting--my-text-changes-in-paratext-do-not-appear-in-the-pdf}

**Why this happens:** Normally PTXprint notices that the text changed. With [**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate) ticked, it may not process the text again. Picture captions come from PTXprint's own picture list.

**What to do:**

1. Save the text in Paratext.
2. Untick **Layout Only** and print.
3. For picture captions, click [**Refresh List**](#s-btn-refreshCaptions) on the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab.
4. If you use **SpeedSlice**, make sure it is not hiding the part that you changed.

### My changes are not kept after I close PTXprint, or Save does nothing {#31-troubleshooting--my-changes-are-not-kept-after-i-close-ptxprint-or-save-does-nothing}

**Why this happens:** **Quit** does not save. Or the configuration is locked. A locked configuration is never saved, not even when you print.

**What to do:**

1. Click **Save** (or **Print (Make PDF)**) before **Quit**.
2. If **Save**, **Delete** and **Notes** are greyed out, the configuration is locked. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click the lock button and type the password.
3. Or click **Save As** and make a new, unlocked configuration.

### The PDF has only a few chapters, or it starts in the middle of a book {#31-troubleshooting--the-pdf-has-only-a-few-chapters-or-it-starts-in-the-middle-of-a-book}

**Why this happens:** **SpeedSlice** is still on. Or [**From Chapter**](#s-t-chapfrom) and **To** limit the chapters.

**What to do:**

1. In the **PDF Preview** window, right-click a `\p` or `\m` paragraph, choose **SpeedSlice** and click [**Disable**](#s-btn-slice-cancel).
2. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, check **From Chapter** and **To**, and print again.

## 5.4 Text and fonts {#31-troubleshooting--text-and-fonts}

### Some letters print as empty boxes (☐) or question marks {#31-troubleshooting--some-letters-print-as-empty-boxes-or-question-marks}

**Why this happens:** The font has no shape for these characters.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, tick [**Use Fallback Font**](#s-c-useFallbackFont) (Regular and Full views).
2. Click [**Find Missing Characters**](#s-btn-findMissingChars) to see which characters are missing.
3. Click **Select Font...** next to the list and choose a font that has them.
4. Or choose a **Regular** font that supports your whole alphabet.
5. If only numbers are boxes, check [**Digit mapping**](#s-fcb-fontdigits) in the **Pick a Font** dialog. Set it to **Default** if the font has no digits for that script.
6. In the **PDF Preview** window, tick [**Layout Analysis**](#s-c-layoutAnalysis). Purple marks show missing characters.

### Bold or italic text looks fake (thick, blurred or slanted wrongly) {#31-troubleshooting--bold-or-italic-text-looks-fake-thick-blurred-or-slanted-wrongly}

**Why this happens:** The font family has no real bold or italic typeface, so PTXprint makes one from the regular letters. The button on the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab shows the style in brackets, for example *(bold)*.

**What to do:**

1. On the **Fonts+Script** tab, click **Select Font...** for **Regular** and choose a family shown in [**bold**](#s-c-styFaceBold) in the list. These families have all four typefaces.
2. Or click **Select Font...** for **Bold** or [**Italic**](#s-c-styFaceItalic) and choose a real bold or italic font.
3. Or, in **Pick a Font**, change [**Embolden**](#s-s-fontBold) and [**Slant**](#s-s-fontItalic) to improve the fake style.

### Some text is in the wrong font {#31-troubleshooting--some-text-is-in-the-wrong-font}

**Why this happens:** The style for that text has its own font, or the characters come from the fallback font. In a diglot, the header can use the font of the other text.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab, find the marker. A bold **Font** label means the style has its own font. Click the bold label to go back to the main font.
2. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, check [**Use Fallback Font**](#s-c-useFallbackFont) and the characters in its list.
3. In a diglot or polyglot, on the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab, choose the text letter ([**L**](#32-glossary--l), [**R**](#32-glossary--r), [**A**](#32-glossary--a) …) in the drop-down in front of each part of the header.
4. If you chose a new **Regular** font, check [**Bold**](#s-c-styFaceBold), [**Italic**](#s-c-styFaceItalic) and **Bold Italic** again.

### My font is not in the list {#31-troubleshooting--my-font-is-not-in-the-list}

**Why this happens:** The font is not installed, or only for one user, or PTXprint has not refreshed its list.

**What to do:**

1. Install the font for all users.
2. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, click **Refresh Font List**.
3. If it is still missing, restart PTXprint.

### Letters do not join, or vowel marks are in the wrong place {#31-troubleshooting--letters-do-not-join-or-vowel-marks-are-in-the-wrong-place}

**Why this happens:** [**Text Script**](#s-fcb-script) is wrong, or the font needs Graphite.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, set **Text Script** to your script.
2. For a Graphite font, click **Select Font...** for **Regular**, tick [**Graphite Rendering**](#s-c-fontGraphite), and click **OK**. Then print.

### Hyphenation does not work {#31-troubleshooting--hyphenation-does-not-work}

**Why this happens:** There is no hyphenation list, the list is empty, [**Hyphenate**](#s-c-hyphenate) is not ticked, or [**Between Letters**](#s-c-letterSpacing) spacing is on.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, click [**Create List...**](#s-btn-generateHyphenationList) and read the message. It says how many words were used.
2. If the number is 0, untick [**Only Use Approved Hyphenation Words**](#s-c-hyphenApprovedWords) and click **OK** again, or approve words in the Paratext Wordlist.
3. Tick **Hyphenate**. Make sure **Between Letters** in **Spacing Adjustments** is unticked. Then print.

### Long lines do not break in Thai, Khmer, Myanmar, Chinese or similar scripts {#31-troubleshooting--long-lines-do-not-break-in-thai-khmer-myanmar-chinese-or-similar-scripts}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint does not know where it may break a line.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, set [**Text Script**](#s-fcb-script) to your script.
2. Tick [**Specify Line Break Locale**](#s-c-linebreakon) and type the language code, for example `th`, `km`, `my` or `zh`.
3. Or mark the break points with `/` in the text (Thai, Lao, Myanmar, Tai Tham, New Tai Lue).

### Coloured text prints in black {#31-troubleshooting--coloured-text-prints-in-black}

**Why this happens:** [**Enable Colored Text (as Specified in Stylesheet)**](#s-c-colorfonts) is not ticked, or [**PDF Output Format**](#s-fcb-outputFormat) is **Print-Gray (B/W)**.

**What to do:** Tick **Enable Colored Text (as Specified in Stylesheet)** on the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, and check **PDF Output Format** on the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab.

### My change on the Styles tab has no effect {#31-troubleshooting--my-change-on-the-styles-tab-has-no-effect}

**Why this happens:** You changed a different marker or level (for example `s1` instead of `s2`). Or another style or stylesheet wins. Or a setting on another tab controls it.

**What to do:**

1. Check which marker the text really uses. On the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab, click the filter button next to [**Find**](#s-t-styleSearch) to show only markers used in your books.
2. `\p` gets its size and line spacing from the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab (**Base Font Size** and **Base Line Spacing**).
3. If you chose **Justified** but the text is ragged, tick [**Justify Paragraphs**](#s-c-justify) on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab.
4. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, check [**Apply Stylesheet Overrides (ptxprint-mods.sty)**](#s-c-useModsSty). It is applied last and may set the same value.
5. Print again.

### Some text is missing from the PDF {#31-troubleshooting--some-text-is-missing-from-the-pdf}

**Why this happens:** A setting removes it. For example [**Include Contents of Marker**](#s-c-styTextProperties) is unticked for its style, or a [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab setting removes headings, introductions or empty verses.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab, a marker with a line through it is not printed. Tick **Include Contents of Marker**.
2. On the **Body** tab, check [**Book Introductions**](#s-c-bookIntro), [**Introductory Outlines**](#s-c-introOutline), [**Include Scripture Text**](#s-c-mainBodyText), [**Headings**](#s-c-sectionHeads), [**Parallel Passage Refs**](#s-c-parallelRefs) and [**Hide Empty Verses**](#s-c-hideEmptyVerses).
3. For study notes, tick [**Extended Footnotes (\ef)**](#s-c-extendedFnotes) on the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab (Full view).

## 5.5 Layout and spacing {#31-troubleshooting--layout-and-spacing}

### There is white space at the bottom of every page {#31-troubleshooting--there-is-white-space-at-the-bottom-of-every-page}

**Why this happens:** The text area does not hold a whole number of lines. The left-over part of a line is empty on every page.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, look at [**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) (Regular and Full views). If it is red, this is the cause.
2. Click **one** fine-tune button: next to [**Base Line Spacing (pt)**](#s-s-linespacing), or next to the top or bottom margin.
3. The number turns blue. Print again.

### Some pages or columns end early, with empty lines at the bottom {#31-troubleshooting--some-pages-or-columns-end-early-with-empty-lines-at-the-bottom}

**Why this happens:** With [**Align Text to Baseline**](#s-c-noGrid), all lines sit on a fixed grid. The typesetter will not leave one line of a paragraph alone at the top or bottom of a page, keeps a heading with the next lines, and keeps pictures and notes with their verse. So a page sometimes ends one or more lines early.

**What to do:**

1. Do this last, when all other settings are final.
2. In the **PDF Preview** window, right-click a paragraph on this page or the page before and choose **Try Shrink -1 line** to pull text up. Or choose **Expand +1 line** on the page before to push a line down.
3. Or use the **Auto Page Fill** tool (the lightning icon in the **PDF Preview** window).
4. If a picture is near the gap, move it or make it smaller.
5. In poetry books such as Psalms, try [**Optimize Layout for Poetry Books**](#s-c-optimizePoetryLayout) on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab (see "Optimize Layout for Poetry Books has no effect").
6. For a quick draft, move the switch on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab to **Variable Line Spacing**. This fills the columns, but the lines no longer line up on both sides of the paper.

### The last page of a book has only a few lines {#31-troubleshooting--the-last-page-of-a-book-has-only-a-few-lines}

**Why this happens:** The book is just a little too long to end on the page before.

**What to do:**

1. In the **PDF Preview** window, find paragraphs in the last few pages whose last line is short.
2. Right-click each one and choose **Try Shrink -1 line** (or **Shrink Both**) until the lines move back. Or use the **Auto Page Fill** tool.
3. If many lines must move, make a small change for the whole book (for example a slightly smaller **Base Font Size**, or [**Min/Shrink**](#s-s-minSpace) in **Spacing Adjustments** on **Fonts+Script**). Then check all pages again.
4. To let the next book start on the same page, set [**Where to start a new book**](#s-fcb-bookstartpage) to **Same page** ([**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** sub-tab, **Page Layout and Spacing**).

### I asked to shrink a paragraph, but nothing changed {#31-troubleshooting--i-asked-to-shrink-a-paragraph-but-nothing-changed}

**Why this happens:** The paragraph has no room to lose a line (common for short paragraphs, or when the last line is almost full). Or the PDF has not been updated yet.

**What to do:**

1. Wait a few seconds if [**Auto-update**](#s-c-updatePDF) is ticked, or click **Print (Update PDF)**.
2. Right-click again and choose **Shrink Both**.
3. Or try a longer paragraph on the same page, or on the page before.

### Fixing one page broke a later page {#31-troubleshooting--fixing-one-page-broke-a-later-page}

**Why this happens:** Every change moves all the text after it.

**What to do:**

1. Make all other layout changes (fonts, margins, pictures) **before** you adjust paragraphs.
2. Work from the front of the book to the back. Fix the first problem page, then use **Locate the next issue** in the **PDF Preview** window.

### Text looks squashed, stretched or has big gaps between words {#31-troubleshooting--text-looks-squashed-stretched-or-has-big-gaps-between-words}

**Why this happens:** Paragraph adjustments or the page filler made the letters narrower or wider. Or the word spacing range is too wide. Or [**Keep Repeated Words Together**](#s-c-glueredupwords) or [**Prevent Orphan Words**](#s-c-preventorphans) forces bad line breaks.

**What to do:**

1. In the **PDF Preview** window, tick [**Adjustments**](#s-c-pdfadjoverlay) to see changed paragraphs (coloured bars). Reset the worst ones (right-click › **Reset Adjustments** › **Paragraph**).
2. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** sub-tab, **Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings**, raise **Minimum Text Shrink** (for example to 97%) and lower **Maximum Text Expand** (for example to 103%).
3. On the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab, check [**Between Words**](#s-c-spacing) in **Spacing Adjustments**. A very high [**Max/Stretch**](#s-s-maxSpace) allows big gaps.
4. Turn on hyphenation to give the lines more break points.

### Almost everything on the Layout, Fonts+Script and Styles tabs is greyed out {#31-troubleshooting--almost-everything-on-the-layout-fonts-script-and-styles-tabs-is-greyed-out}

**Why this happens:** [**Lock UI Layout Settings**](#s-c-lockUI4Layout) is ticked.

**What to do:** Change to the **Full** view. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Main** sub-tab, **General** area, untick **Lock UI Layout Settings**.

### The font size changed when I changed the line spacing (or the other way round) {#31-troubleshooting--the-font-size-changed-when-i-changed-the-line-spacing-or-the-other-way-round}

**Why this happens:** [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) is ticked on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab. It keeps the two numbers in the same proportion.

**What to do:** Untick **Lock Ratio**, then type the font size and line spacing you want.

### The header or footer is cut off, or too close to the edge of the paper {#31-troubleshooting--the-header-or-footer-is-cut-off-or-too-close-to-the-edge-of-the-paper}

**Why this happens:** The header and footer sit inside the top and bottom margins. A large gap between the header and the text moves the header towards the edge.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, look at the blue numbers in the margin picture.
2. Make [**Start of Page to Top of Text (mm)**](#s-s-topmargin) (or [**Bottom of Text to End of Page (mm)**](#s-s-bottommargin)) larger.
3. Or make [**Bottom of Header to Top of Text (pt)**](#s-s-headerposition) (or [**Bottom of Text to Top of Footer (pt)**](#s-s-footerposition)) smaller.

### My PDF suddenly looks different, but I did not change anything on the main tabs {#31-troubleshooting--my-pdf-suddenly-looks-different-but-i-did-not-change-anything-on-the-main-tabs}

**Why this happens:** An [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab setting may have changed, or an extra file (changes file, mods file) may be on. Someone on the team may have changed the configuration through Paratext Send/Receive.

**What to do:**

1. On the **Advanced** tab, **Other** sub-tab, click the filter button. Only groups with changed settings are shown, with [**bold**](#s-c-styFaceBold) labels.
2. On the **Main** sub-tab, check which boxes are ticked in [**Text Processing & Stylesheets**](#13-advanced--text-processing-stylesheets).
3. Check the **Notes** box on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab for comments from the team.

### Coloured marks, bars or codes appear in the margins of my PDF {#31-troubleshooting--coloured-marks-bars-or-codes-appear-in-the-margins-of-my-pdf}

**Why this happens:** A proof-reading option is on.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** sub-tab, **PDF Options, Covers, Show/Hide**, untick the "show" options (for example [**Show adjust points**](#s-c-showadjpoints), [**Show USFM codes**](#s-c-showusfmcodes), [**Show Error Bars For Overfull Lines**](#s-c-showhboxerrorbars), [**Mark Trigger Points**](#s-c-mktrigpts)).
2. In the [**Diglot**](#31-troubleshooting--diglot) group, untick [**Show Diglot Trace Marks**](#s-c-vistrace).

The coloured bars and boxes in the **PDF Preview** window ([**Adjustments**](#s-c-pdfadjoverlay), [**Paragraph Boxes**](#s-c-pdfparabounds), [**Layout Analysis**](#s-c-layoutAnalysis)) are only on the screen, not in the PDF.

### "Optimize Layout for Poetry Books" has no effect {#31-troubleshooting--optimize-layout-for-poetry-books-has-no-effect}

**Why this happens:** It only works for the books listed beside [**Use Special Features for These Books**](#s-c-useChapterLabel) on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, while that box is ticked. With an empty list, nothing is optimized.

**What to do:** Change to the **Full** view. Tick **Use Special Features for These Books** and type the book codes (for example `PSA PRO`) in its list.

## 5.6 Pictures {#31-troubleshooting--pictures}

### No pictures appear in the PDF {#31-troubleshooting--no-pictures-appear-in-the-pdf}

**Why this happens:** Pictures are off, or the picture list (PicList) is empty, or place-holders are used.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, [**Global Options**](#s-lb-settings), tick [**Include Pictures (illustrations)**](#s-c-includeillustrations).
2. Change to the **Regular** view to see the picture table. If it is empty, click **Generate...**. PTXprint uses only the pictures in its list, not the `\fig` lines in Paratext directly.
3. Make sure [**Use Place-holders (Smallest PDF File)**](#s-c-figplaceholders) is not chosen.
4. On the **Details** sub-tab, check that **Print** is ticked under **Media**.

### Some pictures are missing {#31-troubleshooting--some-pictures-are-missing}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint cannot find the picture file (grey row in the table), or the picture's book is not being printed, or [**Image Types**](#s-t-imageTypeOrder) excludes the file type.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, look for grey rows and check the [**Filename**](#s-t-plFilename).
2. Put the file in the project's `figures` or `local\figures` folder, or tick [**Use Other Location**](#s-c-useCustomFolder) and choose the folder with [**Picture Folder...**](#s-btn-selectFigureFolder). If the file is in a subfolder, make sure [**Exclude Subfolders**](#s-c-exclusiveFiguresFolder) is unticked.
3. Clear the **Image Types** box if it only lists some types.
4. After printing, check the missing-pictures count and list on [**Global Options**](#s-lb-settings). [**Omit Missing Pictures**](#s-c-skipmissingimages) skips missing files without an error, so it can hide the problem.

### A picture is on the wrong page or in the wrong place {#31-troubleshooting--a-picture-is-on-the-wrong-page-or-in-the-wrong-place}

**Why this happens:** A picture goes on the page of its anchor verse only if there is room. Otherwise it moves to a later page. Large pictures move more often.

**What to do:**

1. In the **PDF Preview** window, right-click the picture, choose **Change Anchor Ref**, and choose a verse a little earlier (or later).
2. Or right-click and choose another **Vertical Position** or **Horizontal Position**.
3. Make the picture smaller with **Shrink by 1 line**, or with **Scale** on the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, **Details** sub-tab. Then print.

### A picture row is red in the table {#31-troubleshooting--a-picture-row-is-red-in-the-table}

**Why this happens:** At this size and scale the picture is too tall for the page.

**What to do:** On the **Details** sub-tab, make **Scale** smaller, or change **Frame Size** from **Span Width** to **Column Width**.

### I cannot choose the picture position I want {#31-troubleshooting--i-cannot-choose-the-picture-position-i-want}

**Why this happens:** The position lists depend on each other. For example, **Span Width** only allows **Top**, **Bottom** and **Below Notes**, and no horizontal position.

**What to do:** Choose **Frame Size** first, then **Vertical Position**, then **Horizontal Position**.

### My caption changes in Paratext do not show {#31-troubleshooting--my-caption-changes-in-paratext-do-not-show}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint keeps its own copy of the captions in the picture list.

**What to do:** On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, click [**Refresh List**](#s-btn-refreshCaptions) (size and position settings stay the same), and print.

### The picture credits are missing or wrong {#31-troubleshooting--the-picture-credits-are-missing-or-wrong}

**Why this happens:** The colophon or front matter has no `\zimagecopyrights`, or a picture is not from a known illustration series, or the page numbers are not yet known.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick [**Colophon at End of Publication**](#s-c-colophon) and check that its text contains `\zimagecopyrights`. Or put `\pc \zimagecopyrights` in the front matter.
2. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, **Details** sub-tab, type the credit in [**Copyright Attribution**](#s-t-plCopyright) for pictures that do not show **Automatic**.
3. Print twice.

### My picture checks, credits or notes are gone {#31-troubleshooting--my-picture-checks-credits-or-notes-are-gone}
