**Why this happens:** In older PTXprint versions, the [**Checklist**](#s-lb-checklist) answers, credits and picture notes were not read back when a configuration was opened. Saving could then overwrite them. This is fixed now, but answers lost before the fix cannot be recovered.

**What to do:** On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, **Checklist** sub-tab (and [**Copyright Attribution**](#s-t-plCopyright) on **Details**), enter the lost answers again. They are now kept.

### The message "Image Anchor Not Found" appears when I right-click a picture {#31-troubleshooting--the-message-image-anchor-not-found-appears-when-i-right-click-a-picture}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint cannot match the picture in the PDF to a row in the picture list, for example after the list changed.

**What to do:** Print again so the preview matches the picture list. Then make the change on the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, **Details** sub-tab.

## 5.7 Notes and cross-references {#31-troubleshooting--notes-and-cross-references}

### Footnote or cross-reference settings are greyed out {#31-troubleshooting--footnote-or-cross-reference-settings-are-greyed-out}

**Why this happens:** Most settings need another setting first.

**What to do:**

1. Tick [**Include Footnotes**](#s-c-includeFootnotes) on the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, **Footnotes** sub-tab.
2. For the caller box, tick **Show Callers**.
3. **End of Column** needs **Two Column Layout** on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.
4. **Side Margin** needs [**Margin Notes Col Width (mm)**](#s-c-useMarginNotes) on the **Layout** tab.
5. The **Source for References** settings need [**Use External List of Cross-References**](#s-c-useXrefList) (Full view).

### The callers in the PDF are not the ones I typed {#31-troubleshooting--the-callers-in-the-pdf-are-not-the-ones-i-typed}

**Why this happens:** Each note in Paratext can ask for no caller (`\f -`) or a fixed caller. PTXprint obeys that.

**What to do:** On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, tick [**Override hidden/automatic Footnote caller settings**](#s-c-fnOverride) (or the cross-reference version), and print.

### The cross-reference placement changed by itself {#31-troubleshooting--the-cross-reference-placement-changed-by-itself}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint keeps the footnote and cross-reference placements in step. For example, **End of Column** for one changes the other too.

**What to do:** After you change one placement, check both the **Footnotes** and the **Cross-References** sub-tabs.

### Changing the cross-reference rule settings does nothing {#31-troubleshooting--changing-the-cross-reference-rule-settings-does-nothing}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint draws only one rule above the notes at the bottom of the page. It uses the footnote rule settings, unless the footnotes are at the **End of Book**.

**What to do:** Change the rule on the **Footnotes** sub-tab instead.

### The footnotes run into the footer {#31-troubleshooting--the-footnotes-run-into-the-footer}

**What to do:** On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, **Footnotes** sub-tab, make **Space Above Rule** larger. Or, on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, make [**Bottom of Text to Top of Footer (pt)**](#s-s-footerposition) larger.

### Margin notes do not appear {#31-troubleshooting--margin-notes-do-not-appear}

**Why this happens:** [**Margin Notes Col Width (mm)**](#s-c-useMarginNotes) on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab only makes the space. The notes must also be sent there.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, set **Placement of Footnotes** (and/or [**Placement of Cross-References**](#07-notes--placement-of-cross-references)) to **Side Margin**.
2. For headings in the margin, tick [**In Margin**](#s-c-headingInMargin) on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab.

### The external cross-references show the wrong book names {#31-troubleshooting--the-external-cross-references-show-the-wrong-book-names}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint uses the short book names from the Paratext project's **Scripture Reference Settings** (these should match the `\toc3` lines).

**What to do:** Correct the book names in Paratext, and print again.

## 5.8 Diglot {#31-troubleshooting--diglot}

### My change has no effect in a diglot {#31-troubleshooting--my-change-has-no-effect-in-a-diglot}

**Why this happens:** Each text has its own configuration. The second text's fonts, font size, styles and notes come from its own (secondary) configuration. Page settings (page size, margins, header and footer positions, the footnote rule and others) always come from the primary configuration.

**What to do:**

1. For the second text's fonts, styles or notes: on the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab, right-click its row and choose **Edit Settings…**. Make the change, then click **Return to Primary**.
2. For page size, margins or headers: make sure you are in the primary configuration (the big button says **Print (Make PDF)**, not **Return to Primary**).
3. Print from the primary configuration.

### The big button says "Return to Primary" instead of "Print" {#31-troubleshooting--the-big-button-says-return-to-primary-instead-of-print}

**Why this happens:** You are in the secondary configuration of a diglot (after **Edit Settings…**).

**What to do:** Click **Return to Primary**, then **Print (Make PDF)**. (The small **Print** button prints only the secondary text.)

### PTXprint says "These books are not available in the secondary diglot project" {#31-troubleshooting--ptxprint-says-these-books-are-not-available-in-the-secondary-diglot-project}

**Why this happens:** You selected a book that the second project does not have.

**What to do:** On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, select only books that are in every project of the diglot.

### PTXprint says "Failed to merge texts due to a Syntax Error" (Diglot Merge Error) {#31-troubleshooting--ptxprint-says-failed-to-merge-texts-due-to-a-syntax-error-diglot-merge-error}

**Why this happens:** One of the texts has a marker error.

**What to do:**

1. Run **Basic Checks** in Paratext for every project in the diglot, and fix the errors.
2. If you use a changes file ([**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab), check that a rule has not caused the error.
3. Print each text on its own first, then the diglot.

### The status line says "No Config found for diglot", or Print is greyed out {#31-troubleshooting--the-status-line-says-no-config-found-for-diglot-or-print-is-greyed-out}

**Why this happens:** A row on the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab has no project or configuration.

**What to do:** On the **Diglot** tab, choose a **Project** and then a **Configuration** in every row.

### The diglot columns have big gaps, or the texts do not line up well {#31-troubleshooting--the-diglot-columns-have-big-gaps-or-the-texts-do-not-line-up-well}

**Why this happens:** One text needs more space than the other.

**What to do:**

1. Give the longer text more **% Width** (for example 55 and 45), or a smaller font size or line spacing in its row.
2. Try **Auto-calculate optimum widths of diglot columns** with one short book selected (two texts only).
3. Try another [**Merging mode**](#s-fcb-diglotMerge), for example **Scored (Chapter)** or **Chapter Verse**.
4. Then try the **Auto Page Fill** tool in the **PDF Preview** window (experimental for diglots and polyglots).

### The secondary caption is missing under a picture {#31-troubleshooting--the-secondary-caption-is-missing-under-a-picture}

**Why this happens:** [**Captions**](#s-c-pic-Captions) is not ticked in that text's row, or the texts use different picture files or verses, so the picture is not shared. Pictures are never shared in the books listed in [**Use Serial Layout for These Books**](#s-t-diglotSerialBooks).

**What to do:** On the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab, tick **Captions** in that text's row. Check that both texts use the same picture file at the same verse.

### The % Width numbers are red {#31-troubleshooting--the-width-numbers-are-red}

**Why this happens:** The widths of the texts on one page do not add up to 100.

**What to do:** Change the numbers, or right-click a row and choose **Distribute Widths**.

### I cannot untick Diglot (or Polyglot) {#31-troubleshooting--i-cannot-untick-diglot-or-polyglot}

**Why this happens:** This is on purpose, so that you do not lose your diglot settings. PTXprint opens the [**Save As Monoglot**](#10-diglot--save-as-monoglot) dialog instead.

**What to do:** Type a new configuration name and click **OK**. PTXprint opens a one-text copy. The diglot configuration stays as it was.

### Two Column Layout on the Layout tab is greyed out {#31-troubleshooting--two-column-layout-on-the-layout-tab-is-greyed-out}

**Why this happens:** A diglot always uses columns, so PTXprint ticks this box and locks it while the diglot is on.

## 5.9 Headers, footers and page numbers {#31-troubleshooting--headers-footers-and-page-numbers}

### There is no header on the first page of a book {#31-troubleshooting--there-is-no-header-on-the-first-page-of-a-book}

**Why this happens:** This is normal. PTXprint prints no header (or header rule) on the page where a book starts.

**What to do:** For a page number on that page, tick [**Print Page Number at Bottom of Intro Page(s)**](#s-c-pageNumTitlePage) on the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab (Regular and Full views).

### The header references are empty on some pages {#31-troubleshooting--the-header-references-are-empty-on-some-pages}

**Why this happens:** This is normal on pages without verses, for example introduction or glossary pages.

### The header shows the last verse where I expected the first verse {#31-troubleshooting--the-header-shows-the-last-verse-where-i-expected-the-first-verse}

**Why this happens:** [**Mirror Pages**](#s-c-mirrorpages) is ticked on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab. On left-hand pages PTXprint swaps **First Reference** and **Last Reference**, and also **Inner** and **Outer**.

**What to do:** Choose the other item on the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab. Or untick **Mirror Pages** if every page should look the same.

### My own header text prints wrongly, or the PDF fails after I typed a header {#31-troubleshooting--my-own-header-text-prints-wrongly-or-the-pdf-fails-after-i-typed-a-header}

**Why this happens:** In the header and footer boxes, spaces and the characters `# % & ^ ~ \` need a backslash before them.

**What to do:** Type `\ ` (a backslash and a space) for each space, for example `DRAFT\ \isodate`. Type `\#`, `\%` and so on for those characters.

### The footer shows "<Enter ID>" instead of the time {#31-troubleshooting--the-footer-shows-instead-of-the-time}

**Why this happens:** Older PTXprint versions saved the footer item **Time (HH:MM)** wrongly.

**What to do:** Update PTXprint. Configurations with this problem are corrected when they are opened. Then print again.

### The page numbers do not start at the number I set {#31-troubleshooting--the-page-numbers-do-not-start-at-the-number-i-set}

**Why this happens:** [**Starting Page Number (for Scripture Books)**](#s-s-startPageNum) applies at the first Scripture book when the front matter uses its own page numbering. If the front matter uses normal page numbers, numbering continues from the front matter.

**What to do:** Check the page number codes (`\nopagenums`, `\resetpagenums`, `\dopagenums`) in the front matter on the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab (advanced).

### The table of contents is empty or has wrong page numbers {#31-troubleshooting--the-table-of-contents-is-empty-or-has-wrong-page-numbers}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint needs a first run to learn the page numbers. With [**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun) it runs only once.

**What to do:**

1. Untick **Quick Run**.
2. Make sure **Table of Contents** is ticked on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, and the front matter contains `\ztoc|main\*`.
3. Print again.

### A variable prints as "<Type Value Here>" {#31-troubleshooting--a-variable-prints-as}

**Why this happens:** The front matter uses a variable that has no value yet.

**What to do:** On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, type a value in the **Variables and Values** table, and print again.

### The front matter does not appear in the PDF {#31-troubleshooting--the-front-matter-does-not-appear-in-the-pdf}

**What to do:** On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick [**Local Front Matter**](#s-c-frontmatter), and print again.

### My front matter changes disappeared {#31-troubleshooting--my-front-matter-changes-disappeared}

**Why this happens:** **Generate** on the **Front Matter** sub-tab replaces the whole front matter. [**Refresh**](#s-btn-refreshViewerText) also throws away unsaved changes. **Finish** in the [**Cover Wizard**](#s-btn-coverGenerate) replaces the cover sections. There is no Undo.

**What to do:** Type the changes again. In future, copy important text to a safe place before you click **Generate**, and make cover text changes after you use the wizard.

### The cover was turned off by itself {#31-troubleshooting--the-cover-was-turned-off-by-itself}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint turns off [**Create Cover Page**](#s-c-makeCoverPage) when you untick [**Local Front Matter**](#s-c-frontmatter). The status line says "The Cover is disabled because Local Front Matter is turned off."

**What to do:** On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick **Local Front Matter**, then **Create Cover Page** again.

### No cover is made, or the Cover Wizard button is greyed out {#31-troubleshooting--no-cover-is-made-or-the-cover-wizard-button-is-greyed-out}

**Why this happens:** [**Create Cover Page**](#s-c-makeCoverPage) is not ticked, or the front matter has no cover sections. The cover is also a **separate** PDF (name ending **\_cover**), not part of the main PDF.

**What to do:**

1. On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick [**Local Front Matter**](#s-c-frontmatter) and **Create Cover Page**. The [**Cover Wizard...**](#s-btn-coverGenerate) button then works.
2. Run the **Cover Wizard** and click **Finish** to create the cover sections.
3. Print. Look for the cover on the [**Cover**](#15-peripherals--cover) tab of the **PDF Preview** window.

### The Cover Wizard says "Existing cover settings found" {#31-troubleshooting--the-cover-wizard-says-existing-cover-settings-found}

**Why this happens:** The configuration has cover styles or cover sections that the wizard did not make, or that were changed by hand. The wizard cannot build on them.

**What to do:** Click **Delete and Continue** to delete the old cover and start a new one with the wizard. Or click **Cancel (keep my settings)** to keep the cover as it is and change it by hand (the wizard does not open).

### The Finish button in the Cover Wizard is greyed out {#31-troubleshooting--the-finish-button-in-the-cover-wizard-is-greyed-out}

**Why this happens:** **Finish** works only on the last (**Review**) step, and only when a title was typed in the front cover step.

**What to do:** Type a title in the front cover step, then go to the **Review** step.

### The colophon is missing {#31-troubleshooting--the-colophon-is-missing}

**Why this happens:** [**Colophon at End of Publication**](#s-c-colophon) is unticked. PTXprint unticks it when you tick [**Local Front Matter**](#s-c-frontmatter), and when you tick [**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate).

**What to do:** On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, tick **Colophon at End of Publication** again. Untick **Layout Only** at the bottom of the window, and print again.

## 5.10 Settings and configurations {#31-troubleshooting--settings-and-configurations}

### I lost my changes after I chose another configuration {#31-troubleshooting--i-lost-my-changes-after-i-chose-another-configuration}

**Why this happens:** When you choose another configuration in **Name**, PTXprint does **not** save the current one. (When you choose another **Project**, it does save first.)

**What to do:** The lost changes cannot be recovered. Make them again. In future, click **Save** (or **Print (Make PDF)**) before you change configuration.

### I deleted a configuration and want to know what is gone {#31-troubleshooting--i-deleted-a-configuration-and-want-to-know-what-is-gone}

**Why this happens:** **Delete** (after **Yes**) removes the settings and working files of that one configuration. This cannot be undone. PTXprint then changes to **Default**. The PDFs you made are **not** deleted, and other configurations are not touched. (Older PTXprint versions also emptied the output folder of all configurations. This is fixed.)

**What to do:**

1. To get the settings back, use **Import Settings...** on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab with a PDF made with [**Include Config Settings Within PDF**](#s-c-inclSettingsInPDF), or with a ZIP archive.
2. If the status line lists files that could not be deleted, close them in other programs (for example the PDF viewer).

### I clicked Reset and all my settings in Default are gone {#31-troubleshooting--i-clicked-reset-and-all-my-settings-in-default-are-gone}

**Why this happens:** For the **Default** configuration, **Delete** is replaced by [**Reset**](#20-import--reset) (Regular and Full views). **Reset** does not ask first. It sets every setting of **Default** back to the PTXprint defaults, and removes the saved files of **Default** (including its styles and picture list). Other configurations and PDFs are not changed.

**What to do:**

1. If the settings are in a PDF made with [**Include Config Settings Within PDF**](#s-c-inclSettingsInPDF), use **Import Settings...** on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab to bring them back.
2. Or import them from another configuration, or from a ZIP archive.
3. In future, use **Save As** to keep your work in a named configuration, not in **Default**.

### The lock button or the Copy configuration button is greyed out {#31-troubleshooting--the-lock-button-or-the-copy-configuration-button-is-greyed-out}

**Why this happens:** The **Default** configuration is selected. It cannot be locked, and it is never copied to other projects.

**What to do:** Use **Save As** to make a named configuration, then lock or copy that one.

### I cannot lock or unlock my configuration {#31-troubleshooting--i-cannot-lock-or-unlock-my-configuration}

**Why this happens:** To unlock, the password must be the same as when you locked. To lock, the password box must not be empty. **Cancel** never locks or unlocks.

**What to do:**

1. Click the lock button, type the password and click **OK**. If it is wrong, the status line says "Incorrect password".
2. If you cannot unlock it, use **Save As** to make a new, unlocked copy.

### The OK button in "Save Current Configuration As..." is greyed out {#31-troubleshooting--the-ok-button-in-save-current-configuration-as-is-greyed-out}

**Why this happens:** The name is empty, has spaces or special characters, or is already used.

**What to do:**

1. Read the message below the box. Use only letters a–z and A–Z, numbers, `(`, `)`, `_` and `-`.
2. To replace an existing configuration with that name, tick [**Replace it if it already exists**](#s-c-overwriteConfig). (**Default** can never be replaced.)

### Copy Configuration changed the titles in the other projects {#31-troubleshooting--copy-configuration-changed-the-titles-in-the-other-projects}

**Why this happens:** [**Keep each project's own language-specific variables**](#s-c-copyConfig-skipVars) was unticked, so the target projects got this project's titles and language name.

**What to do:** Copy again with that box ticked, or correct the values in the **Variables and Values** table on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab of each target project.

### Import Settings says "Cannot find any settings to import from the selected file" {#31-troubleshooting--import-settings-says-cannot-find-any-settings-to-import-from-the-selected-file}

**Why this happens:** The PDF was made without [**Include Config Settings Within PDF**](#s-c-inclSettingsInPDF) (on the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab), or with a very old PTXprint version.

**What to do:** Use another source, for example a ZIP archive made with [**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra), or a saved configuration. In future, keep **Include Config Settings Within PDF** ticked.

### I imported only one group of settings, but everything changed {#31-troubleshooting--i-imported-only-one-group-of-settings-but-everything-changed}

**Why this happens:** [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything) was still ticked. In the **Basic** view the **Everything** tab is hidden but still ticked. Also, when the target is a **new** configuration name or an external folder, PTXprint always ticks **Everything**.

**What to do:**

1. Choose an existing configuration as the target.
2. Change to the **Regular** view, open **Import Settings...** again, and untick **Everything** before you tick the groups you want.

### Imported styles did not change {#31-troubleshooting--imported-styles-did-not-change}

**Why this happens:** PTXprint only updates styles that you have not changed in the target configuration. The fonts inside styles come with **Fonts+Script**, not with **Styles**.

**What to do:** In the **Import Settings** dialog, tick [**Override ALL Style Settings**](#s-c-sty-OverrideAllStyles). For style fonts, also tick **Fonts+Script**.

### A setting changed by itself {#31-troubleshooting--a-setting-changed-by-itself}

**Why this happens:** Some settings change others to keep them working together. For example:

* [**Hyphenate**](#s-c-hyphenate) unticks [**Between Letters**](#s-c-letterSpacing).
* **Right-to-Left** ticks [**RTL Book Binding**](#s-c-RTLbookBinding).
* **Variable Line Spacing** ticks [**Fill Columns**](#s-c-variableLineSpacing) and [**Allow Unbalanced Columns**](#s-c-allowUnbalanced).
* Changing between one and two columns halves or doubles the [**Base Indent**](#s-s-indentUnit).
* **Print-CMYK**, **Print-Gray** and **Print-Spot** tick [**Only Show on Odd Pages**](#s-c-tabsOddOnly) for thumb tabs.
* The footnote and cross-reference placements change together.
* [**Local Front Matter**](#s-c-frontmatter) and [**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate) untick the colophon.
* [**Compare PDFs**](#s-c-createDiff) keeps the previous PDF even if [**Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept**](#s-s-keepVersions) is 0.

**What to do:** Read the status line. PTXprint often says what it changed. Change the setting back if you need to.

## 5.11 Comparing PDFs {#31-troubleshooting--comparing-pdfs}

### Compare PDFs does not show a diff PDF {#31-troubleshooting--compare-pdfs-does-not-show-a-diff-pdf}

**Why this happens:** No differences were found, or the comparison could not be made.

**What to do:** Read the status line at the bottom of the window:

* **No differences found** – the two PDFs look the same.
* **Nothing to compare with yet: make a change and print again** – there is no previous PDF yet. Print once more.
* **Cannot find the PDF to compare with: ...** – the file chosen with **Select...** is gone. Choose it again.
* **Cannot compare PDFs: the pages are different sizes** – the page size changed. Only pages of the same size can be compared.
* **No pages could be compared. Check the Start Page Offset** – make [**Start Page Offset**](#s-s-diffOffset) smaller.
* **No differences found, but the old Diff PDF is open and cannot be removed** – close the old diff PDF in your PDF program.

### Every page shows as changed in the diff PDF {#31-troubleshooting--every-page-shows-as-changed-in-the-diff-pdf}

**Why this happens:** The pages are probably not lined up, or something changed on every page (margins, headers, page numbers).

**What to do:** Change to the **Full** view. On the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab, in [**Compare PDFs**](#s-c-createDiff):

1. If one PDF has extra pages at the start (for example a cover), set [**Start Page Offset**](#s-s-diffOffset).
2. If you changed only the margins or the gutter, tick [**Smart Check**](#s-c-diffSmart).
3. If only headers, footers or page numbers changed, tick [**Headers + Footers**](#s-c-diffIgnoreHeadFoot) under **Ignore When Comparing**.

Extra pages at the end of the longer PDF always show as changed. This is correct.

## 5.12 I cannot find a setting {#31-troubleshooting--i-cannot-find-a-setting}

### A tab or setting that I used before has disappeared {#31-troubleshooting--a-tab-or-setting-that-i-used-before-has-disappeared}

**Why this happens:** The view level is lower than before. Lower view levels hide many settings. (The [**Peripherals**](#s-lb-Peripherals) and [**Finishing**](#s-lb-Finishing) tabs show only their main settings in the **Basic** view. The [**Publications**](#ch-16-publications) tab is only in the **Full** view.)

**What to do:**

1. Click **≡** › [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) › **Regular View** or **Full View**.
2. Or type the name of the setting in **Search for settings** (bottom-left, or **Ctrl+F**). PTXprint raises the view level if the setting is hidden.

### The PDF has pictures (or a diglot, borders, thumb tabs …) but I cannot find the setting {#31-troubleshooting--the-pdf-has-pictures-or-a-diglot-borders-thumb-tabs-but-i-cannot-find-the-setting}

**Why this happens:** The feature was turned on in a higher view level. Hidden settings still work.

**What to do:**

1. Change to **Full View**.
2. Look for tabs with blue names. A blue tab name means a feature on that tab is on.
3. Turn the feature off on that tab.

### A setting is greyed out {#31-troubleshooting--a-setting-is-greyed-out}

**Why this happens:** It needs another setting first, or another setting blocks it. Common examples:

| Greyed-out setting | What it needs |
| --- | --- |
| Almost all of **Layout**, **Fonts+Script** and **Styles** | Untick [**Lock UI Layout Settings**](#s-c-lockUI4Layout) ([**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, Full view). |
| **Save**, **Delete**, **Notes** | Unlock the configuration (lock button on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab). |
| Lock button, **Copy configuration to other projects** | Choose a configuration other than **Default**. |
| [**Reset**](#20-import--reset) (Basic tab) | Regular or Full view. |
| **Two Column Layout** | Turn off the diglot. A diglot always uses columns. |
| [**Verse**](#s-c-rangeShowVerse) (header references) | Tick [**Chapter**](#s-c-rangeShowChapter) first. |
| [**Parallel Passage Refs**](#s-c-parallelRefs) | Tick [**Headings**](#s-c-sectionHeads) on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab. |
| [**Hanging Poetry Verse Numbers**](#s-c-hangpoetry) | Untick [**Marginal Verses**](#s-c-marginalverses). |
| [**Optimize Layout for Poetry Books**](#s-c-optimizePoetryLayout) | Tick [**Use Special Features for These Books**](#s-c-useChapterLabel) (**Body** tab). |
| [**Between Letters**](#s-c-letterSpacing) | Untick **Interlinear** on the **Advanced** tab. |
| **End of Column** (notes) | Tick **Two Column Layout**. |
| **Side Margin** (notes) | Tick [**Margin Notes Col Width (mm)**](#s-c-useMarginNotes) on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab. |
| An **Edit...** button on the **Advanced** tab | Tick the check box for that file first. |
| [**Scale to fit**](#s-c-scaleToFit) (Finishing) | Set [**Pages Per Spread**](#s-fcb-pagesPerSpread) to **1-up**. |
| [**Color Hue**](#s-col-spotColor), **Tolerance** | Choose **Print-Spot** as [**PDF Output Format**](#s-fcb-outputFormat). |
| **Locate...** (PDF Preview) | Tick [**Layout Analysis**](#s-c-layoutAnalysis). |
| Fine-tune buttons (Layout) | Nothing to fix: [**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) is already blue. |
| [**Mirror**](#s-fcb-plMirror) (picture) | Choose [**OK to mirror**](#s-r-picreverse-OK) on the picture's [**Checklist**](#s-lb-checklist) sub-tab. |
| **Generate** (Front Matter) | Unlock the configuration. |
| [**Cover Wizard...**](#s-btn-coverGenerate) | Tick [**Create Cover Page**](#s-c-makeCoverPage) ([**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab). |
| **Auto-calculate optimum widths of diglot columns** | A diglot with exactly two texts, and **Print** must be available. |
| [**Custom Script**](#s-c-oth-customScript) (Import Settings) | Import from a ZIP archive or a saved configuration, not a PDF. |
| [**Include Transcelerator Questions**](#s-c-txlQuestionsInclude) | The project needs Transcelerator data. |

**What to do:** Hover the mouse over the greyed-out setting; the tooltip often explains it. See also the chapter about that tab.

### The Help tab has very few links, or links do not open {#31-troubleshooting--the-help-tab-has-very-few-links-or-links-do-not-open}

**Why this happens:** [**Disable ALL Internet Use**](#s-c-noInternet) is ticked on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab. PTXprint shows "Internet Access Disabled" when you click a web link.

**What to do:** On the **Advanced** tab, **Main** sub-tab, **General** area, untick **Disable ALL Internet Use**.

### PTXprint does not show my projects {#31-troubleshooting--ptxprint-does-not-show-my-projects}

**Why this happens:** The [**Base Projects Directory**](#s-l-projects-dir) points to the wrong folder.

**What to do:** On the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab, click [**Change...**](#s-btn-changeProjectsDir) next to **Base Projects Directory**. Choose the folder that *contains* your Paratext project folders, and click **Use Selected**.

## 5.13 Getting more help {#31-troubleshooting--getting-more-help}

If your problem is not in this chapter:

1. Read **Common problems** in the chapter for the tab you are using.
2. On the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab, click [**Create Report...**](#s-btn-generateReport) and read the warnings and errors.
3. Ask the **Support Agent** or the **PTXprint User Community** (links on the **Help** tab).
4. Make an archive with [**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra) (choose only the book that shows the problem), and email it to **ptxprint_support@sil.org** with a clear description, your PTXprint version and screenshots.

# 6. Basic tab {#ch-03-basic}

## 6.1 What this tab is for {#03-basic--what-this-tab-is-for}

The **Basic** tab is the first tab in PTXprint. You come here to:

* choose the **project** (the Paratext project with the Scripture text),
* choose, save, lock, copy or delete a **configuration** (a named set of settings),
* choose **what to print** – one book, part of a book, several books, or a Bible module,
* check the **copyright and license** statement for the publication.

Start here every time. Most other settings depend on the project and configuration that you choose here.

## 6.2 Project {#03-basic--project}

Choose your Paratext project in the **Project** list. PTXprint shows the full name of the project next to the list.

* When you change to another project, PTXprint first saves the current configuration. Then it opens the configuration that you last used with the new project (or **Default**).
* The last item in the **Project** list is a blue **Import...** item. It opens the [**Import Scripture...**](#03-basic--import-scripture) dialog. Use it when you have a Scripture text bundle (a .zip file) but not a Paratext project, or to install the sample text (the Berean Standard Bible).

### Copyright & Licensing {#03-basic--copyright-licensing}

(Regular and Full views.) Click **Copyright & Licensing** to open the area. It has two parts:

* **Copyright** – the copyright statement. PTXprint fills it in from the Paratext project settings. You can change it here. Click **Reload copyright from Paratext project** to get the Paratext text back.
* [**License**](#s-ecb-licenseText) – choose one of the Creative Commons licenses, **All Rights Reserved**, or type your own license.

PTXprint puts these texts into the front matter (for example on the back of the title page) through the variables `\zcopyright` and `\zlicense`. Special codes work in both boxes: `(c)` becomes ©, `(r)` becomes ®, `(tm)` becomes ™, `~` is a non-breaking space, and `//` forces a new line.

## 6.3 Layout Configuration {#03-basic--layout-configuration}

A **configuration** (or layout) is a named set of settings. One project can have many configurations, for example one for a draft and one for the final book. See the chapter about the main window for more about configurations and saving.

* **Name** – the list of saved configurations. Choose one to load its settings. Or type a new name here and click **Save** to make a new configuration. Use only the letters a–z and A–Z, numbers, brackets `( )`, underscores `_` and hyphens `-`. No spaces.
* The **Save As** button (an icon next to the name) opens the [**Save Current Configuration As...**](#03-basic--save-current-configuration-as) dialog.
* The **lock** button locks or unlocks the configuration with a password.
* The **Copy configuration to other projects** button opens the [**Copy Configuration To...**](#03-basic--copy-configuration-to) dialog. (Regular and Full views.) It is greyed out for the **Default** configuration, because **Default** is never copied to other projects.
* **Delete** removes the selected configuration. For the **Default** configuration, this button is replaced by [**Reset**](#20-import--reset).
* **Import Settings...** opens the **Import Settings** dialog, to bring in settings from a PDF, a ZIP archive, or another configuration. See the chapter ["Importing settings"](#ch-20-import). (Basic, Regular and Full views.)
* [**Run Tutorial...**](#s-btn-runTutorial) steps through a tutorial file on the current project and configuration. See ["Run a tutorial"](#03-basic--run-a-tutorial) below. (Basic, Regular and Full views.)
* **Notes** – an optional description of the configuration, for you and your team. (Basic, Regular and Full views.)

When you choose another configuration in the **Name** list, PTXprint does **not** save the current one. Click **Save** first.

## 6.4 What to Print {#03-basic--what-to-print}

Choose one of three ways to say what goes into the PDF:

* [**Single Book**](#s-r-book-single) – choose one book in the list. To print only part of the book, type chapter numbers in [**From Chapter**](#s-t-chapfrom) and **To**. When you choose a new book, PTXprint sets the chapters to the whole book.
* [**Portions or Multiple Books**](#s-r-book-multiple) – click [**Select Multiple Books...**](#s-btn-chooseBooks) to choose books by clicking them, or type a list in the box. You can type book codes (`MAT MRK LUK JHN`), book ranges (`MAT-REV`) and references (`JHN 2:1-12`, `PSA 23; 100; 117`, `GEN 1:1-2:3`). Use the 3-letter USFM codes (for example `JHN`, not `John`). Press **Ctrl+B** to jump to this box.
* [**Bible Module**](#s-r-book-module) – print a Paratext module (a .sfm file that lists passages to include). Click [**Choose...**](#s-btn-chooseBibleModule) to select the module file. Click **Edit...** to see it on the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab. (Bible Module: Basic, Regular and Full views; **Edit...**: Regular and Full.)

If you type in **From Chapter** or **To**, PTXprint changes to **Single Book**. If you type in the book list, PTXprint changes to **Portions or Multiple Books**.

The FRT (front matter) book is not in the book lists. Set up the front matter on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab instead.

## 6.5 Dialogs on this tab {#03-basic--dialogs-on-this-tab}

### Save Current Configuration As... {#03-basic--save-current-configuration-as}

Opens when you click the **Save As** button. Type a name in [**Configuration Name**](#s-t-configName) and click **OK**. PTXprint makes a new configuration with a copy of the current settings, saves it, and changes to it. **OK** stays greyed out until the name is valid. A message below the box says if the name has spaces or special characters, or if a configuration with that name already exists.

If the name already exists, you can tick [**Replace it if it already exists**](#s-c-overwriteConfig). Then PTXprint deletes the old configuration and saves the current settings in its place. The **Default** configuration can never be replaced. The box is unticked each time the dialog opens, so you must choose to replace each time.

Tip: Click **Save** before **Save As...**, so that the new configuration starts from your latest settings.

### Lock/Unlock Configuration {#03-basic--lock-unlock-configuration}

Opens when you click the **lock** button. Locking protects a configuration so that nobody changes or deletes it by mistake.

* **To lock:** type a password (up to 16 characters) and click **OK**. PTXprint saves the configuration and then locks it. The lock icon changes, and dots appear in the box next to the name.
* **To unlock:** click the lock button again, type the same password, and click **OK**. If the password is wrong, the configuration stays locked and the status line says "Incorrect password".
* You must type a password to lock. If the box is empty, PTXprint does not lock the configuration and asks you for a password.
* **Cancel** (or closing the dialog) never locks or unlocks anything.
* While a configuration is locked, **Save**, **Delete** and **Notes** are greyed out, and PTXprint does not save changes (not even when you print). You can still try out settings and print, but the changes are not kept.
* You cannot lock the **Default** configuration.

### Copy Configuration To... {#03-basic--copy-configuration-to}

Opens when you click the **Copy configuration to other projects** button. Use it when several projects need the same layout (for example, a series of New Testaments in related languages).

1. Click the projects that should receive a copy of the current configuration. The current project is shown in black and cannot be chosen. The [**Recent**](#s-ecb-mpsTargets) list at the bottom shows your selection, and remembers your last 10 selections.
2. Choose what to do if a target project already has a configuration with the same name:
   * [**Do NOT Replace Existing Config**](#s-r-copyConfig-noReplace) – skip those projects. Use this the first time you copy.
   * [**Merge Configurations From Both**](#s-r-copyConfig-merge) – combine the two. Settings that were changed in the target project since the first copy are kept.
   * [**Overwrite With Recent Changes**](#s-r-copyConfig-overwrite) – settings that were changed in this (source) project replace the target settings.
3. Leave [**Keep each project's own language-specific variables**](#s-c-copyConfig-skipVars) ticked (the normal choice), so that each target project keeps its own titles and language name. Untick it only if the target projects should get the same values as this project.
4. Click **OK**.

The **Default** configuration is never copied, and the button is greyed out while **Default** is selected. Use **Save As** to give the configuration a name first.

PTXprint copies the saved files of the configuration: the settings, the styles, the changes and TeX files, and the front matter. Adjust lists (paragraph adjustments) are not copied, because they belong to one text. Click **Save** before you copy, so that the copy has your latest settings.

### Select Books To Export to PDF {#03-basic--select-books-to-export-to-pdf}

Opens when you click [**Select Multiple Books...**](#s-btn-chooseBooks). Each book in the project is a button. Click a button to select or unselect that book. Hold **Shift** and click another book to select or unselect all books between the two. The buttons at the side select groups: [**All Books**](#s-b-mbsAll), [**Old Testament**](#s-b-mbsOT), [**New Testament**](#s-b-mbsNT), [**Deuterocanon**](#s-b-mbsDC), [**Extra Material**](#s-b-mbsXtra), [**Toggle Books**](#s-b-mbsToggle) (reverse the selection), and [**Reset All**](#s-b-mbsNone) (unselect all). A group button selects all books of that group. If they are all selected already, it unselects them. Click **OK**. PTXprint puts the books in the book list in normal Bible order. You can then change the order by typing in the list.

### Import Scripture... {#03-basic--import-scripture}

Opens when you choose **Import...** at the end of the **Project** list. There are two ways to get a text:

* [**Install BSB**](#s-b-installBSB) – installs the Berean Standard Bible that comes with PTXprint. It is good for practice and as a second text in a diglot.
* **Step 1 – Step 3** – install a Scripture text bundle (.zip):
  1. Download a bundle from the [**Primary DBL site**](#s-lb-DBLdownloads) (Digital Bible Library – you must log in) or the [**Open.Bible site**](#s-lb-openBible). Choose a bundle that has the text (not only audio). The USX format is best.
  2. Click **Locate...** and choose the .zip file.
  3. Check the project name in **Assign a Name for the Project** and click **OK**.

PTXprint creates the new project in a folder called `_PTXprint` inside your Paratext projects folder, and opens it.

### Please Confirm... {#03-basic--please-confirm}

PTXprint asks you to confirm before something that cannot be undone:

* **"You are about to REMOVE the '...' configuration"** – appears when you click **Delete**. It names the configuration. Click **Yes** to delete it, or **No** to keep it. Its settings and working files are deleted. PDF files that you made from it are **not** deleted.
* **"You are about to CREATE a diglot (or polyglot) configuration"** – appears when you turn on a diglot. PTXprint suggests that you first use **Save As...** to make a new configuration for the diglot.

## 6.6 Common tasks {#03-basic--common-tasks}

### Start a new publication from an existing configuration {#03-basic--start-a-new-publication-from-an-existing-configuration}

1. In **Project**, choose the project.
2. In **Name**, choose the configuration that is closest to what you want.
3. Click **Save** (so that the latest settings are on disk).
4. Click the **Save As** button. Type a new name (for example `NT_A5`) and click **OK**.
5. Now change the settings. The old configuration stays as it was.

### Print one book, or part of a book {#03-basic--print-one-book-or-part-of-a-book}

1. Click [**Single Book**](#s-r-book-single) and choose the book in the list.
2. To print only some chapters, type the first chapter in [**From Chapter**](#s-t-chapfrom) and the last chapter in **To**.
3. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

### Print several books, or selected passages {#03-basic--print-several-books-or-selected-passages}

1. Click [**Select Multiple Books...**](#s-btn-chooseBooks), click the books you want (or click [**New Testament**](#s-b-mbsNT)), then click **OK**.
2. Or type in the book list, for example `MAT-ACT` or `PSA 23; 100; 117 LUK 15:11-32`.
3. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

### Protect a finished configuration {#03-basic--protect-a-finished-configuration}

1. Choose the configuration in **Name** (not **Default**).
2. Click the **lock** button.
3. Type a password and click **OK**. Remember the password.

### Use the same layout for another project {#03-basic--use-the-same-layout-for-another-project}

1. Click **Save**.
2. Click the **Copy configuration to other projects** button. (Regular or Full view. The configuration must not be **Default**.)
3. Click the target project(s).
4. Choose [**Do NOT Replace Existing Config**](#s-r-copyConfig-noReplace), leave [**Keep each project's own language-specific variables**](#s-c-copyConfig-skipVars) ticked, and click **OK**.
5. In **Project**, choose the target project and check the copied configuration.

### Set or correct the copyright statement {#03-basic--set-or-correct-the-copyright-statement}

1. Change to the **Regular** or **Full** view if needed.
2. Click **Copyright & Licensing** to open it.
3. Type the copyright text (type `(c)` for ©), or click **Reload copyright from Paratext project**.
4. Choose or type the [**License**](#s-ecb-licenseText).

### Get a text to practise with {#03-basic--get-a-text-to-practise-with}

1. Open the **Project** list and choose **Import...** (the last item).
2. Click [**Install BSB**](#s-b-installBSB). PTXprint installs and opens the BSB project.

### Delete a configuration that you do not need {#03-basic--delete-a-configuration-that-you-do-not-need}

1. Choose it in **Name**.
2. Click **Delete**. Check that the message names the right configuration, then click **Yes**.
3. PTXprint changes to the **Default** configuration and deletes the settings and working files of the old one. The PDF files that you made from it stay in the output folder.

### Run a tutorial {#03-basic--run-a-tutorial}

A tutorial is a file with a list of steps (a .json file, or a recorded test in a .zip file). You may get one from a trainer.

1. Choose the project and configuration to practise on. The tutorial makes its changes there, so use a practice configuration (for example make one with **Save As**).
2. Click [**Run Tutorial...**](#s-btn-runTutorial) and choose the tutorial file.
3. A small tutorial window opens. It shows the next step, and PTXprint highlights the control that the step uses.
4. Click **Step** (or press **Space**) to do the next step, **Skip** (or [**S**](#32-glossary--s)) to leave it out, or **Play** (or [**P**](#32-glossary--p)) to do the steps one after another. **Run to end** does all the remaining steps.
5. Close the tutorial window to stop. If the tutorial needed a higher view level, PTXprint changes the view level while it runs and changes it back when you close the window.

## 6.7 Common problems {#03-basic--common-problems}

### My recent changes were lost when I chose another configuration {#03-basic--my-recent-changes-were-lost-when-i-chose-another-configuration}

**Cause:** Choosing another configuration in the **Name** list does not save the current one. **What to do:** Always click **Save** before you change configurations.

### The lock button is greyed out {#03-basic--the-lock-button-is-greyed-out}

**Cause:** The **Default** configuration cannot be locked. **What to do:** Use **Save As** to make a named configuration, then lock that one.

### I cannot save, and Delete and Notes are greyed out {#03-basic--i-cannot-save-and-delete-and-notes-are-greyed-out}

**Cause:** The configuration is locked. **What to do:** Click the lock button and enter the password, or use **Save As** to make a new, unlocked copy.

### There is a Reset button instead of Delete {#03-basic--there-is-a-reset-button-instead-of-delete}

**Cause:** The **Default** configuration is selected. It cannot be deleted, so [**Reset**](#20-import--reset) is shown instead. Be careful: **Reset** asks no question. It at once sets all settings of the Default configuration back to the PTXprint defaults, and deletes the files in the Default configuration folder. Other configurations are not changed.

### The OK button in "Save Current Configuration As..." is greyed out {#03-basic--the-ok-button-in-save-current-configuration-as-is-greyed-out}

**Cause:** The name is empty, has spaces or special characters, or is already used. **What to do:** Read the message below the box. Use only letters a–z and A–Z, numbers, `(`, `)`, `_` and `-`.

### PTXprint says "Unknown book code" {#03-basic--ptxprint-says-unknown-book-code}

**Cause:** The book list has a word that is not a 3-letter USFM book code (for example `John`). **What to do:** Use the codes, for example `JHN`, `MAT`, `1CO`.

### I cannot find the FRT book in the list {#03-basic--i-cannot-find-the-frt-book-in-the-list}

**Cause:** PTXprint does not list FRT as a book. **What to do:** Set up front matter on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab.

### The Primary DBL site and Open.Bible site links do not work {#03-basic--the-primary-dbl-site-and-open-bible-site-links-do-not-work}

**Cause:** [**Disable ALL Internet Use**](#s-c-noInternet) is ticked on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab. **What to do:** Untick it, or download the bundle another way and use **Locate...**.

### Copyright & Licensing or Copy configuration are missing, or Reset is greyed out {#03-basic--copyright-licensing-or-copy-configuration-are-missing-or-reset-is-greyed-out}

**Cause:** They are only available in the **Regular** and **Full** views. **What to do:** Click **≡** › [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) › **Regular View**.

### The Copy configuration to other projects button is greyed out {#03-basic--the-copy-configuration-to-other-projects-button-is-greyed-out}

**Cause:** The **Default** configuration is selected. PTXprint never copies **Default** to other projects. **What to do:** Use **Save As** to save the settings under another name, then copy that configuration.

## 6.8 Settings reference {#03-basic--settings-reference}

### Import Scripture... (dialog) {#03-basic--import-scripture-dialog}

#### OK {#s-btn-dbl-ok}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Installs the bundle chosen with **Locate...**, using the name in **Assign a Name for the Project**, and opens the new project. Greyed out until the name is valid and not already used.

#### Cancel {#s-btn-dbl-cancel}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Closes the dialog without installing anything. PTXprint goes back to the project that was open before.

#### Install BSB {#s-b-installBSB}

Button · shown in: all views

> The Berean Standard Bible is a Public Domain English Bible. It is bundled with PTXprint but needs to be installed in your Projects folder.
>
> This is a good training project and can also be used in diglots.

Installs the BSB as a project called `BSB` in your projects folder, opens it and closes the dialog. No internet is needed. Use it to practise, to try out settings, or as the second text in a diglot.

#### Locate... {#s-btn-locateDBLbundle}

Button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Locate DBL bundle

> After downloading a scripture text bundle (.zip) file you need to tell PTXprint where the .zip file is located so that it can install it as a special resource project.

Opens a file chooser in the `Bundles` folder of your Paratext projects folder. PTXprint then shows the file name and suggests a project name from the bundle (adding a number if that name is already used). Shortcut: **Alt+O**.

#### Step 3 Assign a Name for the Project – Assign a name to a DBL bundle {#s-t-DBLprojName}

Text box · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> PTXprint will create this project within a subfolder called '\_PTXprint'. Use a short name (8 characters or fewer is best) for the new project. Do not use the name of an existing Project.

PTXprint suggests a name from the bundle. Use no spaces or special characters. A message appears below the box if the name cannot be used.

#### Primary DBL site {#s-lb-DBLdownloads}

Link · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Visit the Digital Bible Library to download a DBL Scripture bundle

> There are hundreds of Scripture bundles available at the Digital Bible Library website which you may download and use in a publication. You must log in to the site in order to access resources.
>
> Use resources which contain the text (not just the audio) and preferably select the USX download option.
>
> Note: If this option is disabled, it is due to the ["Disable ALL Internet Use"](#s-c-noInternet) option which has been set on the General section of the [Advanced tab](#ch-13-advanced).

Opens the Digital Bible Library website in your browser.

#### Open.Bible site {#s-lb-openBible}

Link · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Visit the Open.Bible site to download a Scripture bundle

> There are hundreds of Scripture bundles at the Open.Bible website which you may download and use in a publication.
>
> Use resources which contain the text (not just the audio) and preferably select the USX download option.
>
> Note: If this option is disabled, it is due to the ["Disable ALL Internet Use"](#s-c-noInternet) option which has been set on the General section of the [Advanced tab](#ch-13-advanced).
>
> If you don't already have a Scripture Text Bundle, then you can download a USX or USFM text bundle from an online scripture repository.

Opens the Open.Bible website in your browser. Its bundles are openly licensed.

### Save Current Configuration As... (dialog) {#03-basic--save-current-configuration-as-dialog}

#### OK {#s-btn-cfg-ok}

Button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

Creates the new configuration, saves it, and changes to it. Greyed out until the name is valid.

#### Cancel {#s-btn-cfg-cancel}

Button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

Closes the dialog. No new configuration is made.

#### Configuration Name – Enter a name for the configuration to be saved {#s-t-configName}

Text box · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> Enter a name for the configuration to be saved.
>
> Note that only Roman/Latin names are supported using: a-z A-Z, 0-9, parentheses, underscores and hyphens. Spaces are not permitted.

Use a short, clear name such as `NT_A5` or `Draft_2col`. Letters with accents are not allowed. The message below the box says if the name is not valid or already exists. Write longer descriptions in **Notes** on the Basic tab.

#### Replace it if it already exists {#s-c-overwriteConfig}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> If a configuration with this name already exists, delete it and save the current settings in its place. (Useful for tests and tutorials that make a fresh copy each time they run.)

Leave it unticked in normal use; then PTXprint does not accept a name that already exists. When ticked, the old configuration is deleted when you click **OK**, and this cannot be undone. If you type the name of the configuration that you are in, PTXprint makes it again from the configuration it was first copied from (if PTXprint knows it), or else just saves it.

### Select Books To Export to PDF (dialog) {#03-basic--select-books-to-export-to-pdf-dialog}

#### OK {#s-btn-mbs-ok}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Puts the selected books in the book list, in normal Bible order. PTXprint changes to [**Portions or Multiple Books**](#s-r-book-multiple) if any books are selected.

#### Cancel {#s-btn-mbs-cancel}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Closes the book selector without changing the book list.

#### All Books {#s-b-mbsAll}

Button · shown in: all views

> Click to turn ALL books on/off.

If all books are already selected, it unselects them all.

#### Old Testament {#s-b-mbsOT}

Button · shown in: all views

> Click to turn OT books on/off.

If they are all selected already, it unselects them. Other books are not changed.

#### New Testament {#s-b-mbsNT}

Button · shown in: all views

> Click to turn NT books on/off.

If they are all selected already, it unselects them. Other books are not changed.

#### Deuterocanon {#s-b-mbsDC}

Button · shown in: all views

> Click to turn DC books on/off.

If they are all selected already, it unselects them. Other books are not changed.

#### Extra Material {#s-b-mbsXtra}

Button · shown in: all views

> Click to turn Extra books on/off.

Extra books are for example the glossary (GLO), the indexes (TDX, NDX) and XXA–XXG. If they are all selected already, it unselects them. Other books are not changed.

#### Toggle Books {#s-b-mbsToggle}

Button · shown in: all views

> Click to toggle ALL books. Those which are selected will be deselected, and the unselected ones will be selected.

For example, click [**New Testament**](#s-b-mbsNT) and then **Toggle Books** to select everything except the New Testament.

#### Reset All {#s-b-mbsNone}

Button · shown in: all views

> Click to turn OFF all books.

Use it to start your selection again.

#### Why is FRT not listed? {#03-basic--why-is-frt-not-listed}

Label · shown in: all views

> The FRT book in Paratext contains front matter for a publication. Visit the Peripherals page to set up front matter for this publication.

### Copy Configuration To... (dialog) {#03-basic--copy-configuration-to-dialog}

#### OK {#s-btn-mps-ok}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Copies the current configuration to all selected projects, using the option you chose. The copy uses the saved files, so click **Save** in the main window before you open this dialog.

#### Cancel {#s-btn-mps-cancel}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Closes the dialog. Nothing is copied.

#### Recent {#s-ecb-mpsTargets}

Drop-down list · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Shows selected target projects. Pick a previous selection from the dropdown, or select projects in the grid above.

You can also type project names here, separated by spaces. PTXprint remembers your last 10 selections, which helps when you copy to the same group of projects again and again.

#### Do NOT Replace Existing Config {#s-r-copyConfig-noReplace}

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Copy Config: Do NOT Replace Existing Config

> Selecting this option will prevent any changes overwriting an existing configuration of the same name in the target project(s).
>
> This option is usually used when copying a configuration to other projects for the first time.

Projects that already have a configuration with this name are left unchanged. The safest choice.

#### Merge Configurations From Both {#s-r-copyConfig-merge}

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Copy Config: MERGE Configurations From Both

> Selecting this option will MERGE the settings from the source configuration with the identically named configuration in the target project. Any changes that were made to the target project's configuration since it was first shared will be kept (i.e. modified target settings are retained if there is a clash of settings).

Settings not changed in the target are updated from this project.

#### Overwrite With Recent Changes {#s-r-copyConfig-overwrite}

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Copy Config: OVERWRITE With Recent Changes

> Selecting this option will REPLACE (or overwrite) any settings in the identically named configuration in the target project IF those settings were changed in the source project since the configuration was first shared. (i.e. if both source and target projects modified a setting, then the source project's setting will "win").

Use it when this project is the "master" layout for a group of projects.

#### Keep each project's own language-specific variables {#s-c-copyConfig-skipVars}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Copy Config: Keep target project's own variables

> When checked, the variable values (such as the main title, subtitle and language name, and the Strong's index titles) are NOT copied, so each target project keeps its own. A configuration that is new to a target project starts without them, rather than with the source project's values.
>
> Uncheck this to copy these values as well.

The variables are listed on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab. After the copy, fill them in on each target project that did not have this configuration before.

### Lock/Unlock Configuration (dialog) {#03-basic--lock-unlock-configuration-dialog}

#### OK {#s-btn-pw-ok}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Locks the configuration with the password you typed, or unlocks it if the password matches. If the configuration is not locked and the box is empty, nothing is locked and PTXprint asks for a password. If the password is wrong, the configuration stays locked and the status line says so.

#### Cancel {#s-btn-pw-cancel}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Closes the dialog. Nothing is locked or unlocked, and the password box is cleared.

#### Enter Password – Enter password for config {#s-t-password}

Text box · shown in: all views

> Enter a password of up to 16 characters to lock/unlock this saved configuration.

PTXprint stores only a coded form of the password. If you forget it, you cannot unlock the configuration in PTXprint, so keep it somewhere safe.

# 7. Layout tab {#ch-04-layout}

## 7.1 What this tab is for {#04-layout--what-this-tab-is-for}

The **Layout** tab sets the shape of every page: page size, margins (the empty space around the text), one or two columns, the size of the main text and the space between lines.

Come here when you start a new publication, when the printer tells you the page size, or when the text does not fit the number of pages you want. Most settings change the whole book. After a change, click **Print** again to see the result.

Some words used in this chapter:

* **pt (point)** – a small unit used for type. 1 pt is about 0.35 mm. 72 pt is about one inch (25.4 mm).
* **Baseline** – the invisible line that the letters sit on.
* **Line spacing** – the distance from the baseline of one line to the baseline of the next.
* **Gutter** – an extra empty space. A *binding gutter* is extra space at the spine of the book. A *column gutter* is the space between two columns of text.
* **Text area** – the part of the page where the main text goes. The margins are outside it.

## 7.2 Page Setup {#04-layout--page-setup}

This area holds [**Page Size**](#04-layout--page-size), [**Base Font Size (pt)**](#s-s-fontsize), [**Base Line Spacing (pt)**](#s-s-linespacing), [**Base Indent**](#s-s-indentUnit), the binding gutter and the page-layout options.

### Page size {#04-layout--page-size}

Choose a size from the **Page Size** list, or type your own: width, comma, height, for example `148mm, 210mm`. You can use `mm`, `cm` or `in`. A typed size is saved when you save the configuration (or click **Print**). After that, it is in the list for all your projects. To remove a saved size, select it, right-click in the box and choose **Remove**. Ask your printer for the exact trim size (the size of the finished, cut page) before you start. Changing the page size later moves every line.

### Font size and line spacing (and how they work together) {#04-layout--font-size-and-line-spacing-and-how-they-work-together}

* [**Base Font Size (pt)**](#s-s-fontsize) is the size of the letters in normal paragraphs. All other text (headings, footnotes, verse numbers and so on) is sized *relative to* it. A bigger base font makes headings and footnotes grow by the same proportion.
* [**Base Line Spacing (pt)**](#s-s-linespacing) is the distance from one line to the next. It is normally bigger than the font size, so that the lines do not touch. 11 pt text with 14 pt line spacing is a common choice.

The [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) box (ticked by default) joins these two numbers:

* When it is ticked and you change the font size, the line spacing changes by the same proportion. For example, 11 pt text on 14 pt spacing changed to 12 pt text gives about 15.3 pt spacing. The page keeps the same "look", only bigger.
* It also works the other way round: changing the line spacing changes the font size.
* When it is not ticked, you can change each number on its own. Use this for more (or less) space between lines with the same size letters.
* When you tick it again, PTXprint keeps the ratio the two numbers have *now*.

The line spacing decides how many lines fit on a page.

### Lines Per Page and the fine-tune buttons {#04-layout--lines-per-page-and-the-fine-tune-buttons}

[**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) is calculated from the page height, the top and bottom margins and the line spacing. It updates when you change any of these.

* **Blue**: a whole number of lines fits the text area. No space is wasted.
* **Red**: the text area holds a whole number of lines plus part of a line. That part of a line is empty space at the bottom of each page.

When the number is red, three small fine-tune buttons (icon of justified lines) become active. One is next to [**Base Line Spacing (pt)**](#s-s-linespacing). The other two are next to the top and bottom margins in the **Margins** area. Each makes a small change so that a whole number of lines fits:

* If more than half a line is spare, it makes room for one more line.
* If less than half a line is spare, it spreads the same lines a little further apart (or makes the margin a little larger).

Click only **one** of the three buttons: the one for the setting you are most willing to change. The number turns blue and the buttons become grey again.

If [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) is ticked, the line-spacing button also changes the font size a little. To keep the font size exact, untick **Lock Ratio** first, or use a margin button.

### Binding gutter, Outer Gutter and Mirror Pages {#04-layout--binding-gutter-outer-gutter-and-mirror-pages}

* [**Binding Gutter (mm)**](#s-c-pagegutter) adds extra space to the inner edge of each page (near the spine), on top of **Side Margin Width**. Thick books need more, because the pages curve into the spine. The gutter changes sides on odd and even pages, so it is always at the spine.
* [**Outer Gutter**](#s-c-outerGutter) moves that extra space to the outer edge, for journaling or wide-margin Bibles where readers write in the outer margin.
* [**Mirror Pages**](#s-c-mirrorpages) makes odd and even pages mirror each other. Header items on the left of a right-hand page appear on the right of a left-hand page, so they stay on the outer (or inner) edge. In a diglot (two-language) layout it also keeps the primary text on the inner side, near the spine.

Whether the gutter swaps sides on odd and even pages is controlled by [**Double Sided Layout**](#s-c-doublesided) ([**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** tab, **Page Layout and Spacing**). It is normally on.

### Align Text to Baseline / Variable Line Spacing {#04-layout--align-text-to-baseline-variable-line-spacing}

This is a switch with [**Align Text to Baseline**](#s-c-noGrid) on the left and **Variable Line Spacing** on the right.

* **Align Text to Baseline** (left, the normal setting) puts every line on a fixed grid. Lines on the front and back of a sheet line up exactly. This matters on thin Bible paper, where the other side shows through. But some columns may end with an empty line or two. You fix these by hand with the page-filling tools in the PDF Preview.
* **Variable Line Spacing** (right) stretches the space between lines a little so that every column is filled to the bottom. Good for quick drafts and thicker paper. Front-to-back alignment is lost, and the whole book re-flows when you change it.

Switching to **Variable Line Spacing** also ticks [**Fill Columns**](#s-c-variableLineSpacing) and [**Allow Unbalanced Columns**](#s-c-allowUnbalanced). How much lines may stretch or shrink is set on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** tab, **Page Layout and Spacing**.

### Notelines (journaling layout) {#04-layout--notelines-journaling-layout}

[**Notelines**](#s-c-noteLines) prints ruled lines in a wide margin for readers' own notes. Ticking it also ticks **Binding Gutter** and [**Outer Gutter**](#s-c-outerGutter), and sets the gutter to 40 mm if it was under 30 mm. A colour button appears for the line colour. More noteline settings (spacing, offset, type) are on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** tab, **Page Layout and Spacing**.

### Margin Notes {#04-layout--margin-notes}

[**Margin Notes Col Width (mm)**](#s-c-useMarginNotes) creates an extra column beside the text. Footnotes, cross-references and (if you choose) section headings can go in it, beside their verse. Ticking it only creates the space. To put notes there, choose **Side Margin** as the position on the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab. To put headings there, tick [**In Margin**](#s-c-headingInMargin) on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab.

The column is normally on the right (or outer) edge. In a one-column layout, tick [**Margin Notes on Left/Inner**](#s-c-marginNotesInner) to put it on the left (or inner) edge.

If too many notes do not fit beside the text in one column, PTXprint moves the extra notes to the top of the margin column of the next column or page. This happens by itself; there is no setting for it. Check those pages in the PDF Preview, because a moved note is no longer beside its verse.

These settings are shown in the **Regular** and **Full** views.

## 7.3 Two Column Layout {#04-layout--two-column-layout}

Tick **Two Column Layout** for two columns of main text; untick it for one. When you change this, PTXprint halves (two columns) or doubles (one column) [**Base Indent**](#s-s-indentUnit), because a narrow column needs a smaller indent.

Most settings in this area only work with two columns:

* **Gutter Width (mm)** – the space between the columns. 4 mm is common.
* **Vertical Rule in Gutter** – a thin line down the middle of the gutter.
* **Adjust Top (pt)** – moves the top of that line up (negative) or down (positive). Greyed out until **Vertical Rule in Gutter** is ticked.
* [**Allow Unbalanced Columns**](#s-c-allowUnbalanced) – lets the two columns on a page end at different heights, by up to a set number of lines.

[**Thickness of Rule (pt)**](#s-s-ruleThickness) also works in one column, because it also sets the horizontal rule under the header.

A diglot (two languages side by side) needs two columns, so the **Two Column Layout** box is then greyed out.

## 7.4 Margins {#04-layout--margins}

The **Margins** area sets the empty space around the text, and the position of the header (the line at the top of the page, often with the book name and page number) and the footer (the line at the bottom).

### The margin diagram and its colours {#04-layout--the-margin-diagram-and-its-colours}

Next to the margin settings is a small picture of a page. It shows one or two columns, the vertical rule and the header rule, as you have set them. Coloured arrows show what each number measures:

* **Orange** – [**Side Margin Width (mm)**](#s-s-margins): from the edge of the page to the text.
* **Red** (top) – [**Start of Page to Top of Text (mm)**](#s-s-topmargin): the top margin.
* **Red** (bottom) – [**Bottom of Text to End of Page (mm)**](#s-s-bottommargin): the bottom margin.
* **Purple** (top) – [**Bottom of Header to Top of Text (pt)**](#s-s-headerposition): header-to-text gap.
* **Purple** (bottom) – [**Bottom of Text to Top of Footer (pt)**](#s-s-footerposition): text-to-footer gap.
* **Green** – [**Space between Rule and Top of Text (pt)**](#s-s-rhruleposition): rule-to-text gap.
* **Blue** – two values PTXprint calculates (you cannot type in them): top of page to header, and footer to bottom of page.

When the mouse is over a margin box, the picture shows only that box's arrow.

Margins are in **mm**, but the header and footer gaps are in **pt**.

### Header and footer position {#04-layout--header-and-footer-position}

The header sits *inside* the top margin, and the footer normally sits *inside* the bottom margin. So a bigger header gap moves the header up towards the page edge. Watch the blue numbers: if one becomes very small (or negative), the header or footer is too close to the edge and may be cut off when the book is trimmed.

Tick [**Place Footer Text Above the Bottom Margin**](#s-c-noinkinmargin) to put the footer inside the text area instead of in the margin.

Tick [**Horizontal Rule**](#s-c-rhrule) to draw a line under the header. Set its position with [**Space between Rule and Top of Text (pt)**](#s-s-rhruleposition).

To see the margins, header and footer areas on the page, tick [**Guides and Baselines**](#s-c-gridLines) on the **Content** tab of the **PDF Preview** window.

## 7.5 Change the Grid Settings dialog (graph paper) {#04-layout--change-the-grid-settings-dialog-graph-paper}

PTXprint can show a ["graph paper"](#s-c-gridGraph) grid over the pages in the **PDF Preview**, to measure things such as a margin or a picture.

Open the **PDF Preview**, go to its **Content** tab and tick **Graph Paper**. Click **Settings** next to it to open the **Change the Grid Settings** dialog. There you choose:

* **Major Units** – centimetres or inches between the thicker (major) lines, plus their colour and thickness.
* **Minor Divisions** – how many thinner lines between two major lines, plus their colour and thickness.
* **Place Grid** – **Whole Page**, **In Margin Areas** or **Only in Text Area**.

## 7.6 Lock UI Layout Settings {#04-layout--lock-ui-layout-settings}

When the typesetting is almost finished, you can protect the layout from accidental changes. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Main** tab, **General** area, tick **Lock UI Layout Settings**. (This is only shown in the **Full** view.)

While it is ticked, most of the **Layout** tab is greyed out (page size, font size, line spacing, columns, gutter, margins and more). The whole [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab and the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab are also greyed out. Untick it to make changes again.

## 7.7 Common tasks {#04-layout--common-tasks}

### How do I change the page size? {#04-layout--how-do-i-change-the-page-size}

1. On the **Layout** tab, **Page Setup** area, click the [**Page Size**](#04-layout--page-size) list.
2. Choose a size, for example **148mm, 210mm (A5)**, or type width, comma, height, for example `140mm, 216mm`.
3. If [**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) is red, click one fine-tune button (see the next task).
4. Click **Print**.

### How do I stop wasting space at the bottom of every page? {#04-layout--how-do-i-stop-wasting-space-at-the-bottom-of-every-page}

1. On the **Layout** tab, look at [**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) (shown in the **Regular** and **Full** views).
2. If it is red, click one fine-tune button: next to [**Base Line Spacing (pt)**](#s-s-linespacing), or in the **Margins** area next to the top or bottom margin. Choose the setting you are most willing to change.
3. The number turns blue. Click **Print**.

### How do I make the text bigger or smaller without changing the look of the page? {#04-layout--how-do-i-make-the-text-bigger-or-smaller-without-changing-the-look-of-the-page}

1. On the **Layout** tab, make sure [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) is ticked.
2. Change [**Base Font Size (pt)**](#s-s-fontsize). The line spacing changes with it.
3. If [**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) is red, click one fine-tune button.
4. Click **Print**.

### How do I put more space between the lines but keep the same letter size? {#04-layout--how-do-i-put-more-space-between-the-lines-but-keep-the-same-letter-size}

1. On the **Layout** tab, untick [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline).
2. Make [**Base Line Spacing (pt)**](#s-s-linespacing) larger, for example from 14 to 15.
3. Tick **Lock Ratio** again if you want the new ratio kept.
4. Click **Print**.

### How do I change between one and two columns? {#04-layout--how-do-i-change-between-one-and-two-columns}

1. On the **Layout** tab, tick or untick **Two Column Layout**.
2. For two columns, set **Gutter Width (mm)** and choose whether you want **Vertical Rule in Gutter**.
3. Check [**Base Indent**](#s-s-indentUnit). PTXprint changes it automatically, but you may want to adjust it.
4. Click **Print**.

### How do I add extra space at the spine for binding? {#04-layout--how-do-i-add-extra-space-at-the-spine-for-binding}

1. On the **Layout** tab, **Page Setup** area, tick [**Binding Gutter (mm)**](#s-c-pagegutter).
2. Type the extra space in the box beside it, for example 5 mm. Ask your printer how much your book's thickness needs.
3. Leave [**Outer Gutter**](#s-c-outerGutter) unticked.
4. Click **Print**.

### How do I make a journaling (wide-margin) Bible? {#04-layout--how-do-i-make-a-journaling-wide-margin-bible}

1. On the **Layout** tab, tick [**Notelines**](#s-c-noteLines) (shown in the **Regular** and **Full** views). PTXprint ticks **Binding Gutter** and [**Outer Gutter**](#s-c-outerGutter) and sets a wide gutter (at least 40 mm).
2. Change the gutter width if needed, and choose the line colour with the colour button.
3. Click **Print**.

### How do I put footnotes and cross-references in the side margin? {#04-layout--how-do-i-put-footnotes-and-cross-references-in-the-side-margin}

1. On the **Layout** tab, tick [**Margin Notes Col Width (mm)**](#s-c-useMarginNotes) and type the column width.
2. On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, set the position of footnotes and/or cross-references to **Side Margin**.
3. For section headings in the margin too, tick [**In Margin**](#s-c-headingInMargin) on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab.
4. For the column on the left (or inner) edge, tick [**Margin Notes on Left/Inner**](#s-c-marginNotesInner) (one column only).
5. Click **Print**.

### How do I see a measuring grid on the page? {#04-layout--how-do-i-see-a-measuring-grid-on-the-page}

1. Click **Print** so that the **PDF Preview** opens.
2. On the preview's **Content** tab, tick [**Graph Paper**](#s-c-gridGraph).
3. Click **Settings** next to it to change units, colours and where the grid is drawn. Click **OK**.

## 7.8 Common problems {#04-layout--common-problems}

### Almost everything on the Layout tab is greyed out {#04-layout--almost-everything-on-the-layout-tab-is-greyed-out}

**Cause:** [**Lock UI Layout Settings**](#04-layout--lock-ui-layout-settings) is ticked. This also greys out the whole [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab and the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab.

**What to do:** Change the view level to **Full**. On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Main** tab, **General** area, untick **Lock UI Layout Settings**.

### I changed the font size and the line spacing changed too (or the other way round) {#04-layout--i-changed-the-font-size-and-the-line-spacing-changed-too-or-the-other-way-round}

**Cause:** [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) is ticked (the normal setting).

**What to do:** Untick **Lock Ratio** before you change one number on its own.

### I clicked the line-spacing fine-tune button and my font size changed {#04-layout--i-clicked-the-line-spacing-fine-tune-button-and-my-font-size-changed}

**Cause:** [**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) is ticked, so the font size follows the line spacing.

**What to do:** Untick **Lock Ratio** and type your font size again. Then use the fine-tune button again, or use the top or bottom margin button instead.

### The fine-tune buttons are greyed out {#04-layout--the-fine-tune-buttons-are-greyed-out}

**Cause:** [**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) is already a whole number (blue), so there is nothing to fix. They are also greyed out when [**Lock UI Layout Settings**](#04-layout--lock-ui-layout-settings) is ticked.

### The fine-tune buttons and Lines Per Page are not visible {#04-layout--the-fine-tune-buttons-and-lines-per-page-are-not-visible}

**Cause:** They are only shown in the **Regular** and **Full** views. Change the view level from the main menu.

### I cannot untick Two Column Layout {#04-layout--i-cannot-untick-two-column-layout}

**Cause:** A diglot (two languages) is set up. A diglot needs two columns.

### The Base Indent changed by itself {#04-layout--the-base-indent-changed-by-itself}

**Cause:** Switching between one and two columns halves or doubles the indent.

**What to do:** Type the indent you want after you change the number of columns.

### "Margin Notes on Left/Inner" is greyed out {#04-layout--margin-notes-on-left-inner-is-greyed-out}

**Cause:** It only works with one column, and only when [**Margin Notes Col Width (mm)**](#s-c-useMarginNotes) is ticked.

### Margin notes do not appear even though I ticked Margin Notes {#04-layout--margin-notes-do-not-appear-even-though-i-ticked-margin-notes}

**Cause:** The Layout tab setting only makes the space.

**What to do:** On the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab, choose **Side Margin** for footnotes and/or cross-references.

### The header or footer is too close to the edge of the page {#04-layout--the-header-or-footer-is-too-close-to-the-edge-of-the-page}
