# 13. Diglot tab (two or more languages) {#ch-10-diglot}

## 13.1 What this tab is for {#10-diglot--what-this-tab-is-for}

A [**diglot**](#s-lb-Diglot) is a publication with two texts side by side on the page. The texts can be two languages, two scripts of the same language, or two translations. A **polyglot** has three or more texts. PTXprint lines the texts up so that the same verses (or paragraphs) start at the same height in each column.

Each text in a diglot comes from its own Paratext project and uses its own PTXprint configuration. The configuration you have open when you tick [**Diglot (or Polyglot)**](#s-c-diglot) becomes the **primary** text (code [**L**](#32-glossary--l)). The other texts are **secondary** texts (code [**R**](#32-glossary--r), then [**A**](#32-glossary--a), [**B**](#32-glossary--b), [**C**](#32-glossary--c) …). The primary configuration controls the page: page size, margins, headers and footers, and most layout settings. Each secondary configuration controls how its own text looks: its fonts, font size, line spacing, footnotes and so on.

Come to this tab to turn a configuration into a diglot, choose the other project(s), set the column widths, and choose how the texts are merged (joined together). The **Diglot** tab is shown in the **Regular** and **Full** views only. When **Diglot (or Polyglot)** is ticked, the tab name turns blue.

**Important:** turning a diglot on cannot simply be undone. Before you start, go to the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, **Layout Configuration** area, and use **Save As** to make a new configuration for the diglot, so your normal (single-text) configuration stays as it is.

## 13.2 Diglot (or Polyglot) {#10-diglot--diglot-or-polyglot}

The [**Diglot (or Polyglot)**](#s-c-diglot) checkbox is in the frame title. All other settings on the tab are hidden until it is ticked.

When you tick it:

1. PTXprint asks you to confirm. Click **Yes** to continue, or **No** to stop.
2. A table appears with two rows: [**L**](#32-glossary--l) (your current project and configuration) and [**R**](#32-glossary--r) (empty).
3. PTXprint opens the **Project** list for the **R** row so you can choose the secondary project.
4. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, **Two Column Layout** is ticked and greyed out. A diglot always uses two (or more) columns. The gutter (the space between the columns) and **Vertical Rule in Gutter** on the **Layout** tab now control the space and the line between the texts.

If you later untick the box, PTXprint does not turn the diglot off. Instead it opens the [**Save As Monoglot**](#10-diglot--save-as-monoglot) dialog (see below).

## 13.3 The texts table {#10-diglot--the-texts-table}

The table lists one row for each text. Left-click a cell to change it. Right-click anywhere in the table to open a menu. You can have up to 9 texts (codes L, R, A–G).

The columns are:

* **Code** – the letter that identifies this text (L, R, A, B …). L is always the primary text and cannot be changed. The cell is shaded with the background colour of that text, if one is set.
* **1|2** – which page of an open book the text goes on: **1** = the left page, **2** = the right page. For a normal side-by-side diglot, leave every text on **1**. Put texts on **2** only if you want them on the facing page (see [**Layout**](#10-diglot--layout) below).
* **Project** – the Paratext project for this text. You cannot change it for the L row.
* **Configuration** – which PTXprint configuration of that project to use. The list shows the configurations that exist for the project you chose. A project and configuration pair can only be used once in the table.
* [**Captions**](#s-c-pic-Captions) – tick to print this text's picture captions under shared pictures. The L text always shows its captions.
* **Font Size** and **Spacing** – the font size and line spacing (in pt; 1 pt is about 0.35 mm) for this text. These are the same values as **Font Size** and **Line Spacing** on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab of that text's configuration. Changing them here changes them there.
* **% Width** – how much of the page width this text takes. The values for all texts on the same page must add up to 100. If they do not, the numbers turn red and bold.
* **Weight** – how much this text counts when PTXprint decides where to line the texts up. Leave the values equal unless you have a reason to change them.

The right-click menu has these items:

* **Add a row/text** – adds another text (this makes a polyglot). Choose its **Project** and **Configuration** next.
* **Move Up** / **Move Down** – change the order of the extra texts. The L and R rows cannot be moved.
* **Copy Font Size to All** / **Copy Spacing to All** – copy the value of the selected row to every row.
* **Distribute Widths** – share the width evenly between all texts on the same page as the selected row.
* **Delete Row** – remove the selected text. The L and R rows cannot be deleted.
* **Edit Settings…** – switch the whole PTXprint window to the selected secondary text's configuration, so you can change its fonts and other settings (see [**Changing the settings of a secondary text**](#10-diglot--changing-the-settings-of-a-secondary-text) below). Not available for the L row.
* **Set Color…** – choose a light background colour (shading) behind this text's column. This can help readers find the right text.
* **Remove All Colors** – remove the shading from all texts.

Next to the table, a small picture shows how the texts will sit on the page, using the widths and colours from the table.

## 13.4 Layout {#10-diglot--layout}

The **Layout** text box describes where each text goes. PTXprint fills it in for you from the **1|2** column, so most people never need to type in it.

* Letters next to each other share a page, side by side. **LR** means L on the left and R on the right of every page.
* A comma starts the next page of the spread. **L,R** means L fills the left page and R fills the facing right page.
* A hyphen **-** is a page with no Bible text.

Every code in the table must appear in the layout, and L and R must always be there. If the layout has a problem, the preview shows a red **Layout Error** box with the reason, for example "Missing: A", "L or R missing", "Spaces not allowed" or "Comma required for multi-page spread". The check runs when you leave the box.

## 13.5 Merging mode {#10-diglot--merging-mode}

Before printing, PTXprint merges the texts into one file, in "chunks" that should line up across the columns. **Merging mode** chooses how the chunks are made:

* **Chapter Verse** – lines the texts up on chapters and verses. Only offered for a diglot (two texts).
* **Scored** – the default. It uses a scoring method and also tries to line up paragraphs where the verse numbers match. This usually gives the best result.
* **Scored (Chapter)** – like **Scored**, but always lines up at the start of each chapter.
* **Scored (Verse)** – like **Scored**, but lines up at every verse. This can leave many small gaps.

For a polyglot (three or more texts), only the three **Scored** options are offered.

## 13.6 Column widths and auto-balance {#10-diglot--column-widths-and-auto-balance}

Two texts rarely take the same amount of space. One language may need 20% more words than the other. If both columns are 50% wide, the shorter text has white space under every chunk. To fix this, give the longer text more width in the **% Width** column (for example 55 and 45), or make its font size or line spacing a little smaller.

The **Auto-calculate optimum widths of diglot columns** button does this for you. It prints the job 10 or more times, trying widths near the current ones, and keeps the widths that give the fewest pages. So select one short book on the main window before you click it. The button only works for a diglot with exactly two texts, and only when the **Print** button is available. When it has finished, the button is released, and you can use it again (for example after you change a font size).

## 13.7 Notes, headers and other options {#10-diglot--notes-headers-and-other-options}

* [**Separate Notes in Two Columns**](#10-diglot--separate-notes-in-two-columns) (ticked by default) keeps each text's footnotes under its own column. If you untick it, the footnotes of all texts are put together in one notes area, one after another. This can be useful when only one of the texts has footnotes.
* [**Vertical Rule in Notes Area**](#s-c-diglotNotesRule) draws a line between the separate notes columns. [**Join with Rule Above**](#s-c-diglotJoinVrule) makes this line meet the line between the text columns, so there is no small gap. The text-column line itself is **Vertical Rule in Gutter** on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.
* [**Adjust Center Header Based on Column Widths**](#s-c-diglotAdjCenter) moves the centre part of the header (and footer) so that it sits above the gutter, when the two columns have different widths.
* [**Use Serial Layout for These Books**](#s-t-diglotSerialBooks) lists books that should not be merged. For these books PTXprint prints the whole book in the primary text, then the whole book in the secondary text, one after the other. Use this for front matter, introductions, glossaries and other back matter. The default list is **FRT BAK GLO XXA XXB**.

## 13.8 Changing the settings of a secondary text {#10-diglot--changing-the-settings-of-a-secondary-text}

The look of each secondary text (fonts, font size, line spacing, footnote settings, styles, and so on) comes from its own configuration. To change it:

1. On the **Diglot** tab, right-click the row of that text and choose **Edit Settings…**.
2. The PTXprint window now shows the secondary project and configuration. The big **Print** button changes to **Return to Primary**. A small **Print** button appears next to it.
3. Change the settings you need, for example on the **Fonts+Scripts** tab or the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab.
4. If you want to check this text by itself, click the small **Print** button. It makes a PDF of the secondary text only.
5. Click **Return to Primary** to go back to the primary configuration. Then click **Print** to make the diglot PDF.

Some settings always come from the primary configuration, whatever the secondary configuration says. These include the page size, margins, header and footer positions, the footnote rule, where cross-references go, page breaks before chapter 1, book introductions and the outline, parallel passage references and the chapter range. The page border and the centre footer of the secondary text are also turned off. So change these in the primary configuration.

## 13.9 What happens to pictures, notes and headers {#10-diglot--what-happens-to-pictures-notes-and-headers}

**Pictures.** Pictures come from each text's own picture list. If both texts have the same picture file at the same verse, PTXprint prints it once. The primary caption is used, and the secondary caption is added if [**Captions**](#s-c-pic-Captions) is ticked for that text. If a picture is only in one text, or uses a different file, it is printed in that text's column. Pictures are not shared in the books listed in [**Use Serial Layout for These Books**](#s-t-diglotSerialBooks), because those books are printed one text after the other. There, each text keeps its own pictures and captions. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, the picture list shows the secondary caption in the **Sec.Caption** column, and pictures that belong only to a secondary text have the text's code after the book code in the anchor (for example **MATR 5.3**).

**Notes.** Whether a text has footnotes and cross-references depends on that text's own configuration (its [**Notes+Refs**](#s-lb-NotesRefs) settings). The layout of the notes area (separate or together, rules) is set on this tab.

**Headers and footers.** The headers and footers are set in the primary configuration, on the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab. When diglot is on, each header part (and the center footer) has a small drop-down with the code letter of one of the texts in the table above. Choose [**L**](#32-glossary--l) to use the primary text (its references and its font) for that part, [**R**](#32-glossary--r) for the secondary text, or, in a polyglot, any of the other letters. The list shows only the texts you have set up, with each letter's project. If [**Mirror Pages**](#s-c-mirrorpages) is ticked on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, the texts also swap sides on even pages, so each text stays on the same side relative to the binding.

**Front matter.** The [**Generate Front Matter**](#14-viewedit--generate-front-matter) dialog ([Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals)) offers a [**DIGLOT**](#s-lb-Diglot) template when diglot is on.

## 13.10 Auto Page Fill for diglots and polyglots (experimental) {#10-diglot--auto-page-fill-for-diglots-and-polyglots-experimental}

The **Auto Page Fill** tool in the PDF Preview window (see the chapter on the PDF Preview window) also works for a diglot or polyglot. When [**Diglot (or Polyglot)**](#s-c-diglot) is ticked, PTXprint uses a special version of the tool. It tries to fill each page, and it also tries to keep the texts side by side at the same height, so that each chunk ends at about the same line in every column. This version is new and experimental. Check the result carefully, and fix the pages it could not fill by hand.

On the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** sub-tab, in the **Automatic Page Filler** area, [**The cost of imbalance in a polyglot slice**](#s-s-pbpolyimbalance) sets how important it is that the columns end at the same height. A higher value makes the tool try harder to keep the columns even. A lower value lets it accept columns of different heights if the paragraphs look better. This setting is only used for diglots and polyglots.

## 13.11 Save As Monoglot {#10-diglot--save-as-monoglot}

You cannot just switch a diglot off, because that would lose all the diglot settings. When you untick [**Diglot (or Polyglot)**](#s-c-diglot), the **Save As Monoglot** dialog opens instead:

* Click **Cancel** to keep the diglot as it is.
* Or type a name for a new configuration and click **OK**. PTXprint saves a copy of the current settings under that name, with diglot turned off, and opens it. Your diglot configuration is left unchanged.

## 13.12 Common tasks {#10-diglot--common-tasks}

### Set up a diglot {#10-diglot--set-up-a-diglot}

1. Make sure both projects print well on their own. Each one needs a PTXprint configuration you are happy with (fonts, styles, notes).
2. Open the primary project. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, in the **Layout Configuration** area, click **Save As** and give the diglot its own configuration name (for example `Diglot`).
3. On the **Diglot** tab, tick [**Diglot (or Polyglot)**](#s-c-diglot). Click **Yes** in the message.
4. In the [**R**](#32-glossary--r) row, choose the secondary **Project**, then its **Configuration**.
5. Check that **% Width** is 50 and 50 (or another pair that adds up to 100).
6. Leave [**Merging mode**](#10-diglot--merging-mode) on **Scored**.
7. On the main window, choose one short book that exists in both projects. Click **Print**.
8. Look at the result. Then balance the widths (see below) and adjust the headers on the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab.

### Change the font of the secondary text {#10-diglot--change-the-font-of-the-secondary-text}

1. On the **Diglot** tab, right-click the [**R**](#32-glossary--r) row and choose **Edit Settings…**.
2. Go to the **Fonts+Scripts** tab and change the font.
3. Click **Return to Primary**.
4. Click **Print**.

To change only the font size or line spacing, you do not need to switch: type the new value in the **Font Size** or **Spacing** cell of that row.

### Balance the columns so there is less white space {#10-diglot--balance-the-columns-so-there-is-less-white-space}

1. Print a short book and see which column has the most white space.
2. Give the longer text more width: for example **% Width** 55 for L and 45 for R. Make sure the two numbers add up to 100.
3. Print again and compare the page count.
4. Or select one short book and click **Auto-calculate optimum widths of diglot columns**. Wait until it has finished all its print runs.

### Add a third text (polyglot) {#10-diglot--add-a-third-text-polyglot}

1. Right-click in the table and choose **Add a row/text**. A new row (code [**A**](#32-glossary--a)) appears.
2. Choose its **Project** and **Configuration**.
3. Right-click a row and choose **Distribute Widths**, so all three texts share the page.
4. Check that the [**Layout**](#10-diglot--layout) box contains all the codes (for example **LRA**).
5. Print.

### Put the two texts on facing pages {#10-diglot--put-the-two-texts-on-facing-pages}

1. In the [**R**](#32-glossary--r) row, change **1|2** to **2**.
2. Check that the [**Layout**](#10-diglot--layout) box now shows **L,R**.
3. Set **% Width** to 100 for each text (each one has a page to itself).
4. Print.

### Keep the introduction and glossary as whole books {#10-diglot--keep-the-introduction-and-glossary-as-whole-books}

1. In [**Use Serial Layout for These Books**](#s-t-diglotSerialBooks), type the book codes, with spaces between them, for example `FRT INT GLO BAK`.
2. Print. These books are printed one after the other (primary first, then secondary) instead of side by side.

### Shade the background of each text {#10-diglot--shade-the-background-of-each-text}

1. Right-click the row of a text and choose **Set Color…**.
2. Choose a light colour and click **OK**.
3. Repeat for the other texts if you want. To remove all shading, right-click and choose **Remove All Colors**.

### Turn a diglot back into a normal (single-text) configuration {#10-diglot--turn-a-diglot-back-into-a-normal-single-text-configuration}

1. Untick [**Diglot (or Polyglot)**](#s-c-diglot). The [**Save As Monoglot**](#10-diglot--save-as-monoglot) dialog opens.
2. Type a new configuration name (letters, numbers, `-`, `_` and brackets only, no spaces).
3. Click **OK**. PTXprint opens the new single-text configuration. The diglot configuration is still there if you need it again.

## 13.13 Common problems {#10-diglot--common-problems}

**The Print button is greyed out, or the status bar says "No Config found for diglot".**
The secondary row has no valid project or configuration. In the [**R**](#32-glossary--r) row (and any other rows), choose a **Project** and then a **Configuration**.

**Error: "These books are not available in the secondary diglot project".**
You selected a book that the secondary project does not have. Select only books that exist in every project. (Books listed in [**Use Serial Layout for These Books**](#s-t-diglotSerialBooks) are not checked.)

**Error: "Failed to merge texts due to a Syntax Error" (Diglot Merge Error).**
One of the texts has a marker error. Run the Basic Checks in Paratext for every project in the diglot. If you use a changes file (on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab), check that a rule there has not caused the error.

**The texts do not line up well, or there are big gaps under each chunk.**
Try another [**Merging mode**](#10-diglot--merging-mode) (for example **Scored (Chapter)** or **Chapter Verse**). Change the **% Width** so the longer text gets more space, or reduce its font size or line spacing. Try **Auto-calculate optimum widths of diglot columns**. To fill the pages after that, you can try the **Auto Page Fill** tool in the PDF Preview window (experimental for diglots; see above).

**The % Width numbers are red.**
The widths of the texts on one page do not add up to 100. Change them, or right-click and choose **Distribute Widths**.

**The layout preview shows a red "Layout Error".**
Read the message in the box. Usually a code is missing from the [**Layout**](#10-diglot--layout) box, or the **1|2** column does not match the layout (texts on page 2 must come after the comma). Change the **1|2** values and PTXprint will rebuild the layout.

**I cannot untick Diglot (or Polyglot).**
This is on purpose. PTXprint opens the [**Save As Monoglot**](#10-diglot--save-as-monoglot) dialog so your diglot settings are not lost. Give a new name and click **OK** to get a single-text configuration.

**Two Column Layout on the Layout tab is greyed out.**
A diglot always uses columns, so PTXprint ticks this box and locks it while diglot is on.

**I changed the secondary text's font (or margins) but nothing changed.**
Fonts and other text settings must be changed in the secondary configuration: use **Edit Settings…**, then **Return to Primary**. Page size, margins, header positions and similar page settings always come from the primary configuration, so change those there.

**The big button says "Return to Primary" instead of "Print".**
You are looking at a secondary configuration (after **Edit Settings…**). Click **Return to Primary**, then **Print**. The small **Print** button prints only the secondary text.

**The secondary text has no footnotes.**
Footnotes and cross-references are switched on or off in each text's own configuration. Use **Edit Settings…** for that text and check its notes settings.

**The secondary caption is missing under a picture.**
Tick [**Captions**](#s-c-pic-Captions) in that text's row. Also check that both texts use the same picture file at the same verse; otherwise PTXprint treats them as two different pictures. In books listed in **Use Serial Layout for These Books**, pictures are not shared, so each text shows only its own caption.

**A picture is printed twice.**
The two texts probably have the same picture with a different file name or at a different verse. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, make the entries match, or remove the picture from one text.

**The header shows the references of only one text.**
On the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab, choose a text letter in the drop-down in front of each part of the header. For example, use [**L**](#32-glossary--l) for the left part and **R** for the right part. If a polyglot text's part stays empty, check that its book has an `\h` line: the reference takes the book name from it.

**The primary text is on the left on some pages and on the right on others.**
[**Mirror Pages**](#s-c-mirrorpages) is ticked on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab. With it, the columns swap on even pages. Untick it if you want the primary text always on the left.

**The Auto-calculate button is greyed out.**
It only works with exactly two texts, and only when printing is possible. (In older versions the button could stay pressed after one run until PTXprint was restarted. This is fixed.)

**The Chapter Verse merging mode is missing.**
You have three or more texts. Only the **Scored** modes work for a polyglot.

**The Diglot tab is missing.**
The tab is only shown in the **Regular** and **Full** views. Change the view level.

## 13.14 Settings reference {#10-diglot--settings-reference}

### Save As Monoglot... (dialog) {#10-diglot--save-as-monoglot-dialog}

#### OK {#s-btn-disableDiglot-ok}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Saves the current settings under the new name with diglot turned off, and opens that new configuration. The diglot configuration is not changed. Greyed out until you type a valid new name.

#### Cancel {#s-btn-disableDiglot-cancel}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Closes the dialog. The configuration stays a diglot and nothing is changed.

#### Save as a new Configuration (which will be a monoglot) – Enter a name for the configuration to be saved {#s-t-newMonoglotConfigName}

Text box · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Enter a name for the configuration to be saved.
>
> Note that only Roman/Latin names are supported using: a-z A-Z, 0-9, parentheses, underscores and hyphens. Spaces are not permitted.

If the name is not allowed, or a configuration with that name already exists, a message appears and **OK** stays greyed out.

### Diglot {#10-diglot--diglot}

#### Diglot (or Polyglot) {#s-c-diglot}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Enable diglot or discript publication · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> A Diglot publication contains two languages, or scripts, or texts.
>
> A Polyglot contains more than two. Right-click in the table below to add other texts to the list.
>
> Tip: use Save As first. Unticking this later does not simply switch back; it offers to save a single-text copy of the configuration under a new name.

The open configuration becomes the primary (L) text. Make a separate configuration with **Save As** (on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab) first. When it is ticked, **Two Column Layout** on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab is ticked and locked.

#### Diglot (or Polyglot) {#10-diglot--diglot-or-polyglot-2}

##### Use Default Header Settings for Diglot {#s-c-diglotHeaders}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Diglot: Use default header settings · Needs: [“Diglot (or Polyglot)”](#s-c-diglot) · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> Checking this option will override the header settings and place the Reference Ranges on the outer edges and Page Number in (or near) the middle.

This checkbox is normally hidden. In this version it is saved with the configuration but it does not change the printed headers. Set the headers on the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab instead, using the text letter drop-down in front of each part.

##### Adjust Center Header Based on Column Widths {#s-c-diglotAdjCenter}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Diglot: Adjust center header horizontal position · Needs: [“Diglot (or Polyglot)”](#s-c-diglot) · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> If the column widths of the two sides of the diglot are unequal, PTXprint can ensure that the content of the center header matches the position of the gutter (space between the two different columns).

The centre header and footer move towards the gutter instead of staying in the middle of the page. With equal widths it makes no difference.

##### Separate Notes in Two Columns {#s-c-diglotSeparateNotes}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Diglot: Keep notes in distinct columns · Needs: [“Diglot (or Polyglot)”](#s-c-diglot) · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> If this option is disabled, the footnotes from both sides of the diglot get merged together and are interspersed one after the other.
>
> Depending on the scripts and text direction, this may or may not be desirable. If in doubt, leave this option checked ON.

Untick it when only one text has notes; the notes then go in one shared area, in the order they are met. Unticking it greys out [**Vertical Rule in Notes Area**](#s-c-diglotNotesRule) and [**Join with Rule Above**](#s-c-diglotJoinVrule).

##### Layout {#s-t-layout}

Text box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Diglot (or Polyglot)”](#s-c-diglot) · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> The Layout string describes how the various texts should appear on the page(s).
>
> All of the texts listed in the table above must be mentioned. The comma represents the next page. A forward slash / will put one text under the other on the same page (this is still to come and cannot be used yet).

PTXprint fills this in from the **1|2** column of the table, so you seldom need to type here. Letters together share a page; a comma starts the facing page; a hyphen is a page with no text. Spaces are not allowed. If you use `/`, PTXprint reports "Complex layouts are not yet supported".

##### Merging mode – Diglot/Polyglot: Merging Mode {#s-fcb-diglotMerge}

Drop-down list · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Choices: Chapter Verse | Scored | Scored (Chapter) | Scored (Verse) · Needs: [“Diglot (or Polyglot)”](#s-c-diglot) · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> When the different texts of a diglot are merged, there are various algorithms which may be used to obtain the best overall result:
>
> \* Chapter Verse - aligns on chapters and verses
>
> \* Scored - an alternative algorithm which uses weighted scores\
> and tries to align paragraphs when the verse numbers match
>
> \* Scored (Chapter) - as a minimum, forces alignment at chapter breaks
>
> \* Scored (Verse) - as a minimum, forces alignment at each verse, which\
> can result in a lot of breaks!
>
> Note that for polyglots, only the Scored options are available to be used.

Start with **Scored**. If chapters drift out of line, try **Scored (Chapter)**. Use **Scored (Verse)** only when other modes fail, because it can leave many gaps.

##### When the different texts of a diglot are merged, there are v... {#10-diglot--when-the-different-texts-of-a-diglot-are-merged-there-are-v}

Text box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Diglot (or Polyglot)”](#s-c-diglot) · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> When the different texts of a diglot are merged, there are various algorithms which may be used to obtain the best overall result:
>
> \* Chapter Verse - aligns on chapters and verses
>
> \* Scored - an alternative algorithm which uses weighted scores\
> and tries to align paragraphs when the verse numbers match
>
> \* Scored (Chapter) - as a minimum, forces alignment at chapter breaks
>
> \* Scored (Verse) - as a minimum, forces alignment at each verse, which\
> can result in a lot of breaks!
>
> Note that for polyglots, only the Scored options are available to be used.

##### Auto-calculate optimum widths of diglot columns {#s-btn-adjust-diglot}

Toggle button (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Diglot (or Polyglot)”](#s-c-diglot) · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> Auto calculate primary percentage by trying to reduce the page count. This will run your print job up to 10 times or more, so choose a small book to run on. It will attempt to find the best balance of column widths near to the current % Width values. Only available for a diglot with two texts.

It changes only the **% Width** of the L and R rows. It is greyed out for polyglots and when printing is not possible. When the runs are finished (or if an error stops them), the button is released, so you can click it again.

##### Use Serial Layout for These Books – List of diglot books not to be merged, to come one after the other {#s-t-diglotSerialBooks}

Text box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Diglot (or Polyglot)”](#s-c-diglot) · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> Some books (e.g. Introduction, Glossary, Back Matter, etc.) in a diglot publication should not be merged to appear side-by-side, but instead need to occur one after the other.
>
> Add the 3-letter book codes for any books that should not be merged. These will appear one after the other.

Separate the codes with spaces. The primary version is printed in full, then the secondary version. The default is **FRT BAK GLO XXA XXB**. Pictures in these books are not shared between the texts: each text keeps its own pictures and captions.

##### Separate Notes in Two Columns {#10-diglot--separate-notes-in-two-columns}

###### Vertical Rule in Notes Area {#s-c-diglotNotesRule}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Diglot: Vertical rule in notes area · Needs: [“Separate Notes in Two Columns”](#10-diglot--separate-notes-in-two-columns), [“Diglot (or Polyglot)”](#s-c-diglot) · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> Add a vertical rule between the two sides of the notes area of the diglot.

Often used together with **Vertical Rule in Gutter** on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, which draws the line between the text columns.

###### Join with Rule Above {#s-c-diglotJoinVrule}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Diglot: Join notes rule with gutter rule · Needs: [“Separate Notes in Two Columns”](#10-diglot--separate-notes-in-two-columns), [“Vertical Rule in Notes Area”](#s-c-diglotNotesRule), [“Diglot (or Polyglot)”](#s-c-diglot) · Shown when: “Diglot (or Polyglot)”

> To prevent a small gap in the line allow the vertical line to extend down into the notes area.

Makes one continuous line from the gutter line down through the notes area.

# 14. Tabs+Borders tab {#ch-11-tabsborders}

## 14.1 What this tab is for {#11-tabsborders--what-this-tab-is-for}

This tab adds two kinds of decoration:

* [**Thumb Tabs**](#s-c-thumbtabs) – coloured blocks at the outer edge of the page, with a short book name in them. When the book is closed, the reader sees the blocks on the edge of the paper and can open the book near the right Bible book. They are useful in long publications such as a whole Bible or a New Testament.
* [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments) – a border around the page or the text, a graphic behind section headings, a decoration at the end of each book, decorated verse numbers, and borders around book titles. Some cultures value such decoration highly in Scripture publications.

Each area is collapsed until you tick its checkbox; until then you only see a short description. The tab name shows **Tabs** and [**Borders**](#s-btn-sbBorders), and each word turns blue when that feature is on. The tab is shown in the **Regular** and **Full** views.

This chapter also describes the **Border Settings** dialog, which sets the look of a border (lines, ornaments, colours and padding). You open it from the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab with the **Borders...** button.

"pt" means point; 1 pt is about 0.35 mm. Thumb tab sizes are in mm.

## 14.2 Thumb Tabs {#11-tabsborders--thumb-tabs}

**Where the tabs go.** Each Scripture book gets a tab position, counting down from the top of the page: the first book at position 1 (top), the next at position 2, and so on. When the positions run out, the next book starts again at the top. Front matter, glossaries and other non-Scripture books get no tab. Positions are worked out from all the books in the multiple-book list on the main window, even if you print only one book. So the tab for Mark is in the same place whether you print the whole NT or only Mark.

**Size.** For normal tabs, [**Height**](#s-s-thumbheight) is the size along the page edge and **Length** is how far the tab reaches in from the edge. For rotated tabs it is the other way round.

[**Number of Tab Positions**](#s-s-thumbtabs) is how many tabs fit down the page. PTXprint recalculates it from the page height, the top and bottom margins and the tab size whenever these change. Bigger = tabs overlap; smaller = tabs spread apart.

**Grouped Tabs.** Many Bible books are short, so giving each its own position would need too many positions. Neighbouring short books can share one position, and each still has its own name in the tab. The **Grouped Tabs** button restores PTXprint's default groups.

[**Restart Tabs at MAT**](#s-c-thumbrestart) starts a new cycle at Matthew, so the New Testament tabs start again at the top.

[**Rotate Tabs**](#s-c-thumbrotate) turns the text to run along the page edge (good for narrow margins and longer names). The drop-down list next to it chooses which way the text faces on left and right pages. The preview on the tab shows facing pages.

[**Only Show on Odd Pages**](#s-c-tabsOddOnly) is for thin paper, so a tab on the back of the page does not show through.

**Tab text and colour.** By default the tab text is the short book name from each book's `\toc3` line. [**Tab Color**](#s-col-thumbback) sets only the block colour. The text colour, font and size come from the style: click [**Edit Style**](#s-lb-style-toc3) to change them on the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab. Tabs usually use a dark block with white or light text.

The [**\toc3**](#s-r-thumbText-toc3) and [**\zthumbtab**](#s-r-thumbText-zthumbtab) options choose where the tab text comes from. If the **Table of Contents** on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab is on but does not use `\toc3`, PTXprint selects **\zthumbtab** and greys out both options.

## 14.3 Ornamental Decorations {#11-tabsborders--ornamental-decorations}

Tick each kind of decoration you want. A file name next to a **Select...** button shows which graphic is used. Choosing a file ticks that decoration's checkbox for you. The **Select...** buttons open PTXprint's own border-art folder, but you can pick a PDF file from anywhere.

### Section Headings {#11-tabsborders--section-headings}

* **PDF border (Legacy)** – a PDF graphic behind each `\s`, `\s1` and `\s2` heading. **Scale**: 1 = the graphic's own size. **Shift**: in pt, positive = up, negative = down. The graphic does not grow with the heading, so make sure every heading fits, also two-line headings. You may need more space before and after headings on the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab.
* **Dynamic Border** – a box around each heading block that grows and shrinks with the heading. It is controlled by the special style `cat:headingsbox|esb`; the link opens it on the **Styles** tab, where you set its background colour and border ([**Borders...**](#s-btn-sbBorders) button).

### Border {#11-tabsborders--border}

* **PDF border (Legacy)** – a PDF graphic (for example a frame) on every page. It is stretched to the full page if [**Full page**](#s-c-borderPageWide) is ticked, otherwise to the page size without the binding gutter.
* **Dynamic Border** – a border around the Bible text on each page. Introductions, footnotes and other peripheral material are outside it. It can be plain, double or ornamental. It is controlled by the `textborder` style ([**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab, **Other** category); change it with the [**Borders...**](#s-btn-sbBorders) button in **Sidebar Settings**.
* [**Page Border**](#s-r-border-page) – meant to place a border of the same size on every page, whatever the content, controlled by the `\pageborder` style. If you do not get the result you want, use **Dynamic Border** or **PDF border (Legacy)**.

A border takes space, so you will probably need larger margins on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab so it does not touch the text or the paper edge.

### End of Book Decoration {#11-tabsborders--end-of-book-decoration}

A small graphic after the last verse of each Scripture book. PTXprint suggests its own `decoration.pdf`.

### Verse Number Decorator {#11-tabsborders--verse-number-decorator}

* [**End of Ayah**](#s-r-decorator-ayah) – the verse number inside the font's "End of Ayah" character (U+06DD), common in Arabic script. The font must contain this character. [**Move Ayah**](#s-c-decorator-endayah) moves the decorated number to the end of the verse; the `\vp` link opens the style for the moved numbers.
* [**Verse Border Graphic**](#s-r-decorator-file) – a small PDF graphic (for example a star) behind each verse number, adjusted with **Scale** and **Shift** (pt, positive = up).

The `\v` link opens the verse number style. You may need a smaller font size or another colour so the numbers fit inside the decoration.

### Book Title Borders {#11-tabsborders--book-title-borders}

A border around the book title (`\mt1` and `\mt2`), controlled by the special style `cat:titlebox|esb`. The link opens it on the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab to change its colours and border.

## 14.4 Border Settings dialog {#11-tabsborders--border-settings-dialog}

The dialog belongs to a style on the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab. To open it, select the style (for example a sidebar style, `textborder`, `cat:headingsbox|esb` or `cat:titlebox|esb`), open **Sidebar Settings**, and click [**Borders...**](#s-btn-sbBorders). **OK** saves the changes in that style; **Cancel** leaves the style as it was.

**Borders** area:

* [**Type of Border**](#s-fcb-sbBorderStyle) – **None**, **Plain (single)** (one line), **Double** (two lines) or **Ornamental** (a pattern of ornaments).
* **Left**, **Right**, **Top**, **Bottom**, **Inner**, **Outer** – which sides get a border. Use **Inner**/**Outer** if the border should follow the binding (inner = near the spine). Ticking **Inner** or **Outer** unticks **Left** and **Right**, and the other way round.
* **Border Width**, **Line Thickness**, [**Line Color**](#s-col-sbBorderColor), [**Fill Color**](#s-col-sbBorderFillColor), and **Select Ornamental Border** (the pattern, only for **Ornamental**) – see the control notes. [**Ornamental Border Style**](#s-lb-openOrnamentsCatalog) opens the ornaments catalogue (a PDF).

**Padding** area, on two tabs:

* **Box** – space between the edge of the box (its background colour) and the text inside it.
* **Border** – space between the inside edge of the border and the box inside it.

Each tab has four values in a cross: top, bottom, left (or inner) and right (or outer), in pt. [**Uniform Box Padding**](#s-c-boxPadSymmetrical) / [**Uniform Border Padding**](#s-c-bdrPadSymmetrical) use the top value for all four sides and grey out the other three. Negative values are allowed. The picture in the dialog shows the effect.

## 14.5 Common tasks {#11-tabsborders--common-tasks}

### Add thumb tabs to a Bible or New Testament {#11-tabsborders--add-thumb-tabs-to-a-bible-or-new-testament}

1. On the main window, select all the books in the multiple-book list.
2. On the **Tabs+Borders** tab, tick [**Thumb Tabs**](#s-c-thumbtabs).
3. Set [**Height**](#s-s-thumbheight) and **Length** (for example 8 mm and 15 mm).
4. Choose a dark [**Tab Color**](#s-col-thumbback).
5. Click [**Edit Style**](#s-lb-style-toc3) and set a light text colour (for example white).
6. Print and look at the outer edge of the pages.

### Let short books share a tab position {#11-tabsborders--let-short-books-share-a-tab-position}

1. Tick [**Thumb Tabs**](#s-c-thumbtabs).
2. Click the **Grouped Tabs** button for the default groups, or type your own in the **Grouped Tabs** box, for example `PHM TIT; 1JN 2JN 3JN JUD`.
3. Print. Each group uses one position, but each book keeps its own name.

### Make the text in the tabs run along the page edge {#11-tabsborders--make-the-text-in-the-tabs-run-along-the-page-edge}

1. Tick [**Rotate Tabs**](#s-c-thumbrotate).
2. In the drop-down list next to it, choose how the text faces, for example **Each Facing Outward**.
3. Check the preview on the tab, then print.

### Start the New Testament tabs at the top again {#11-tabsborders--start-the-new-testament-tabs-at-the-top-again}

Tick [**Restart Tabs at MAT**](#s-c-thumbrestart) and print.

### Put a decorative border around the Bible text {#11-tabsborders--put-a-decorative-border-around-the-bible-text}

1. Tick [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments), then **Border**, and choose **Dynamic Border**.
2. On the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab, select the `textborder` style (in the **Other** category).
3. Open **Sidebar Settings** and click [**Borders...**](#s-btn-sbBorders).
4. Choose the [**Type of Border**](#s-fcb-sbBorderStyle) (for example **Ornamental**), the ornament, the **Border Width** (at least 10 pt for ornaments) and the colours. Click **OK**.
5. On the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab, make the margins larger if the border is too close to the text or the paper edge.
6. Print.

### Use a ready-made PDF frame on every page {#11-tabsborders--use-a-ready-made-pdf-frame-on-every-page}

1. Tick [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments), then **Border**.
2. Choose **PDF border (Legacy)**, click **Select...** and choose the PDF file.
3. Tick [**Full page**](#s-c-borderPageWide) if the frame should cover the whole page.
4. Make the margins larger on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab if needed, then print.

### Decorate the verse numbers {#11-tabsborders--decorate-the-verse-numbers}

1. Tick [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments), then [**Verse Number Decorator**](#s-c-inclVerseDecorator).
2. Choose [**Verse Border Graphic**](#s-r-decorator-file) and click **Select...** to choose a small PDF graphic. (For Arabic script, you can choose [**End of Ayah**](#s-r-decorator-ayah) instead.)
3. Print. If the number does not fit, change **Scale** and **Shift**, or click the `\v` link to make the verse numbers smaller.

### Add a graphic at the end of each book {#11-tabsborders--add-a-graphic-at-the-end-of-each-book}

1. Tick [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments), then [**End of Book Decoration**](#s-c-inclEndOfBook).
2. Click **Select...**, choose a PDF graphic, and print.

### Put a border around book titles or section headings {#11-tabsborders--put-a-border-around-book-titles-or-section-headings}

1. Tick [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments).
2. Tick [**Book Title Borders**](#s-c-inclTitleBorders), or tick [**Section Headings**](#s-c-inclSectionHeader) and choose **Dynamic Border**.
3. Click the style link (`cat:titlebox|esb` or `cat:headingsbox|esb`). The [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab opens with that style selected.
4. Change the background colour, and click [**Borders...**](#s-btn-sbBorders) in **Sidebar Settings** to change the border.
5. Print.

## 14.6 Common problems {#11-tabsborders--common-problems}

**I cannot see the thumb tab or ornament settings.**
Tick [**Thumb Tabs**](#s-c-thumbtabs) or [**Ornamental Decorations**](#s-c-useOrnaments). If the whole tab is missing, change the view level to **Regular** or **Full**.

**The thumb tabs overlap each other, or there are big gaps between them.**
Change [**Number of Tab Positions**](#s-s-thumbtabs) (larger = closer and may overlap, smaller = further apart), or change [**Height**](#s-s-thumbheight) (or **Length** for rotated tabs). Group short books in **Grouped Tabs**, or tick [**Restart Tabs at MAT**](#s-c-thumbrestart).

**My value for Number of Tab Positions keeps changing.**
PTXprint recalculates it whenever the tab size, page size or margins change. Set those first, then adjust this number last.

**The thumb tab is blank.**
The book has no `\toc3` line, or it has an empty `\zthumbtab` line. If the table of contents does not use `\toc3`, the `\toc3` text is removed and cannot be used for the tabs. On the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, include `\toc3` in the table of contents, or add the tab text with `\zthumbtab` in the book (in Paratext).

**The \toc3 and \zthumbtab options are greyed out.**
The table of contents on the **Peripherals** tab is on but does not use `\toc3`. Tick `\toc3` there.

**When I print one book, its tab is not at the top.**
This is on purpose: positions come from all the books in the multiple-book list, so each tab stays in the same place in every print.

**I cannot change the colour of the tab text with Tab Color.**
[**Tab Color**](#s-col-thumbback) sets only the block. Click [**Edit Style**](#s-lb-style-toc3) and change the text colour there.

**Message: "Warning: Could not locate decorative PDF(s)".**
A decoration is ticked but its PDF file is missing or was moved. Choose the file again with that decoration's **Select...** button, or untick the decoration.

**The border touches or covers the text.**
Make the margins larger on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab. For a dynamic border, also increase the padding in the **Border Settings** dialog.

**The ornamental border looks broken or squashed.**
Make the **Border Width** at least 10 pt in the **Border Settings** dialog.

**The section heading graphic does not fit the heading.**
Change **Scale** and **Shift**. If headings are sometimes two lines long, use **Dynamic Border** instead of **PDF border (Legacy)**.

**The decorated verse numbers show empty boxes.**
With [**End of Ayah**](#s-r-decorator-ayah), the font does not have the End of Ayah character (U+06DD). Choose a font that has it, or use [**Verse Border Graphic**](#s-r-decorator-file).

**The verse number does not fit inside the verse graphic.**
Increase **Scale**, adjust **Shift**, or click the `\v` link and make the verse number font smaller.

**A Select... button or a Shift/Scale box is greyed out.**
Choose **PDF border (Legacy)** or **Verse Border Graphic** first.

**Clicking the \pageborder link does nothing.**
This link does not open the style. Go to the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab and select the page border style yourself. (The [**\textborder**](#s-lb-style-textborder) link does open the `textborder` style.)

## 14.7 Settings reference {#11-tabsborders--settings-reference}

### Border Settings (dialog) {#11-tabsborders--border-settings-dialog-2}

#### OK {#s-btn-border-ok}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Saves the border settings in the selected style and closes the dialog.

#### Cancel {#s-btn-border-cancel}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Closes the dialog without changing the style.

#### Borders {#11-tabsborders--borders}

##### Left – Borders dialog: Show LEFT border {#s-c-sbBorder-lhs}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views

Ticking it unticks **Inner** and **Outer**. Use **Left** and **Right** when the border does not need to follow the binding.

##### Right {#s-c-sbBorder-rhs}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Borders dialog: Show RIGHT border

Ticking it unticks **Inner** and **Outer**.

##### Top {#s-c-sbBorder-top}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Borders dialog: Show TOP border

Draws the border along the top.

##### Bottom {#s-c-sbBorder-bot}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Borders dialog: Show BOTTOM border

Draws the border along the bottom.

##### Outer {#s-c-sbBorder-out}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Borders dialog: Show OUTER border

Away from the spine. Ticking it unticks **Left** and **Right**.

##### Inner – Borders dialog: Show INNER border {#s-c-sbBorder-inn}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views

Near the spine, so it changes between left and right pages. Ticking it unticks **Left** and **Right**.

##### Border Width (pt) – Borders dialog: Border width {#s-s-sbBorderWidth}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: 0.1–200 (default 2)

> Specify how wide the border should be. Note that for ornamental borders this value needs to be at least 10pt.

For **Plain** this is the thickness of the line.

##### Line Color – Borders dialog: Border line color {#s-col-sbBorderColor}

Colour picker · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Sets the line color for this border.

The colour of the border lines.

##### Type of Border – Borders dialog: Border type {#s-fcb-sbBorderStyle}

Drop-down list · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Choices: None | Plain (single) | Double | Ornamental

> None, a plain (single) line, a double line, or an ornamental pattern.

With **None**, most other settings in the dialog are greyed out. **Line Thickness** and [**Fill Color**](#s-col-sbBorderFillColor) are only used for **Double** and **Ornamental**; the ornament list only for **Ornamental**.

##### Borders dialog: Ornamental border {#s-fcb-sbBorderOrnament}

Drop-down list · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Choices: Han1 | Han2 | Han3 | Han4 | Han5 | Vectorian1 | Vectorian2 | Vectorian3 | Vectorian4 | v85 | v85r | v85out | v86c | v86out | v88 | v88r | v88c | v88out

> A selection of ornamental borders are available to choose from, or a custom-made border may be applied.

**Han** patterns are traditional Chinese-style designs; **Vectorian** and [**v…**](#32-glossary--v) patterns are Victorian-style. See them in the catalogue ([**Ornamental Border Style**](#s-lb-openOrnamentsCatalog) link). Only available when [**Type of Border**](#s-fcb-sbBorderStyle) is **Ornamental**.

##### Fill Color – Borders dialog: Border fill color {#s-col-sbBorderFillColor}

Colour picker · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Sets the fill color for this border.

Fills a **Double** or **Ornamental** border. Greyed out for **Plain (single)**.

##### Ornamental Border Style {#s-lb-openOrnamentsCatalog}

Link · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Show the Ornaments Catalog

> Click to open a PDF containing a catalog of the various Ornamental Borders (pgs 4-7).

Pages 4–7 show the ornamental borders in the list.

##### Line Thickness (pt) – Borders dialog: Border Line Thickness {#s-s-sbBorderLineWidth}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Specify the thickness of the lines which make up the border.

For **Double** and **Ornamental** borders (default 0.3 pt). Greyed out for **Plain (single)**.

#### Padding {#11-tabsborders--padding}

##### Box {#11-tabsborders--box}

###### All/Top (pt) {#11-tabsborders--all-top-pt}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Top padding (pts). When Uniform Box Padding is ticked, this value is used for all four sides.

###### Borders dialog: Box padding bottom {#s-s-sbBoxPadB}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: -200–200 (default 8) · Greyed out by: [“Uniform Box Padding”](#s-c-boxPadSymmetrical)

> The space (pts) between the edge of background box (or figure, if any) and the edge of the text in the box.

Bottom padding of the box.

###### Bottom (pt) – Borders dialog: Box padding right {#s-s-sbBoxPadR}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: -200–200 (default 8) · Greyed out by: [“Uniform Box Padding”](#s-c-boxPadSymmetrical)

> The space (pts) between the edge of background box (or figure, if any) and the edge of the text in the box.
>
> The vertical space (pts) between the top/bottom borders (if any) and the text contained within the box.

Right (or outer) padding of the box.

###### Left/Inner (pt) – Borders dialog: Box padding top {#s-s-sbBoxPadT}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: -200–200 (default 8)

> The space (pts) between the edge of background box (or figure, if any) and the edge of the text in the box.
>
> The horizontal space (pts) between the left/right borders (if any) and the text contained within the box.

Space between the top edge of the box and the text. With [**Uniform Box Padding**](#s-c-boxPadSymmetrical) it is used for all four sides.

###### Borders dialog: Box padding left {#s-s-sbBoxPadL}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: -200–200 (default 8) · Greyed out by: [“Uniform Box Padding”](#s-c-boxPadSymmetrical)

> The space (pts) between the edge of background box (or figure, if any) and the edge of the text in the box.

Left (or inner) padding of the box.

###### Right/Outer (pt) {#11-tabsborders--right-outer-pt}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> The horizontal space (pts) between the left/right borders (if any) and the text contained within the box.

###### Uniform Box Padding {#s-c-boxPadSymmetrical}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Use the same value for the Top, Bottom, Left, and Right padding.

Greys out the bottom, left and right boxes.

##### Border {#11-tabsborders--border-2}

###### All/Top (pt) {#11-tabsborders--all-top-pt-2}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Top padding (pts). When Uniform Border Padding is ticked, this value is used for all four sides.

###### Borders dialog: Border padding bottom {#s-s-sbBdrPadB}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: -200–200 (default 8) · Greyed out by: [“Uniform Border Padding”](#s-c-bdrPadSymmetrical)

> The space between the inside edge of the border and the outside edge of the box inside it.

Bottom padding between the border and the box.

###### Bottom (pt) – Borders dialog: Border padding right {#s-s-sbBdrPadR}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: -200–200 (default 8) · Greyed out by: [“Uniform Border Padding”](#s-c-bdrPadSymmetrical)

> The space between the inside edge of the border and the outside edge of the box inside it.
>
> The vertical space (pts) between the top/bottom borders (if any) and the text contained within the box.

Right (or outer) padding between the border and the box.

###### Left/Inner (pt) – Borders dialog: Border padding top {#s-s-sbBdrPadT}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: -200–200 (default 8)

> The space between the inside edge of the border and the outside edge of the box inside it.
>
> The horizontal space (pts) between the left/right borders (if any) and the text contained within the box.

Top padding between the border and the box. With [**Uniform Border Padding**](#s-c-bdrPadSymmetrical) it is used for all four sides. A negative value makes the box reach under the border.

###### Borders dialog: Border padding left {#s-s-sbBdrPadL}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: -200–200 (default 8) · Greyed out by: [“Uniform Border Padding”](#s-c-bdrPadSymmetrical)

> The space between the inside edge of the border and the outside edge of the box inside it.

Left (or inner) padding between the border and the box.

###### Right/Outer (pt) {#11-tabsborders--right-outer-pt-2}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> The horizontal space (pts) between the left/right borders (if any) and the text contained within the box.

###### Uniform Border Padding {#s-c-bdrPadSymmetrical}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Use the same value for the Top, Bottom, Left, and Right padding.

Greys out the bottom, left and right boxes.

### Tabs+Borders {#11-tabsborders--tabs-borders}

#### Thumb Tabs {#s-c-thumbtabs}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Enable thumb tabs · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> Thumb Tabs are sometimes used in longer publications to help the user find a scripture book more easily. By default these use the \toc3 element in a USFM file to provide the text for the tab. Note: If only a single book is currently selected, it will place the Thumb Tab relative to ALL the books listed in the multiple book list.

Only Scripture books get tabs. Thumb tabs are printed to the edge of the paper, so they need a printer that can print or trim to the edge.

#### Ornamental Decorations {#s-c-useOrnaments}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Ornamental Decorations: Enable decorative borders, rules and verses · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> Enable this option to make use of ornamental borders, rules & verses.
>
> Some cultures place a high value on such decorative features in scripture publications.

Most decorations need extra space, so check the margins and heading spacing after you print.

#### Thumb Tabs {#11-tabsborders--thumb-tabs-2}

##### Height – Thumb tabs: Height {#s-s-thumbheight}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: 3–20 (default 8) · Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> The height of the Thumb Tab measured in millimeters (mm).

Normal tabs: size along the page edge. Rotated tabs: how far the tab reaches in. Changing it recalculates [**Number of Tab Positions**](#s-s-thumbtabs) (for normal tabs).

##### Tab Color – Thumb tabs: Tab color {#s-col-thumbback}

Colour picker · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> The background color of the tabs. Use a dark color here and set the light text color with the Edit Style link.
>
> Thumb Tabs usually use a dark color for the background with a light color (or white) for the foreground text.
>
> The background color is set here, but the foreground text color needs to be set by clicking the Edit Style link.

A dark colour shows well on the edge of the closed book.

##### Rotate Tabs {#s-c-thumbrotate}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Thumb tabs: Rotate tabs · Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> Rotates the tabs so that the text runs along the edge of the page. This works well for narrow margins, but may result in fewer tab positions per page.

Allows longer names in narrow margins. When ticked, the orientation list next to it becomes available.

##### Number of Tab Positions – Thumb tabs: Number of tab positions {#s-s-thumbtabs}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> How many tabs can there be down a page. This is automatically calculated from the Height (or Length when rotated), Page size and Margins. If any of these change then this value will be updated. Increasing it, makes tabs overlap. Reducing it spreads them apart.

PTXprint overwrites your value when the page height, margins or tab size change. After the last position, the next book starts again at the top.

##### Length – Thumb tabs: Length {#s-s-thumblength}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: 3–40 (default 15) · Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> The length of the Thumb Tab measured in millimeters (mm).

Normal tabs: how far the tab reaches in; make it long enough for the longest book name. Rotated tabs: size along the page edge. Changing it recalculates [**Number of Tab Positions**](#s-s-thumbtabs) (for rotated tabs).

##### Grouped Tabs – Thumb tabs: Tabs grouped by books {#s-t-thumbgroups}

Text box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> List book IDs of short books to be grouped together at the same tab position. Use spaces between book IDs, and use ; to separate groups. There is no need to list all the book IDs here - only the special ones which need to share the same tab position.
>
> For example: PHM TIT; 1JN 2JN 3JN JUD
>
> When several shorter adjacent books occur, it is common to group them together to use the same tab position (but still have differently named tabs).

Books not listed get their own position.

##### Length – Thumb tabs: Rotate options {#s-fcb-rotateTabs}

Drop-down list · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Choices: Each Facing Outward | Each Facing Inward | Rotate Both Anticlockwise | Rotate Both Clockwise · Needs: [“Rotate Tabs”](#s-c-thumbrotate), [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> If you choose to Rotate the tabs, there are various options as to how these should be oriented. The preview (right) will show how these will appear on facing pages.

Outward and inward face opposite ways on left and right pages; the other two turn both pages the same way.

##### Restart Tabs at MAT {#s-c-thumbrestart}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Thumb tabs: Restart tabs at New Testament · Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> Normally books will follow sequentially and if the next tab would be off the bottom of the page, then it will be set to the top for a new cycle of tabs. Setting this starts a new cycle at the start of the New Testament (Matthew).

Use it in a whole Bible, so the New Testament has its own run of tabs.

##### Grouped Tabs – Thumb tabs: Reload default book groups {#s-btn-resetTabGroups}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> Clicking this button will replace the Grouped Tabs list with the default groups.

The default groups include `RUT 1SA`, the Minor Prophets in two groups, and the short letters. Any groups you typed are lost.

##### \toc3 {#s-r-thumbText-toc3}

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Thumb tabs: Use \toc3 text · Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> By default, Thumb Tabs use the content and styling of the \toc3 marker.
>
> Note that this setting is interconnected with the Table of Contents settings on the [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals). If \toc3 is not included in the ToC, then this option will be disabled. So it is recommended to use \toc3 as your thumbtab text and include it in the Table of Contents.

The usual choice.

##### \zthumbtab {#s-r-thumbText-zthumbtab}

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Thumb tabs: Use \zthumbtab text · Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> By default, Thumb Tabs use the content and styling of the \toc3 marker. If you prefer different content and/or styling for the tabs, then this\
> \zthumbtab option needs to be enabled, and the thumbtab names entered into your USFM text.
>
> Note that this setting is interconnected with the Table of Contents settings on the [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals). If \toc3 is not included in the ToC, then you are forced to use the \zthumbtab setting here. For that reason it is highly recommended to use \toc3 as your thumbtab text and include it in the Table of Contents.
>
> The USFM extension \zthumbtab can be used to set an alternative value for the thumbtab contents. If a book's header contains a \zthumbtab entry, then\
> \toc3 will not be used as the thumbtab contents. An empty \zthumbtab entry specifies that there should be no text in the thumbtab for that book.

Use it if the tab text should differ from `\toc3`. Add the `\zthumbtab` line to each book's header in Paratext. With this option, [**Edit Style**](#s-lb-style-toc3) opens the `\zthumbtab` style.

##### Edit Style {#s-lb-style-toc3}

Link · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> Click to jump to the appropriate (\toc3 or \zthumbtab) marker in the style editor to change the formatting of the thumb tabs.

Change the text colour, font and size there. Changing the `\toc3` style may also change how `\toc3` text looks elsewhere, such as in the table of contents.

##### Only Show on Odd Pages {#s-c-tabsOddOnly}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Thumb tabs: Only Show on Odd Pages · Needs: [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs) · Hidden until: “Thumb Tabs” · Shown when: “Thumb Tabs”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments)

> When printing thumb tabs on thin paper, it is preferable to only print these tabs on a single side of the page (the odd pages).

Better on thin paper, where a tab printed on both sides can show through.

#### Ornamental Decorations {#11-tabsborders--ornamental-decorations-2}

##### Section Headings {#s-c-inclSectionHeader}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Enable decorative section headings · Needs: [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> Section Headings may be adorned with a special graphic. Ensure that there is adequate space - both horizontal as well as vertical to make sure all headings fit.

Choose **PDF border (Legacy)** for a fixed graphic or **Dynamic Border** for a box that fits the heading.

##### Border {#s-c-inclPageBorder}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Enable decorative borders · Needs: [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> There are different kinds of borders that can be applied to the publication.
>
> Note that if you use a border, it is likely that you will need to adjust the margins to make it fit.

Choose one of the three kinds below it.

##### End of Book Decoration {#s-c-inclEndOfBook}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Enable end of book decoration · Needs: [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> The end of each book may be adorned with a special graphic.

Front matter, glossaries and other non-Scripture books do not get it.

##### Verse Number Decorator {#s-c-inclVerseDecorator}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Enable decorative verse numbers · Needs: [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> Verse numbers can be decorated using either of the options shown below.

[**End of Ayah**](#s-r-decorator-ayah) uses a character from the font; [**Verse Border Graphic**](#s-r-decorator-file) uses a small PDF graphic.

##### Book Title Borders {#s-c-inclTitleBorders}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Enable dynamic title borders · Needs: [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> Dynamic borders can be applied to book titles (\mt1 and \mt2). Styling can be adjusted using the link below.

PTXprint makes the `cat:titlebox|esb` style active for you. Use the link below to change its look.

##### Section Headings {#11-tabsborders--section-headings-2}

###### Select... {#s-btn-selectSectionHeaderPDF}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Select decorative section headings · Needs: “PDF border (Legacy)”, [“Section Headings”](#s-c-inclSectionHeader), [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

Chooses the section heading PDF graphic. The file name appears next to the button.

###### Shift – Decorative section headings: Vertical shift {#s-s-inclSectionShift}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Values: -50–50 · Needs: “PDF border (Legacy)”, [“Section Headings”](#s-c-inclSectionHeader), [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> Vertical shift in pts of the section box image.\
> \+ values shift the box upwards\
> \- values shift the box downwards

Same direction as **Shift** for the verse graphic. Change it in small steps (for example 2 pt) and print to check.

In older versions of PTXprint this worked the other way round. When you open a configuration saved by an older version, PTXprint changes the sign for you, so the graphic stays in place. A configuration saved by this version and opened in an older PTXprint moves the graphic the other way.

###### Scale – Decorative section headings: Scale {#s-s-inclSectionScale}

Number box · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: “PDF border (Legacy)”, [“Section Headings”](#s-c-inclSectionHeader), [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> Scale section header image. 1.0 = its own size,\
> 0\.5 = half size, 2.0 = double size.

0\.8 = 80%, 1.2 = 120%.

###### PDF border (Legacy) {#s-r-sectHead-legacy}

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Section Headings”](#s-c-inclSectionHeader), [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> Place a PDF graphic behind each section heading (\s, \s1, \s2). Use Select... to choose it, and Scale/Shift to fit it.

It does not grow with the heading, so it suits headings that are always one line.

###### Dynamic Border {#s-r-sectHead-dynamic}

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Section Headings”](#s-c-inclSectionHeader), [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> Draw a box around each section heading that grows with the heading. Its look is set by the cat:headingsbox|esb style.

PTXprint makes the `cat:headingsbox|esb` style active for you. Use the link to change it.

###### \cat:headingsbox|esb {#s-lb-style-cat-headingsbox-esb}

Link · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Dynamic Border”, [“Section Headings”](#s-c-inclSectionHeader), [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> If Section Headings sometimes extend to more than one line, then a static PDF section heading is unlikely to work. Instead, a dynamically generated decorative section heading needs to be set up to grow/shrink with the content of the heading. Use this link to show the special style, which needs to be enabled and defined.

On the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab set the background colour and, with [**Borders...**](#s-btn-sbBorders), the border of the box around headings.

##### Border {#11-tabsborders--border-3}

###### Select... {#s-btn-selectPageBorderPDF}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Select decorative borders · Needs: “PDF border (Legacy)”, “Border”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

Chooses the page border PDF. It starts in PTXprint's border-art folder.

###### Full page {#s-c-borderPageWide}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Decorative borders: Expand to fill page · Needs: “PDF border (Legacy)”, “Border”, [“Ornamental Decorations”](#s-c-useOrnaments) · Hidden until: “Ornamental Decorations” · Shown when: “Ornamental Decorations”, [“Thumb Tabs”](#s-c-thumbtabs)

> If set, the border is expanded to the full page. Otherwise it is expanded only to the gutter margins.

If unticked, the graphic is stretched to the page size without the binding gutter.
