# 23. Importing settings {#ch-20-import}

## 23.1 What this dialog is for {#20-import--what-this-dialog-is-for}

The **Import Settings** dialog copies settings from somewhere else into a configuration. Use it when:

* you have a PDF that PTXprint made earlier, and want the same layout again (for example the settings were lost, or the PDF came from another person),
* someone sent you a PTXprint ZIP archive,
* another project or configuration has settings you want to reuse – all of them, or only some groups (for example only the pictures, or only the header and footer).

You can also **extract** the settings from a PDF or ZIP into a normal folder, to look at them.

To open it: on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, in the **Layout Configuration** area, click **Import Settings...**. (Not shown in the **Mini** view.)

The dialog has three parts: **Source of Settings** (where the settings come from), **Target** (where they go), and a row of **category tabs** (what to bring in).

## 23.2 Source of Settings {#20-import--source-of-settings}

Choose one of two sources:

* [**PDF file (with embedded settings) or ZIP archive file**](#s-r-impSource-pdf) – click **Select...** and choose the file.
  * A **PDF** only works if PTXprint made it with [**Include Config Settings Within PDF**](#s-c-inclSettingsInPDF) turned on (on the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab). Otherwise PTXprint says it cannot find any settings in the file.
  * A **ZIP archive** is the kind of file made with [**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra) on the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab.
* [**A Previously Saved Configuration**](#s-r-impSource-config) – choose the **Project** and then the **Configuration** to copy from. Settings are read from the saved files, so if the source is the configuration that is open now, click **Save** first.

## 23.3 Target {#20-import--target}

Choose where the settings go:

* [**A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration**](#s-r-impTarget-prjcfg) – the usual choice. The current project and configuration are filled in. You can choose another existing project, and another configuration, or type a **new** configuration name. A new configuration starts with the PTXprint defaults, and then the imported settings are added. So for a new name, PTXprint ticks [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything) and greys out the category boxes. If you then choose an existing configuration again, **Everything** is unticked again (unless you ticked it yourself).
* [**An External Folder of Settings**](#s-r-impTarget-folder) – click **Select...** and choose a folder. PTXprint copies **all** the settings files from the source into that folder. Nothing in your projects is changed. **Everything** is turned on and the category tabs are greyed out.

**OK** stays greyed out until the choices are complete: a file or source configuration, a target folder or target configuration, and at least one category ticked. It is also greyed out when the source and target are the same configuration, and when the target **Project** name you typed is not one of your projects.

## 23.4 What to import: the category tabs {#20-import--what-to-import-the-category-tabs}

Each tab has a check box in its label: tick it to import that group. Click the tab to see its options.

* **Pictures** – the picture settings and the picture list.
* **Layout** – the page and column layout.
* **Fonts+Script** – fonts and writing-system settings.
* **Styles** – the settings from the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab.
* **Other** – other groups that you choose one by one.
* [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything) – all settings. (Only shown in the **Regular** and **Full** views.)

When **Everything** is ticked, everything is imported, whatever the other boxes say. Untick **Everything** to import only some groups.

### What each category brings in {#20-import--what-each-category-brings-in}

| Category | What is imported |
| --- | --- |
| **Pictures** | The general settings of the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab (include pictures, picture folder, resolution, captions shown, placeholders…) and the picture list. With **Import Entire PicList "as is"** the whole list is replaced. With **Import Elements of PicList** only the parts you tick are copied for each picture. |
| **Layout** | Page size, margins (top, bottom, side), mirror pages and binding gutter, number of columns and column gutter, vertical rule between columns, line spacing, note lines, margin notes, and related settings. **Not** the fonts or font size (in **Fonts+Script**) or the header and footer (in **Other** › [**Header+Footer settings**](#s-c-oth-HeaderFooter)). |
| **Fonts+Script** | The main fonts (regular, bold, italic, bold italic, extra), the font size, the fallback font, text direction, script and line-breaking settings, word and letter spacing, coloured text, and script-specific options. Also the fonts set inside individual styles (for styles that the target already has). Styles whose font you changed in the target keep it, unless [**Override ALL Style Settings**](#s-c-sty-OverrideAllStyles) is ticked. |
| **Styles** | The style settings from the source (the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab). Normally only styles that you have **not** changed in the target are updated. **Override ALL Style Settings** updates all styles. The fonts inside styles come with **Fonts+Script**, not with **Styles**. |
| **Other** | Only the groups that you tick on the **Other** tab (see the control notes below). |
| [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything) | All settings in the source configuration, including the book list, copyright text, diglot and Strong's settings, the whole picture list, styles, front matter, cover, and the special files from the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab. |

### What happens when you click OK {#20-import--what-happens-when-you-click-ok}

1. PTXprint reads the settings from the source.
2. It changes only the ticked groups in the target configuration.
3. It **saves** the target configuration at once.
4. It opens the target project and configuration, and shows a message such as "Imported Settings into: ABC::NT_A5".

There is no Undo. If you are not sure, import into a **new** configuration name first, and check the result there.

## 23.5 RESET {#20-import--reset}

**RESET** at the bottom of the dialog sets all settings of the **current** configuration back to the PTXprint defaults, at once and without asking. It does not reset the style settings. The dialog stays open, and nothing is saved until you click **Save** or **Print (Make PDF)** (or until an import saves the configuration). Use it when you want the target to have only the imported settings, for example before you import styles.

## 23.6 Common tasks {#20-import--common-tasks}

### Get back the settings that were used for a PDF {#20-import--get-back-the-settings-that-were-used-for-a-pdf}

1. On the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, click **Import Settings...**.
2. Click [**PDF file (with embedded settings) or ZIP archive file**](#s-r-impSource-pdf), then **Select...**, and choose the PDF.
3. Under **Target**, click [**A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration**](#s-r-impTarget-prjcfg). In **Configuration**, type a new name, for example `FromPDF`.
4. Check that [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything) is ticked. (For a new name, PTXprint ticks it for you. Change to the **Regular** view if you cannot see it.)
5. Click **OK**. PTXprint opens the new configuration with the settings from the PDF.

### Copy only the pictures from another configuration {#20-import--copy-only-the-pictures-from-another-configuration}

1. Click **Import Settings...**.
2. Click [**A Previously Saved Configuration**](#s-r-impSource-config) and choose the source **Project** and **Configuration**.
3. Check that the **Target** is the configuration you want.
4. Untick [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything), **Layout**, **Fonts+Script**, **Styles** and **Other**. Tick **Pictures**.
5. On the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab, choose **Import Entire PicList "as is"**, or **Import Elements of PicList** and tick only what you want (for example [**Size, Position, Mirror, Rotation settings**](#s-c-pic-SizePosn)).
6. Click **OK**.

### Copy the header and footer from another configuration {#20-import--copy-the-header-and-footer-from-another-configuration}

1. Click **Import Settings...** and choose the source configuration.
2. Untick [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything) and all other categories, and tick **Other**.
3. On the **Other** tab, untick everything except [**Header+Footer settings**](#s-c-oth-HeaderFooter).
4. Click **OK**.

### Look at the settings inside a PDF or ZIP without changing anything {#20-import--look-at-the-settings-inside-a-pdf-or-zip-without-changing-anything}

1. Click **Import Settings...** and choose the PDF or ZIP file as the source.
2. Under **Target**, click [**An External Folder of Settings**](#s-r-impTarget-folder), then **Select...**, and choose an empty folder.
3. Click **OK**. The settings files are copied into that folder.

### Start a configuration again from defaults, then import styles {#20-import--start-a-configuration-again-from-defaults-then-import-styles}

1. Open the configuration on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.
2. Click **Import Settings...**, then [**RESET**](#20-import--reset).
3. Choose the source, untick [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything), and tick **Styles** (and other groups you need).
4. Click **OK**.

## 23.7 Common problems {#20-import--common-problems}

### "Cannot find any settings to import from the selected file" {#20-import--cannot-find-any-settings-to-import-from-the-selected-file}

**Cause:** The PDF was made without [**Include Config Settings Within PDF**](#s-c-inclSettingsInPDF) (on the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab), or with a very old PTXprint version (before 2.3). **What to do:** Use another source, for example a ZIP archive made with [**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra) on the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab.

### The OK button is greyed out {#20-import--the-ok-button-is-greyed-out}

**Cause:** Something is missing: no file selected, no target folder, no target configuration, no category ticked – or the source and target are the same configuration. **What to do:** Check each part of the dialog.

### Everything was imported, but I ticked only one category {#20-import--everything-was-imported-but-i-ticked-only-one-category}

**Cause:** [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything) was still ticked. In the **Basic** view the **Everything** tab is hidden but still ticked (it is ticked by default). Also, when the target is a **new** configuration or an external folder, PTXprint ticks **Everything** itself and you cannot untick it. **What to do:** Import into an existing configuration. Change to the **Regular** view (**≡** › [**View Level**](#s-btn-menu-level) › **Regular View**) and untick **Everything**.

### The styles did not change {#20-import--the-styles-did-not-change}

**Cause:** Without [**Override ALL Style Settings**](#s-c-sty-OverrideAllStyles), only styles still unchanged in the target are updated. **What to do:** Tick **Override ALL Style Settings**, or click [**RESET**](#20-import--reset) before you import.

### The font size did not change when I imported Layout {#20-import--the-font-size-did-not-change-when-i-imported-layout}

**Cause:** The font size belongs to **Fonts+Script**. **What to do:** Tick **Fonts+Script** too.

### The header and footer did not change when I imported Layout {#20-import--the-header-and-footer-did-not-change-when-i-imported-layout}

**Cause:** They belong to **Other** › [**Header+Footer settings**](#s-c-oth-HeaderFooter). **What to do:** Tick **Other** and **Header+Footer settings**.

### Custom Script is greyed out {#20-import--custom-script-is-greyed-out}

**Cause:** The source is a PDF, which does not contain the custom script. **What to do:** Import from a ZIP archive or a saved configuration instead.

### The fonts in some styles did not change {#20-import--the-fonts-in-some-styles-did-not-change}

**Cause:** Fonts inside styles come with **Fonts+Script** (not **Styles**), and styles whose font you changed in the target keep their font. **What to do:** Tick **Fonts+Script**. To replace the fonts in all styles, also tick [**Override ALL Style Settings**](#s-c-sty-OverrideAllStyles).

### The category boxes are greyed out and Everything is ticked {#20-import--the-category-boxes-are-greyed-out-and-everything-is-ticked}

**Cause:** The target is a configuration that does not exist yet (you typed a new name), or an external folder. A new configuration starts from the PTXprint defaults, so everything is imported. **What to do:** To import only some groups, choose an existing configuration as the target.

## 23.8 Settings reference {#20-import--settings-reference}

### Import Settings... (dialog) {#20-import--import-settings-dialog}

#### RESET {#s-btn-resetConfig}

Button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Reset the current Configuration's UI settings

> Warning! This will reset ALL the UI settings for the CURRENT configuration to their default values.
>
> Note that it will NOT reset the Style settings stored in the .sty files.
>
> The reset is not saved until you next save, print, or import with OK.

Resets at once and without asking. See ["RESET"](#20-import--reset) in this chapter.

#### OK {#s-btn-importSettingsOK}

Button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

Imports the ticked groups into the target, saves it, and opens it. With an external folder as target, it copies the settings files there instead. Greyed out until the choices are complete. Shortcut: **Alt+Enter**.

#### Cancel {#s-btn-importCancel}

Button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

Closes without importing. (Changes made with [**RESET**](#20-import--reset) stay on the screen.) Shortcut: **Ctrl+W**.

#### Pictures {#s-c-impPictures}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Import Picture Settings

> Import the picture settings and the picture list. Use the [Pictures tab](#ch-09-pictures) of this dialog to choose how the picture list is combined.

Ticking or unticking it opens the **Pictures** tab of the dialog.

#### Layout {#s-c-impLayout}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Import Layout Settings

> Import page size, margins, columns, line spacing and related settings.

See the table in ["What each category brings in"](#20-import--what-each-category-brings-in). The text on the dialog's [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab also mentions the header and footer, but they are imported with **Other** › [**Header+Footer settings**](#s-c-oth-HeaderFooter).

#### Fonts+Script {#s-c-impFontsScript}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Import Fonts and Script Settings

> Import the font and script settings (Fonts+Scripts tab), including fonts set within individual styles.

Imports fonts inside styles (font name and font features) even when **Styles** is not ticked. Hyphenation settings come with **Other** › [**Body Tab settings**](#s-c-oth-Body), not here.

#### Styles {#s-c-impStyles}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Import Styles Settings

> Import the style settings ([Styles tab](#ch-12-styles)), merged into the target configuration.

Font names and font features inside styles are imported only when **Fonts+Script** (or [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything)) is also ticked.

#### Other {#s-c-impOther}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Import Other Settings

> Use the Other tab of this dialog to choose more groups of settings. If this is not ticked, none of the boxes on the Other tab are used.

Groups on the **Other** tab include Body, Notes+Refs, Header+Footer, Advanced, Cover, Front +Back Matter and Finishing.

#### Everything {#s-c-impEverything}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Import All Settings

> Import all settings and files of the source configuration, whatever the other boxes say.

Use it to recreate a configuration from a PDF or ZIP, or to make a full copy. Ticked by default, and ticked again when you open the dialog with no category ticked. Also turned on automatically (with the other boxes greyed out) when the target is an external folder or a new configuration. In the **Basic** view it is hidden but still works.

#### Source of Settings {#20-import--source-of-settings-2}

##### PDF file (with embedded settings) or ZIP archive file {#s-r-impSource-pdf}

Radio button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Import: From existing PDF file or ZIP archive

> It is possible to import settings from an existing PDF file which was produced earlier by PTXprint. But this only works if the settings are embedded within the PDF. (This is enabled on the [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing)).
>
> Importing from a PTXprint ZIP archive (created on the [Help tab](#ch-21-help)) is also possible.

Click **Select...** to choose the file.

##### A Previously Saved Configuration {#s-r-impSource-config}

Radio button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Import: From Saved Configuration

Choosing a project or configuration in the lists below also selects this option.

##### Project – Import: Project name {#s-fcb-impProject}

Drop-down list · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Choices: unknown · Needs: [“A Previously Saved Configuration”](#s-r-impSource-config)

> Select the project from which the settings will be imported.

Choosing a project fills the **Configuration** list with its configurations and selects **Default**.

##### Configuration – Import: Project configuration {#s-ecb-impConfig}

Drop-down list · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Choices: (None) · Needs: [“A Previously Saved Configuration”](#s-r-impSource-config)

> Select a configuration from the selected project from which the settings will be imported.

Settings are read from the saved files, so save the source configuration first if it is open.

##### Select... {#s-btn-impSource-pdf}

Button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Select PDF to import settings from · Needs: [“PDF file (with embedded settings) or ZIP archive file”](#s-r-impSource-pdf)

> Select either a PTXprint PDF or ZIP archive to import the settings from.
>
> Importing from a PDF will only work if the PDF contains the PTXprint configuration settings (as enabled on the [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing)).

Starts in the output folder of the current project, where PTXprint keeps its PDFs. If the file has no PTXprint settings, PTXprint shows an error and changes back to [**A Previously Saved Configuration**](#s-r-impSource-config). The chosen file name is shown next to the button.

#### Target {#20-import--target-2}

##### An External Folder of Settings {#s-r-impTarget-folder}

Radio button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Extract settings to an external folder

> Settings can be extracted to an external folder.
>
> This may be useful when examining settings from a different user, or when there is a need to recover lost settings from a known good PDF or Zip archive.

No project is changed. [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything) is used automatically.

##### A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration {#s-r-impTarget-prjcfg}

Radio button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Import: Into Project/Configuration

The usual choice. The current project and configuration are filled in when the dialog opens.

##### Project – Import: Project name {#s-ecb-targetProject}

Drop-down list · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Choices: unknown · Needs: [“A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration”](#s-r-impTarget-prjcfg)

> Select an existing project into which the settings will be imported.
>
> Select the project into which the settings will be imported.

You cannot import into a new project. If you type a name that is not one of your projects, **OK** stays greyed out. Choosing a project here also selects **A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration** and fills the **Configuration** list.

##### Select... {#s-btn-tgtFolder}

Button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Select target folder for extracted settings · Needs: [“An External Folder of Settings”](#s-r-impTarget-folder)

> Select a folder to save the settings in. This could be in a temporary location from where just the needed settings can be accessed and copied into the appropriate place of an existing config.

Choose an empty folder, so the extracted files are easy to find. The chosen folder is shown next to the button.

##### Configuration {#s-ecb-targetConfig}

Drop-down list · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Choices: Default · Needs: [“A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration”](#s-r-impTarget-prjcfg)

> Choose a configuration from the selected project into which the settings will be imported.\
> OR Enter a NEW config name which causes a new configuration to be created for the current/new project.
>
> Select a configuration in the selected project into which the settings will be imported.

Importing into a new configuration is the safest way to try an import, because your existing configurations are not changed.

##### Enter a name for the configuration to be saved. {#s-t-targetConfig}

Text box · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration”](#s-r-impTarget-prjcfg)

> Enter a name for the configuration to be saved.
>
> Note that only Roman/Latin names are supported using: a-z A-Z, 0-9, parentheses, underscores and hyphens.

The text part of the target **Configuration** box. No spaces. When you type a new name, PTXprint ticks [**Everything**](#s-c-impEverything) for you.

#### Pictures {#20-import--pictures}

##### Import Entire PicList "as is" (overwrite existing PicList) {#s-r-impPics-entire}

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Import: Entire PicList "as is" (overwrite existing PicList) · Needs: “Pictures”

> Replace the target's whole picture list with the source's. Pictures only in the target are removed. Use it when the source is the master list.

Pictures that were only in the target are removed.

##### Import Elements of PicList (preserving existing PicList) {#s-r-impPics-elements}

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Import: Elements of PicList (preserving existing PicList) · Needs: “Pictures”

> Keep the target's picture list and copy only the parts ticked below, for pictures in both lists.

The parts are captions, size and position, and copyright. [**Add Any New Pictures**](#s-c-impPicsAddNew) and [**Remove Any Old Pictures**](#s-c-impPicsDelOld) control which pictures are in the list.

##### Captions {#s-c-pic-Captions}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Import Elements of PicList (preserving existing PicList)”](#s-r-impPics-elements), “Pictures”

> Copy the captions and the reference shown with each picture. Leave unticked if the target is in another language.

Also copies the caption of the second text in a diglot. Unticked for another language because the captions would be in the wrong language.

##### Size, Position, Mirror, Rotation settings {#s-c-pic-SizePosn}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Import Elements of PicList (preserving existing PicList)”](#s-r-impPics-elements), “Pictures”

> Copy the size, position, scale, mirroring and rotation of each picture.

Useful when two projects share the same pictures and layout.

##### Copyright Information {#s-c-pic-Copyright}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Import Elements of PicList (preserving existing PicList)”](#s-r-impPics-elements), “Pictures”

> Copy the copyright (credit) information of each picture.

Copies the picture credits.

##### Add Any New Pictures {#s-c-impPicsAddNew}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Pictures”

> Add pictures that are in the source list but not yet in the target list.

Leave it ticked unless you want to keep exactly the pictures the target already has.

##### Remove Any Old Pictures {#s-c-impPicsDelOld}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Pictures”

> Remove pictures from the target list that are not in the source list. Tick it when the source list is the complete, final list.

Use it with a complete, final source list.

#### Styles {#20-import--styles}

##### Override ALL Style Settings {#s-c-sty-OverrideAllStyles}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> Normally only styles that have not been changed in the receiving configuration will be imported. But if you require ALL styles to be updated regardless of whether they have already been modified locally, then enable this option. (This also applies to fonts in styles imported with Fonts+Script.)

Without it, your own style changes in the target are kept.

#### Other {#20-import--other}

##### Body Tab settings {#s-c-oth-Body}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> Import the settings of the [Body tab](#ch-06-body).

Includes how books and chapters start, chapter and verse numbers, section headings, hyphenation, glossary markup, and similar.

##### Notes+Refs settings {#s-c-oth-NotesRefs}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> Import the settings of the [Notes+Refs tab](#ch-07-notes).

Footnotes, cross-references, note callers, note rules and study notes.

##### Header+Footer settings {#s-c-oth-HeaderFooter}

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> Import the settings of the [Header+Footer tab](#ch-08-headfoot).

What is shown in the header and footer, and their positions.

##### Thumb Tabs settings {#s-c-oth-ThumbTabs}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> Import the thumb tab settings ([Tabs+Borders tab](#ch-11-tabsborders)).

Use it when two configurations or projects should have matching thumb tabs.

##### Overwrite Front Matter {#s-c-oth-OverwriteFrtMatter}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: [“Front +Back Matter”](#s-c-oth-FrontMatter), [“Cover settings”](#s-c-oth-Cover), “Other”

> Replace the front matter in the target with the source's, instead of only adding the parts that are missing.

Leave it unticked if the target has its own front matter (for example in another language) that you want to keep.

##### Advanced settings {#s-c-oth-Advanced}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> This includes everything on the [Advanced tab](#ch-13-advanced) with the exception of Custom Script processing and Customized Styles (custom.sty).

Includes the changes file, the extra TeX files, and the extra style file (merged with the target's). For the custom script, tick [**Custom Script**](#s-c-oth-customScript). custom.sty is not imported.

##### Cover settings {#s-c-oth-Cover}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> Import the cover settings, cover styles and the cover pages of the front matter.

Also turns on decorations, which the cover uses.

##### Front +Back Matter {#s-c-oth-FrontMatter}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> This includes most of the settings on the [Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals), but not the Variables and Values. Front Matter and also Section Introductions are included in this.

Includes front and back PDFs, table of contents, front matter, colophon and section introductions, plus the source's front matter pages and any variables the target does not have yet. Existing variable values in the target are not changed.

##### Custom Script {#s-c-oth-customScript}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> This includes the Custom Script processing defined on the [Advanced tab](#ch-13-advanced).
>
> Note that it is not possible to extract a custom script from a PDF file, which is why this option is sometimes disabled.

Includes whether the script is used and when it runs. PTXprint finds the script in the source (also inside a ZIP made with [**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra)), copies it into the target configuration folder, and points the **Advanced** tab at the copy. For a Python script, other Python files it uses from the same folder are copied too. Greyed out (and unticked) when the source is a PDF.

##### Borders + Decorations {#s-c-oth-Decorate}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> This includes the various decorative borders and other ornamental features including section headers, end-of-book and verse number decorators.

Includes page borders and the book-title border.

##### Variables + Meta Data {#s-c-oth-Variables}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> Import the variables ([Peripherals tab](#ch-15-peripherals)) and the publication details: copyright statement, licence, colophon and configuration notes. The book selection and any password are not imported.

Variables that the target is missing are also added by [**Front +Back Matter**](#s-c-oth-FrontMatter).

##### Texpert Hacks {#s-c-oth-Texpert}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> Import the expert TeX (TeXpert) settings.

Use it only if you know that the source used special TeX settings.

##### Finishing settings {#s-c-oth-Finish}

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Needs: “Other”

> This includes everything on the [Finishing tab](#ch-17-finishing).

PDF output format, watermark, crop marks, grid, pages per sheet and sheet size, the compare-PDF settings, and whether settings are included in the PDF.

# 24. Help tab and getting support {#ch-21-help}

## 24.1 What this tab is for {#21-help--what-this-tab-is-for}

The **Help** tab is where you go when you need help, or need to find your files. It is shown in every view level.

On this tab you can:

* see where PTXprint keeps your PDF and other files, and open those folders;
* open the documentation, training material and the user community website;
* make an **archive** (a ZIP file) of your project to send to the support team;
* make a **report** about the last PDF, with warnings and errors;
* [**Tidy Up**](#s-btn-deleteTempFiles) temporary files to save disk space;
* change the [**Base Projects Directory**](#s-l-projects-dir) (the folder that holds your Paratext projects);
* open the **About** window to see which version of PTXprint you have.

Many links on this tab open web pages. They are only shown when internet use is allowed. If [**Disable ALL Internet Use**](#s-c-noInternet) is ticked on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, the internet links and the **About** button are hidden. Untick it to see them again. Some items are only shown in the **Full** view; this is noted for each one.

## 24.2 Links and Help {#21-help--links-and-help}

### Folders {#21-help--folders}

* [**Output PDF Location**](#s-l-working-dir) – the folder where PTXprint saves the PDF files it makes. Click the blue link to open it.
* [**Base Projects Directory**](#s-l-projects-dir) – the folder that holds all your Paratext projects. Use [**Change...**](#s-btn-changeProjectsDir) to choose a different one.
* [**PTXprint Program Path**](#s-l-ptxprintdir) (**Full** view only) – the folder where PTXprint itself is installed.

Everything in the output location is made again each time you print. None of it is part of Paratext Send/Receive. Your settings are kept safely in a different place, inside the project's shared folder.

### Documentation and learning {#21-help--documentation-and-learning}

These links open web pages or documents:

* **Documentation | FAQs | Gallery | Support | Download** – the PTXprint home page. PTXprint does not update itself, so check here for new versions and download them yourself.
* **Learn: How to...** – short articles about common tasks.
* **Training (Videos and Presentations)** – videos on the Paratext website and on Vimeo, and a **Training Presentation** (a large set of Google Slides that trainers can use).
* [**User Manual**](#s-lb-userManual) – this manual. It opens in the **Manual** tab of the PDF Preview window, with its contents beside it; click a link to follow it. It comes with PTXprint, so it opens without internet. You can also press **F1** over any setting, or **Ctrl+click** a tab's name, to open the manual at the part about it.
* [**Ornaments Catalog**](#s-lb-ornaments-cat) and [**Technical Reference**](#s-lb-tech-ref) (**Full** view only) – PDF documents that come with PTXprint. They open without internet.
* **Advanced Tech Docs** (**Full** view only) – technical documents for advanced users.
* **Support Agent** – an AI chatbot that answers questions about PTXprint.
* **The PTXprint User Community** – a website where you can ask questions and help other users.
* **Tell us what you think about PTXprint** – a short feedback form.
* **Report an Issue via GitHub** (**Full** view only) – for reporting bugs, if you have a GitHub account.

### Support tools {#21-help--support-tools}

* [**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra) – makes a ZIP file with everything needed to make your PDF again on another computer.
* [**Create Report...**](#s-btn-generateReport) – makes a report page about the last PDF.
* [**Tidy Up**](#s-btn-deleteTempFiles) – deletes temporary files.
* **About** – shows the version number and the names of the developers.

## 24.3 How to ask for help {#21-help--how-to-ask-for-help}

If PTXprint does not do what you expect, you can get help here:

1. **Read this manual** and the [**Common problems**](#21-help--common-problems) sections in each chapter.
2. **Ask the Support Agent** (the AI chatbot link on the **Help** tab). It knows this manual and can answer many questions quickly.
3. **Ask the PTXprint User Community** (the community link on the **Help** tab). Other users and the developers read it.
4. **Email the support team** at **ptxprint_support@sil.org**.

### Before you write {#21-help--before-you-write}

* **Use the latest version.** Check the PTXprint home page. Your problem may already be fixed. The **About** button shows your version.
* **Make sure you can repeat the problem.** Note the exact steps: which project, which configuration, which book, and what you clicked.
* **Make the problem small.** If the problem is in one book, print only that book. If pictures are not involved, untick pictures for now.
* **Click Create Report...** and look at the warnings and errors. They may already tell you what is wrong.

### What to send to ptxprint_support@sil.org {#21-help--what-to-send-to-ptxprint-support-sil-org}

Send one email with:

1. **A clear description of the problem.** What did you want? What happened instead? On which page and in which verse? Copy the exact text of any error message.
2. **Your PTXprint version** (from the **About** window) and your operating system (for example Windows 11).
3. **Screenshots.** One of the problem in the PDF, and one of the PTXprint setting you think is involved. Mark the problem area if you can.
4. **The archive ZIP file** made with [**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra) (see below). With it, the support team can make exactly the same PDF on their computer.

### Making a good archive file {#21-help--making-a-good-archive-file}

1. Select the project and configuration that shows the problem.
2. Choose only the book(s) needed to show the problem. One book is best.
3. If the problem has nothing to do with pictures, untick pictures. Pictures make the archive much larger.
4. On the **Help** tab, click [**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra).
5. Choose where to save the ZIP file, and click **Save**. PTXprint first prints the PDF again, then collects the files. This can take a while.
6. When it is finished, PTXprint opens the folder that contains the ZIP file.
7. Attach the ZIP file to your email.

The archive includes your settings, the USFM text of the selected books, the fonts, the pictures that are used, the PDF, and PTXprint's own typesetting files. Many email systems do not accept attachments larger than about 20 MB. If your ZIP file is too large, make it smaller (fewer books, no pictures), or share it through a file-sharing service and send the link.

The text of your project is inside the archive. If the text is sensitive, check with your project leader before you send it.

An archive is also useful as a long-term record of how a publication was made.

## 24.4 Log tab {#21-help--log-tab}

The **Log** tab is not normally shown in PTXprint. To read the messages from the typesetting program, use the **XeTeX Log** tab on the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab, or use [**Create Report...**](#s-btn-generateReport).

## 24.5 About dialog {#21-help--about-dialog}

The **About** window shows the PTXprint version number, the copyright, a link to the PTXprint home page, the list of developers, and the licence (MIT). Click **Credits** or [**License**](#s-ecb-licenseText) to see more, and **Close** to return. Give the version number when you ask for help.

The **About** button is only shown when [**Disable ALL Internet Use**](#s-c-noInternet) is unticked on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab.

## 24.6 Common tasks {#21-help--common-tasks}

### Find the PDF that PTXprint made {#21-help--find-the-pdf-that-ptxprint-made}

On the **Help** tab, click the blue link next to [**Output PDF Location**](#s-l-working-dir). The folder opens on your computer.

### Send a problem to the support team {#21-help--send-a-problem-to-the-support-team}

1. Follow the steps in [**Making a good archive file**](#21-help--making-a-good-archive-file) above.
2. Email **ptxprint_support@sil.org** with a description, your version number, screenshots and the ZIP file.

### Check the last PDF for problems {#21-help--check-the-last-pdf-for-problems}

1. Click **Print** to make the PDF.
2. On the **Help** tab, click [**Create Report...**](#s-btn-generateReport).
3. The report opens in your web browser. Look at the warnings (for example missing fonts, underfilled pages, or problem markers).

### Free up disk space {#21-help--free-up-disk-space}

On the **Help** tab, click [**Tidy Up**](#s-btn-deleteTempFiles). PTXprint deletes the temporary working folders for all configurations of the current project. Your PDF files and settings are kept.

### Use projects from another Paratext folder {#21-help--use-projects-from-another-paratext-folder}

1. On the **Help** tab, click [**Change...**](#s-btn-changeProjectsDir) next to [**Base Projects Directory**](#s-l-projects-dir).
2. In the **Choose Paratext Projects Folder** window, choose one of the folders that PTXprint found, or click **Browse for a different folder…**.
3. Choose the folder that *contains* your project folders, not a single project folder.
4. Click **Use Selected**. PTXprint goes back to the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab. Choose a project from the new list.

### Show the internet links on the Help tab {#21-help--show-the-internet-links-on-the-help-tab}

1. Open the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab (shown in the **Regular** and **Full** views).
2. Untick [**Disable ALL Internet Use**](#s-c-noInternet).
3. Return to the **Help** tab. The links are now shown.

## 24.7 Common problems {#21-help--common-problems}

**The Help tab has very few links.**
[**Disable ALL Internet Use**](#s-c-noInternet) is ticked on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab. Untick it to see the links. Some items (for example the [**Technical Reference**](#s-lb-tech-ref) and the [**PTXprint Program Path**](#s-l-ptxprintdir)) are only shown in the **Full** view.

**A link opens the page in another language, or through Google Translate.**
When PTXprint is in a language other than English, some links go through Google Translate. Tick [**Only Use English Links**](#s-c-useEngLinks) on the **Advanced** tab to open the original English pages.

**Create Archive... takes a long time.**
PTXprint prints the whole job again before it makes the archive. Choose fewer books, or untick pictures, to make it faster and smaller.

**The archive ZIP file is too big to email.**
Archive only the book that shows the problem. Untick pictures if they are not part of the problem. If it is still too big, use a file-sharing service and send a link.

**"Cannot create Archive!" message.**
The ZIP file is open in another program, or you are saving over a file that is in use. Close the other program, or choose a different file name.

**Tidy Up shows a warning that some folders could not be deleted.**
A file in the folder is still open, for example the PDF in a PDF viewer. Close it and click [**Tidy Up**](#s-btn-deleteTempFiles) again.

**PTXprint does not show my projects.**
The [**Base Projects Directory**](#s-l-projects-dir) may point to the wrong folder. Click [**Change...**](#s-btn-changeProjectsDir) and choose the folder that contains your Paratext projects.

## 24.8 Settings reference {#21-help--settings-reference}

### Help {#21-help--help}

#### Links and Help {#21-help--links-and-help-2}

##### Output PDF Location {#s-l-working-dir}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> The PDF file created is stored in this folder (but should automatically open in your system's PDF viewer anyway).
>
> Note that ALL the files and subfolders in this location are TEMPORARY and can be deleted. None of these files are included in Paratext's Send/Recv data.

The folder is inside the project, in the local PTXprint folder. Click the blue link beside it to open it. [**Tidy Up**](#s-btn-deleteTempFiles) deletes the temporary working files in its sub-folders.

##### Reference Documentation {#s-l-techFAQ}

Label · shown in: all views

> Reference documents for PTXprint:\
> the User Manual, the Ornaments Catalog, the Technical Reference (for advanced users) and, when online, the Advanced Tech Docs.

A heading for the reference documents. The [**User Manual**](#s-lb-userManual) is shown in every view; the other documents only in the **Full** view.

##### PTXprint Program Path {#s-l-ptxprintdir}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Among other things, this folder contains:\
> \* ReleaseNotes.txt\
> \* AboutPTXprint.txt\
> \* MIT License.txt

You normally do not need this folder, unless the support team asks for it. Only shown in the **Full** view.

##### Create Archive... {#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra}

Button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views

> Create a ZIPped archive of all the files required to replicate this configuration. Useful for long-term archiving; but also helpful when availing technical support. The job is printed again first, so this may take a while.
>
> Keep the size to a minimum by turning off features (pictures?) that don't affect the issue being reported.
>
> Email the ZIPped archive file to:\
> mailto:ptxprint_support@sil.org

See [**Making a good archive file**](#21-help--making-a-good-archive-file) in this chapter for what to do before you click and what the archive contains.

##### Tidy Up {#s-btn-deleteTempFiles}

Button · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views\
Also: Delete temporary files and folders

> Delete the TEMPORARY working folders of ALL configurations of this project. This will not delete the resulting PDF files, but will save some space by deleting unneeded files.

Your settings are not deleted either. The next print takes a little longer, because PTXprint must make the working files again. If a file is still open in another program, PTXprint warns that some folders could not be deleted.

##### User Manual {#s-lb-userManual}

Link · shown in: all views\
Also: Show the User Manual

> Open the PTXprint User Manual in the Manual tab of the PDF Preview window.

Opens this manual in the **Manual** tab of the PDF Preview window. See "PDF Preview window" for moving around in it. To go straight to the part about a setting, press **F1** with the mouse over it instead; **Ctrl+click** on a tab's name does the same for the tab.

##### Ornaments Catalog {#s-lb-ornaments-cat}

Link · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Show the Ornaments Catalog

> Click to Open the Ornaments Catalog used for decorating the PDF (refer to the Tabs+Borders settings).

Shows all the decorative ornaments you can use on the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab. The file comes with PTXprint, so it opens without internet. Only shown in the **Full** view.

##### Technical Reference {#s-lb-tech-ref}

Link · shown in: Regular and Full views\
Also: Show the Technical Reference document

> Click to open the Technical Reference document. (For advanced users only).

The PDF comes with PTXprint and explains many settings in detail. Only shown in the **Full** view.

##### Technical Support {#s-l-techSupport1}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Before contacting support, make sure that it is possible to replicate the issue. Then use the ["Create Archive..."](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra) button to make a ZIP file which needs to be emailed to:\
> mailto:ptxprint_support@sil.org

See [**How to ask for help**](#21-help--how-to-ask-for-help) in this chapter.

##### Create Report... {#s-btn-generateReport}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Generate a summary report with details about the PDF produced. This contains informational, warning and error messages about fonts, styles, layout and so on.

Opens the report in your web browser. Its sections include project overview, layout, USFM checks, fonts, writing system, peripheral components, output format, files and log analysis. Make the PDF first, so that the report is up to date. It is a good first check before you ask for help, and you can attach it to your email to the support team.

##### Base Projects Directory {#s-l-projects-dir}

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

> The folder that contains all your Paratext project folders. Use Change... to choose a different folder.

PTXprint lists the projects it finds in this folder on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab. Click the link beside it to open the folder.

##### Change... {#s-btn-changeProjectsDir}

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

> Use this button to change the Base Projects Directory. For example, to use projects from a different version of Paratext.
>
> Do not select a specific project folder, but the parent folder which contains one or more projects.

Opens the **Choose Paratext Projects Folder** window. It lists the Paratext folders PTXprint found and says which ones contain projects. You can also browse for another folder. After the change, PTXprint returns to the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab, so you can choose a project from the new list.

# 25. Glossary of terms {#ch-32-glossary}

## 25.1 How to use this glossary {#32-glossary--how-to-use-this-glossary}

This glossary explains the technical words and PTXprint words used in this manual, in alphabetical order. Where it helps, it names the chapter that tells you more.

## 25.2 1–9 {#32-glossary--1-9}

**1-up, 2-up, 4-up, 8-up** — How many book pages are printed on one side of a sheet. **1-up** is a normal PDF, one page per PDF page. **2-up** puts two pages side by side, for a folded booklet. Set it in [**Pages Per Spread**](#s-fcb-pagesPerSpread) ([**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab).

## 25.3 A {#32-glossary--a}

**Adj List (AdjList, adjustment list)** — The list of paragraph adjustments for each book. Each row asks PTXprint to set one paragraph one line shorter or longer, or with slightly narrower or wider letters. You make adjustments in the PDF Preview window, and see and edit the list on the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab, [**Adj List**](#s-l-AdjList) sub-tab.

**Adjustment (shrink, expand)** — A small change to one paragraph so that it uses one line less (shrink) or more (expand), or so that its letters are a little narrower or wider. Used to make pages fill well. See the [**PDF Preview**](#ch-19-preview) chapter.

[**Align Text to Baseline**](#s-c-noGrid) — A layout choice where every line sits on a fixed grid, so the lines on the front and back of a sheet line up. The other choice is **Variable Line Spacing**. See the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.

[**Alpha**](#s-s-sbAlpha) — How solid a background colour is: 0 is clear (see-through), 1 is fully solid. Used for sidebar backgrounds on the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab.

**Anchor (Anchor Ref)** — The place in the text that a picture belongs to, usually a verse, for example `MRK 4.39`. PTXprint tries to put the picture on the same page as its anchor. See the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab.

**Archive (ZIP archive)** — A ZIP file with everything needed to make your PDF again on another computer: settings, text, fonts and pictures. Make it with [**Create Archive...**](#s-btn-createZipArchiveXtra) on the [**Help**](#ch-21-help) tab, and send it to the support team when you ask for help.

**Auto Page Fill (page filler)** — A tool in the PDF Preview window that tries to make every page full by adjusting paragraphs automatically. It can take a long time. For a diglot or polyglot it also tries to keep the columns at the same height (experimental). See the **PDF Preview** chapter.

[**Auto-update**](#s-c-updatePDF) — An option in the PDF Preview window. When ticked, PTXprint makes a new PDF by itself a few seconds after you adjust something in the preview.

## 25.4 B {#32-glossary--b}

**Back matter** — The pages after the Scripture text, for example a glossary, maps, an index or a colophon. See the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab.

**Base Font Size** — The size of the letters in normal paragraphs, in points. All other text sizes (headings, notes, verse numbers) are relative to it. Set it on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.

[**Base Indent**](#s-s-indentUnit) — The normal width of a paragraph indent. Indents on the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab are multiples of it. Set it on the **Layout** tab.

**Base Line Spacing** — The normal distance from one line of text to the next, in points. Set it on the **Layout** tab.

**Baseline** — The invisible line that the letters sit on.

[**Bible Module**](#s-r-book-module) — A Paratext file that lists passages to print together, for example for a lectionary. You can print one from the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.

**Binding gutter** — Extra empty space at the inner edge of each page, near the spine, so the text does not disappear into the binding. See the **Layout** tab.

**Bleed** — A picture or colour that goes past the edge of the page, so no white strip shows if the printer does not cut exactly. Usually about 3 mm. See the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab.

**Blurb** — A short text on the back cover about the book. Add it in the [**Cover Wizard**](#s-btn-coverGenerate).

**Book code** — The 3-letter code for a book in Paratext and USFM, for example `GEN`, `MAT`, `JHN` or `1CO`. Use these codes when you type book lists in PTXprint.

[**Book View**](#s-c-bkView) — A way to see two facing pages side by side in the PDF Preview window, as in a printed book.

**BSB (Berean Standard Bible)** — A free English Bible that PTXprint can install for you, for practice or as a second text in a diglot. See the **Basic** tab.

## 25.5 C {#32-glossary--c}

**Caller** — The small mark in the text (for example *a*, *b* or †) that tells the reader there is a note. The same mark is often repeated at the start of the note. See the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab.

**Caption** — The text printed with a picture, usually below it. See the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab. In a diglot, a shared picture can show the captions of both texts ([**Captions**](#s-c-pic-Captions) on the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab).

**Category** — A label that groups study notes or sidebars, for example "people" or "places". All sidebars with the same category share one style.

**Changes file (changes.txt)** — A list of search-and-replace rules that PTXprint applies to a temporary copy of the text before typesetting. The Paratext text is not changed. An advanced feature on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab.

[**Chapter label**](#s-t-clHeading) — A word printed before each chapter number instead of a large number alone, for example "Psalm 1". Set it on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab.

**Character style (character marker)** — A style for a few words inside a paragraph, for example `\nd` (name of God) or `\w` (glossary word). Compare **paragraph style**.

**CMYK** — The four inks used by most colour printing presses: Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and blacK. Many printers ask for a CMYK PDF. Choose it in [**PDF Output Format**](#s-fcb-outputFormat) on the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab.

**Colophon** — A short text at the end of the publication with details about it, for example the copyright, the printer and the picture credits. Turn it on and edit it on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab.

[**Column Cross-References**](#s-r-xrpos-centre) — Cross-references printed in a narrow column of their own beside the text, as in many reference Bibles. See the **Notes+Refs** tab.

**Column gutter** — The empty space between two columns of text. See **gutter**.

**Configuration (config, layout)** — A named set of PTXprint settings for one project: page size, fonts, pictures, styles, front matter and so on. One project can have many configurations, for example a draft and a final one. Choose and make configurations on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.

**Copyright statement** — The text that says who owns the rights to the text. PTXprint takes it from Paratext; you can change it on the **Basic** tab. Print it in the front matter with `\zcopyright`.

[**Cover**](#15-peripherals--cover) — The outside of the book: front cover, spine and back cover. PTXprint makes the cover as a separate PDF (name ending **\_cover**). See the **Peripherals** tab.

[**Cover Wizard**](#s-btn-coverGenerate) — A step-by-step window on the **Peripherals** tab that designs the cover: spine, picture, background, front, spine and back cover text. **Finish** writes the cover sections into the front matter.

**Credit overlay** — A small copyright line printed on top of a picture. Some artists require it. See the **Pictures** tab.

**Crop marks (trim marks)** — Thin lines outside the corners of each page that show the printer where to cut. Only add them if the printer asks. See the **Finishing** tab.

**Cross-reference** — A note that lists other places in the Bible about the same thing, for example "Gen 1:1; Ps 33:6". In USFM it is marked with `\x`. PTXprint can also add cross-references from an external list. See the **Notes+Refs** tab.

**Cutout** — A space cut into the side of a paragraph, so that the text flows around a small picture or box. See the **Pictures** tab.

## 25.6 D {#32-glossary--d}

**DBL (Digital Bible Library)** — An online library of Scripture texts. You can download a text bundle from it and install it in PTXprint (see the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab).

**Default configuration** — The configuration called **Default** that every project has. You cannot delete, lock, replace or copy it to other projects, but you can reset it ([**Reset**](#20-import--reset) on the **Basic** tab, with no confirmation).

**Diff PDF** — A PDF that shows in colour what changed between a new PDF and an older one (added text in the [**New Text**](#s-l-ndiffNew) colour, removed text in the [**Old Text**](#s-l-ndiffOld) colour). Make it with [**Compare PDFs**](#s-c-createDiff) on the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab. [**Start Page Offset**](#s-s-diffOffset) lines up PDFs that start on different pages. [**Smart Check**](#s-c-diffSmart) ignores lines that only moved because the margins changed.

[**Digit mapping**](#s-fcb-fontdigits) — An option that prints numbers with the digits of another script (for example Arabic-Indic or Devanagari) when the text uses 0–9. Set it in the **Pick a Font** dialog (see the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab).

[**Diglot**](#s-lb-Diglot) — A publication with two texts side by side on the page, for example two languages. Each text comes from its own Paratext project. See the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab.

**Drop chapter number** — A large chapter number at the start of a chapter, two or more lines high, with the text beside it.

**Dynamic border** — A border that PTXprint draws around text, a heading or a title, and that grows with its contents. Compare **PDF border**. See the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab.

## 25.7 E {#32-glossary--e}

**em** — A unit of width equal to the size of the text. In 10 pt text, 1 em is 10 pt.

[**End of Ayah**](#s-r-decorator-ayah) — A special character (U+06DD) used in Arabic script to decorate verse numbers. See the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab.

**Extended note (study note)** — A longer note, as in a study Bible. In USFM it is marked with `\ef`. PTXprint prints extended notes in their own area at the bottom of the page. See the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab.

**External cross-reference list** — A ready-made list of cross-references that comes with PTXprint (or your own list). PTXprint can add these references to the publication. See the **Notes+Refs** tab.

## 25.8 F {#32-glossary--f}

**Fake (faux) bold and italic** — Bold or italic letters that PTXprint makes from the regular letters (thicker or slanted), when a font has no real bold or italic typeface.

**Fallback font** — A second font that PTXprint uses only for characters that the main font does not have, so they do not print as empty boxes. See the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab.

**Final SFM** — The text of a book after PTXprint has made all its changes, exactly as sent to the typesetter. You can look at it (but not edit it) on the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab.

**Font** — A set of letter shapes, for example *Charis SIL* or *Gentium Plus*. A font family usually has four typefaces: Regular, Bold, Italic and Bold Italic.

**Font feature** — An option built into a font, for example another shape for one letter, or different digits. Choose features with [**Select Features...**](#s-btn-fontFeatures) in the **Pick a Font** dialog.

**Footer** — The line at the bottom of each page, outside the main text. It can hold a page number, a date, a time or a short text. See the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab.

**Footnote** — A note that explains something about the text. In USFM it is marked with `\f`. It is usually printed at the bottom of the page. See the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab.

**Frame size** — The width of the area for a picture or box: one column, the full width (span), a page inside the margins, or the whole sheet. See the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab.

**Front matter** — The pages before the Scripture text, for example the title page, copyright page, table of contents and preface. In Paratext it is the FRT book. Make and edit it on the [**Peripherals**](#s-lb-Peripherals) and [**View+Edit**](#s-lb-Viewer) tabs.

**FRT** — The book code for front matter. PTXprint does not list it with the other books. Set up the front matter on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab instead.

## 25.9 G {#32-glossary--g}

**Glossary** — A list of words with their meanings, usually at the end of the publication. Its book code is GLO.

**Glossary word** — A word in the text that has an entry in the glossary. In USFM it is marked with `\w ...\w*`. Choose how glossary words look (bold, a star before, a star before and after, brackets …) in [**Glossary Word Appearance**](#s-fcb-glossaryMarkupStyle) on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab.

**Glyph** — The shape that a font draws for a character.

**Glyph collision** — Letters or marks that touch or overlap, for example a high mark that hits the line above. [**Layout Analysis**](#s-c-layoutAnalysis) in the PDF Preview window marks these in red.

[**Graph Paper**](#s-c-gridGraph) — A measuring grid that PTXprint can draw over the pages in the PDF Preview window. It is not printed in the PDF.

**Graphite** — A "smart font" technology from SIL. Some fonts for complex scripts need it. Tick [**Graphite Rendering**](#s-c-fontGraphite) in the **Pick a Font** dialog only for fonts made for Graphite.

**Grayscale (B/W)** — Only black ink, in shades of grey. Choose **Print-Gray (B/W)** on the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab for a book printed only in black.

**gsm** — Grams per square metre: the weight of paper. Heavier paper is usually thicker. The [**Cover Wizard**](#s-btn-coverGenerate) can use it to work out the spine width.

**Gutter** — An empty space. The *column gutter* is the space between two columns. The *binding gutter* is extra space at the spine. See the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.

## 25.10 H {#32-glossary--h}

**Hanging indent** — A paragraph whose first line starts further left than the other lines. Poetry and lists often use it. Make it with a negative [**First Line Indent Factor**](#s-s-styFirstLineIndent) on the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab.

**Header (running header)** — The line at the top of each page, outside the main text. It often shows the book name, chapter and verse references, and the page number. See the [**Header+Footer**](#ch-08-headfoot) tab.

**Hyphenation** — Breaking a long word at the end of a line, usually with a hyphen (-), and continuing it on the next line. PTXprint uses the hyphenation list from Paratext. See the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab.

## 25.11 I {#32-glossary--i}

[**Image set**](#s-ecb-artPictureSet) — A downloadable collection of Bible illustrations. You can search it in the picture catalogue ([**Show Catalogue...**](#s-btn-getPictures) on the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab).

**Imposition** — Arranging several book pages on one large sheet, so that after folding and cutting the pages come out in the right order. See **Booklet Pagination** on the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab.

**Interlinear** — Printing a gloss (a short translation) under or above each word of the text, from the Paratext Interlinearizer. See the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab.

**Introduction (book introduction)** — The text before chapter 1 of a book, with markers such as `\is` and `\ip`. Choose whether to print it on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab.

**ISBN** — The international number that identifies a published book. The [**Cover Wizard**](#s-btn-coverGenerate) can print it as a barcode on the back cover, and stores it in the variable **isbn**.

## 25.12 J {#32-glossary--j}

**Justification (justified text)** — Text where both the left and right edges of the lines are straight. PTXprint stretches or shrinks the spaces between words to do this. Compare **ragged**. Set it on the [**Body**](#s-lb-Body) and **Styles** tabs.

## 25.13 K {#32-glossary--k}

**Kashida (tatweel)** — A joining stroke in Arabic script that makes a word longer. It can be used to make lines look better. See the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab.

## 25.14 L {#32-glossary--l}

[**Layout Analysis**](#s-c-layoutAnalysis) — A check in the PDF Preview window that looks for layout problems (wide spaces, rivers, collisions and missing characters) and marks them in colour on the page.

[**Layout Only**](#s-c-noupdate) — A check box in the bottom bar. When ticked, PTXprint does not process the text again if only layout settings changed, so printing is faster. It also unticks the colophon.

**Leading** — Another word for line spacing: the distance from the baseline of one line to the baseline of the next. PTXprint calls it **Line Spacing**.

**Line spacing** — See **leading** and **Base Line Spacing**.

[**Lines Per Page**](#s-l-linesOnPageLabel) — The number of lines of text that fit on a page, shown on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab. Blue when a whole number of lines fits, red when there is wasted space.

[**Lock Ratio**](#s-c-lockFontSize2Baseline) — A check box on the **Layout** tab that keeps the font size and line spacing in the same proportion. When you change one, PTXprint changes the other.

**Locked configuration** — A configuration protected with a password, so that nobody changes or deletes it by mistake. See the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.

## 25.15 M {#32-glossary--m}

**Margin** — The empty space between the text and the edge of the page. Set the margins on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.

[**Margin notes**](#04-layout--margin-notes) — Footnotes, cross-references or headings printed in an extra column at the side of the text, beside their verse. See the **Layout** and [**Notes+Refs**](#s-lb-NotesRefs) tabs.

[**Marginal verses**](#s-c-marginalverses) — Verse numbers printed in a narrow column beside the text instead of inside it. Set them on the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab.

**Marker (USFM marker)** — A short code that starts with a backslash and says what a piece of text is. For example, `\p` starts a paragraph, `\s1` is a section heading, `\v` is a verse number and `\f` is a footnote. Each marker has a style on the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab.

[**Merging mode**](#s-fcb-diglotMerge) — How PTXprint lines up the texts of a diglot or polyglot: by chapters and verses, or by a scoring method. See the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab.

**Mirror (picture)** — To flip a picture from left to right, as in a mirror. See the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab.

[**Mirror Pages**](#s-c-mirrorpages) — A setting that makes left-hand and right-hand pages mirror each other, so items stay on the outer (or inner) edge. See the **Layout** and [**Header+Footer**](#s-lb-HeadFoot) tabs.

**Monoglot** — A publication with only one text (not a diglot or polyglot).

## 25.16 N {#32-glossary--n}

**Non-breaking space** — A space where PTXprint never breaks the line. The words on each side always stay on the same line.

[**Notelines**](#s-c-noteLines) — Ruled lines printed in a wide margin, so readers can write their own notes. Used for journaling Bibles. See the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.

## 25.17 O {#32-glossary--o}

**Odd and even pages** — Right-hand pages have odd numbers (1, 3, 5…). Left-hand pages have even numbers (2, 4, 6…).

**OpenType** — The usual font technology. Most fonts are OpenType fonts. Compare **Graphite**.

**Ornament** — A small decorative pattern or graphic. PTXprint can use ornaments in borders and to decorate pages. See the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab.

**Orphan** — In typesetting, the first line of a paragraph left alone at the bottom of a column or page. On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, [**Prevent Orphan Words**](#s-c-preventorphans) is a different idea: it stops one short word being left alone on the last line of a paragraph. Compare **widow**.

## 25.18 P {#32-glossary--p}

**Padding** — Empty space inside a box or border, between the edge and the text. Set it in the **Border Settings** dialog (see the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab).

**Page filling** — Making the text reach the bottom margin on every page. You do it by adjusting paragraphs in the PDF Preview window, by hand or with **Auto Page Fill**.

[**Page size**](#s-ecb-pagesize) — See [**trim size**](#18-printers--trim-size). A size you type yourself is saved and offered in the **Page Size** list for all your projects.

**Paragraph style (paragraph marker)** — A style for a whole paragraph, for example `\p` (normal paragraph), `\q1` (poetry) or `\s1` (section heading). Compare **character style**.

**Parallel passage reference** — A reference under a section heading that shows where the same event is told in another book, for example "(Mark 1:1-8)". In USFM it is marked with `\r`.

**Paratext** — The program that translation teams use to write and check Scripture. PTXprint prints the text of a Paratext project.

**PDF border (Legacy)** — A ready-made PDF graphic that PTXprint places behind headings or on every page as a frame. Compare **dynamic border**.

**PDF Preview** — The PTXprint window that shows the PDF after you print. You can also use it to fix the layout. See the [**PDF Preview**](#ch-19-preview) chapter.

**PDF/A** — A type of PDF made for keeping documents for a very long time (archiving).

**PDF/X** — A type of PDF made for printing. **PDF/X-1a** is the older, strict type (CMYK, no transparency). **PDF/X-4** is newer and allows RGB colours and transparency. See the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab.

**Penalty** — A number that tells the typesetter how much to avoid something, for example breaking a word. Higher means "avoid this more". 10000 means "never". Penalties are TeXpert settings on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab.

**Periph (peripheral section)** — A section of the front or back matter, for example the title page or the preface. In the front matter each one starts with a `\periph` line.

**Peripheral book** — A book that is not Scripture text, for example front matter (FRT), back matter (BAK), the glossary (GLO) or extra material (XXA, XXB…).

**PicList (picture list)** — The list of all pictures in a configuration. Each line gives the picture file, its anchor, caption, size and position. PTXprint makes it from the `\fig` entries in the text, and then uses only the list. See the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab.

**Placeholder** — An empty box printed where a picture would go. It keeps the layout but makes the PDF very small.

**Polyglot** — A publication with three or more texts side by side. See the [**Diglot**](#ch-10-diglot) tab.

**Primary text** — In a diglot or polyglot, the text of the configuration you started from (code [**L**](#32-glossary--l)). It controls the page size, margins, headers and footers. Compare **secondary text**.

**Project** — A Paratext project: the Scripture text that you want to print, with its settings. Choose it on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab.

**pt (point)** — A small unit used for type. 1 pt is about 0.35 mm. 72 pt is about one inch (25.4 mm). Font sizes and line spacing are given in points.

**Publication** — The book or booklet that you are making. On the [**Publications**](#ch-16-publications) tab (Full view only), a publication is a named set of books that you can print together with others.

## 25.19 Q {#32-glossary--q}

[**Quick Run**](#s-c-quickRun) — A check box in the bottom bar. PTXprint then runs the typesetting only once, which is faster. Untick it for the final PDF, so page references and the table of contents are correct.

## 25.20 R {#32-glossary--r}

**Ragged** — Text where one edge of the lines is not straight (for example ragged right). Compare **justification**.

**Regular expression** — A way to describe patterns of text, used in changes files. An advanced feature.

**Resolution (picture)** — How detailed a picture file is. Low-resolution files are small and good for drafts. High-resolution files are large and needed for printing. Choose on the [**Pictures**](#ch-09-pictures) tab.

**RGB** — The colours used by screens: Red, Green and Blue. Compare **CMYK**.

**River** — A line of white space running down through several lines of text, made by wide word spaces that happen to be one above the other. [**Layout Analysis**](#s-c-layoutAnalysis) marks rivers in yellow.

**Right-to-left (RTL)** — Scripts written from right to left, for example Arabic and Hebrew. Set the direction on the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab.

**Rule** — A thin straight line, for example under the header, between columns, or above the notes.

## 25.21 S {#32-glossary--s}

**Script** — A writing system, for example Latin, Arabic, Devanagari, Myanmar or Han (Chinese). Set the [**Text Script**](#s-fcb-script) on the [**Fonts+Script**](#ch-05-fonts) tab.

**Secondary text** — In a diglot or polyglot, each text other than the primary text (codes [**R**](#32-glossary--r), [**A**](#32-glossary--a), [**B**](#32-glossary--b)…). Each has its own configuration for its fonts and other text settings.

**Section heading** — A heading inside a book that names the next part of the text. In USFM it is marked with `\s1`, `\s2` and so on.

**Send/Receive** — The Paratext command that shares changes with the rest of the team. PTXprint configurations are shared this way. The PDFs are not.

**Sidebar** — A box of extra text, for example a study note about a place or a person, separate from the Scripture text. In USFM it starts with `\esb` and ends with `\esbe`. See the [**Styles**](#ch-12-styles) tab.

**Signature** — A group of sheets that are folded together and sewn or glued into the book as one unit. See the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab.

**Span (Span Width)** — The full width of the text area, across both columns. Used for pictures and boxes.

**SpeedSlice** — A tool in the PDF Preview window that typesets only a few chapters of a long book, so each print is fast while you fix pages. Always turn it off before the final PDF. Not available for diglots. See the [**PDF Preview**](#ch-19-preview) chapter.

[**Spine**](#s-lb-style-cat-coverspine-esb) — The narrow back edge of a bound book, between the front and back covers. Its width depends on the number of pages and the paper. Books with fewer than about 80 pages usually have no spine text. Set it up in the [**Cover Wizard**](#s-btn-coverGenerate).

**Spot colour** — One extra, ready-mixed ink used with black, for example red for headings. See the **Finishing** tab.

[**Spread**](#s-c-mapSpread) — Two facing pages of an open book: a left-hand page and the right-hand page beside it.

**Strong's numbers** — Numbers that identify each Hebrew and Greek word of the Bible. PTXprint can use them in cross-references and to make an index. See the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab.

**Style** — The formatting rules for one marker: its font, size, colour, indents, alignment and spacing. Change styles on the **Styles** tab.

**Stylesheet** — A list of styles for all the markers. PTXprint combines the Paratext stylesheet with its own additions and your changes. See the **Styles** tab.

## 25.22 T {#32-glossary--t}

**Table of contents** — A list of the books with their page numbers, usually in the front matter. Turn it on with **Table of Contents** on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab.

**TeXpert settings** — About 125 fine settings for the typesetting engine, on the [**Advanced**](#ch-13-advanced) tab, **Other** sub-tab. For experienced users. Labels turn bold when a value is changed.

**Text area** — The part of the page where the main text goes. The margins are outside it.

**Thumb tab** — A coloured block at the outer edge of the page, with a short book name in it. When the book is closed, the reader can see the tabs and open the book at the right Bible book. See the [**Tabs+Borders**](#ch-11-tabsborders) tab.

**Tofu** — The empty box (☐) printed when the font has no shape for a character. Use a fallback font or another font to fix it.

**Transcelerator** — A Paratext plugin for making comprehension-checking questions. PTXprint can print the questions. See the [**Notes+Refs**](#ch-07-notes) tab.

[**Trim size**](#18-printers--trim-size) — The size of the finished book page after the printer cuts it. In PTXprint this is the [**Page Size**](#s-ecb-pagesize) on the [**Layout**](#ch-04-layout) tab.

**Tutorial** — A file with a list of steps that PTXprint carries out one at a time on the current configuration, highlighting each control. Start it with [**Run Tutorial...**](#s-btn-runTutorial) on the [**Basic**](#ch-03-basic) tab. Use a practice configuration.

**Typeface (face)** — One style of a font: Regular, Bold, Italic or Bold Italic.

## 25.23 U {#32-glossary--u}

**Underfilled page** — A page or column where the text stops before the bottom margin. PTXprint lists these in the PDF Preview window, so you can fix them.

**Unicode** — The international standard that gives a number to every character in every script. A character can be written as `U+` and a hexadecimal number, for example U+06DD.

**USFM** — Unified Standard Format Markers. The way Paratext stores Scripture text, with markers such as `\p`, `\v` and `\f` that say what each piece of text is.

**USX** — An XML format for Scripture text, used for example in DBL text bundles.

## 25.24 V {#32-glossary--v}

**Variable** — A place-holder in the front matter, written as `\zvar|name\*`. When you print, PTXprint replaces it with a value from the variables table on the [**Peripherals**](#ch-15-peripherals) tab, for example the title of the book. When you copy a configuration to other projects, each project normally keeps its own language-specific variables (titles, language name).

**Variable Line Spacing** — A layout choice where PTXprint may stretch the space between lines a little so that every column is filled to the bottom. Compare [**Align Text to Baseline**](#s-c-noGrid).

[**View level**](#s-btn-menu-level) — How many settings PTXprint shows: **Mini**, **Basic**, **Regular** or **Full**. Hidden settings still work. Change it with **≡** › **View Level** (see the chapter [**The main window, menu and view levels**](#ch-02-main-window)).

## 25.25 W {#32-glossary--w}

**Watermark** — A light text or picture printed on every page, for example the word "DRAFT". Add it on the [**Finishing**](#ch-17-finishing) tab.

**Widow** — In typesetting, the last line of a paragraph left alone at the top of a column or page. On the [**Body**](#ch-06-body) tab, [**Prevent Verse Widow Words**](#s-c-preventwidows) is a different idea: it stops a verse number and a short word being left alone at the end of a line. Compare **orphan**.

## 25.26 X {#32-glossary--x}

**XeTeX** — The typesetting program that PTXprint uses behind the scenes to place the text on the pages. You never need to use it yourself. Its report of the last print run is on the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab (**XeTeX Log**).

## 25.27 Z {#32-glossary--z}

**z-codes** — Extra codes that start with `\z` and that PTXprint understands in addition to normal USFM markers, for example `\zcopyright`, `\zvar|...\*` or `\ztoc|main\*`. Used mostly in the front matter. See the [**View+Edit**](#ch-14-viewedit) tab.

**ZIP file** — A file that holds other files packed together. PTXprint uses ZIP files for archives, image sets and printer orders.
